paragraphs.text: It is evident from the words of St. Luke that many in his time had written about the life of Christ in addition to the Evangelists. Since Luke believed in Christ after having been a Gentile, and attached himself to the Apostles who had witnessed the life of the Lord Jesus and had become ministers of the Word, he felt a responsibility to write about His life as well, because he had followed it with precision. His work as a physician, accustomed to examination and exactness, helped him in this.
This means that Luke gathered his information from two sources:
(1) The Virgin and the disciples who witnessed Christ.
(2) The writings of the many who preceded him, though their writings may have been incomplete.

Here the importance of Church Tradition becomes clear, that is, the oral Apostolic handing down of the faith from the Fathers the Apostles to their disciples until it reached us today. This includes the text of the Holy Bible and all the faith and rites of the Church. It is Tradition that has preserved the Church from the days of the Apostles until now.

May you become accustomed to exactness in understanding the Holy Bible and all the faith and rites of the Church, and may you also examine your own life with exactness in repentance, so that you may grow strongly in the spiritual life.

Since Luke took care to know the details of the life of Christ, he wrote the life of Christ in order to Theophilus, who had believed and been taught much, so as to confirm his faith in Christ. He was a Greek who had become a Christian and was living in Alexandria, and he held a great political position, for Luke calls him "most excellent," that is, His Excellency; and the meaning of his name is "lover of God." So if you, my brother, are a lover of God, this Gospel is addressed to you, as St. Ambrose says.

This chapter has a special importance, because it is the preparation for the birth of Christ; therefore the Church reads it on the four Sundays of the month of Koiak before the Feast of the Nativity. It tells us:
The first Sunday: the annunciation of the birth of John.
The second Sunday: the annunciation of the birth of Christ.
The third Sunday: the Virgin's visit to Elisabeth.
The fourth Sunday: the birth of John the Baptist.

Herod: the king mentioned is Herod the Great, who was a descendant of Esau and hated the Jews. He ruled from 37 BC until about 4 BC. His reign was marked by cruelty, and before the end of his life he killed the children of Bethlehem (the birth of Christ was in 4 BC, and the children were killed when He was a few months old). He ruled all the land of the Jews.
Zacharias: it means "God remembers," and he was a priest.
Elisabeth: that is, "the oath of God," and she was also of the descendants of Aaron the high priest.

They were distinguished by righteousness in fulfilling God's commandments and likewise His ordinances, which are the requirements of the Law. All this is sound spiritual conduct, visible before men. In addition to that, their hearts were pure before God. Because of their righteousness, God chose to speak to them after His speech with His people had ceased for more than three centuries, so that they might bear John, whose name means "God is gracious."
"Thus the love of God appears toward everyone who fears Him. If you hold fast to God's commandments and to your spiritual striving, you will see His tenderness and His many graces.
The course of Abia: in the time of Zacharias there were about 20,000 priests in Judea, divided into 24 courses, each of about a thousand, and each course served in the Temple for a week twice a year.

Despite the righteousness of Zacharias and Elisabeth, they faced a difficult problem, namely childlessness, because barrenness was considered a disgrace in the Old Testament, as a sign of unworthiness to bear the awaited Messiah. They had grown old, and there was no longer any hope of having children. But God's wisdom in the affliction appeared afterward, for the delay in childbearing was so that God might give them John the Baptist ... the greatest of those born of women, who prepares the way of Christ, and who had to be born six months before Christ.

entries.section: (3) The annunciation of the birth of John

paragraphs.text: The week of service of the course of Abia came, and the priests attended, among them the aged Zacharias, and the lot was cast as usual to determine who would enter to offer incense on the golden altar inside the sanctuary, which no one but the priests were permitted to enter.
The lot usually came to a priest no more than once in a lifetime, to enter this great place and offer incense to God, because the number of the course, as we mentioned, was a thousand.
The multitude of the people stood outside the sanctuary, waiting for the blessing of Zacharias the priest after he had burned incense inside the sanctuary.

How great is God's grace in the New Testament, which allows all the priests to enter the sanctuary every day and offer incense in the sight of all the people, and even to come out with the incense to bless all who are present in the Church, because the burning of the incense and its sweet fragrance are a type of the death of Christ on the Cross to take away our sins. For this reason our prayers rise in thanksgiving and praise with this incense ascending to heaven.

entries.section: (3) The annunciation of the birth of John

paragraphs.text: The lot fell on Zacharias, and this was by divine providence ... for when he entered the sanctuary and offered incense on the golden altar in the middle of the sanctuary, before the veil of the Holy of Holies, in which was the ark of the covenant, and then bowed down as the priests were accustomed to do, and rose, a luminous angel of majestic form appeared to him on the right side of the altar of incense. The altar of incense: there were two main altars in Solomon's temple. The first was outside, and sacrifices and offerings were presented on it; the second was inside, and nothing was offered on it but incense, which was also considered an offering and was called "a sweet savour unto the Lord."

From the altar and the Temple divine graces and heavenly blessings are poured out upon us, so that we receive the greatest thing, the Body and Blood of the Lord, and acquire peace and joy ... and our inward eyes are opened to see God and to enjoy fellowship with Him together with all the heavenly ones.

entries.section: (3) The annunciation of the birth of John

paragraphs.text: Before the grandeur of this heavenly appearance, Zacharias was afraid, so the angel reassured him and declared to him that God had cared for his prayers for tens of years until now, not only for the begetting of offspring but also for his longing for the coming of Christ. For as a priest he prayed thus in his liturgical prayers, awaiting the divine Incarnation. The angel promised him that his aged wife would conceive, and even announced the name of the child, "John," that is, God's grace.

How reassuring to the soul is God's care for every prayer and petition we raise to Him, yet He answers at the proper time. So continue, my brother, in your prayers however much the answer is delayed, confident that it will be answered in the fitting way, at the best time that God sees for you.

entries.section: (3) The annunciation of the birth of John

paragraphs.text: The angel declared that John was not an ordinary child who would gladden only the hearts of his aged parents, relatives and neighbors, but that his ministry would extend to become joy for everyone who believes and responds to his call.

entries.section: (3) The annunciation of the birth of John

paragraphs.text: For he shall be great: John will become great in the sight of the Lord, and will be appointed a Nazarite to God.
And shall drink neither wine nor strong drink: he will not drink fermented grape juice nor intoxicating wine.

He shall be filled with the Holy Ghost: he is distinguished from the rest of mankind by being filled with the Holy Spirit while still an unborn child; therefore he is the greatest of those born of women, as Christ Himself declared (Mt 11:11).

entries.section: (3) The annunciation of the birth of John

paragraphs.text: The angel speaks about the nature of John's ministry, which is calling the Jews to repentance and return to God, and the return of love and unity within the family between fathers and children, and calling sinners and the disobedient to God's commandments so that they may repent and think of righteousness.

And this is the preparation for the divine Incarnation. For when the angel declares that John goes before his God, this is a proof of the divinity of Christ, whose ministry begins six months after him; and he also declares that John will be strong in the manner of his ministry like Elijah the prophet.

Zacharias' mind could not believe the divine good news, and he presented his reasons, namely that he and his wife were aged and it was impossible for them to bear a child. Yet history had repeatedly shown the ability of the aged to bear children by God's miraculous work, such as Abraham and Sarah, and barrenness had not stood in the way, as with Isaac and Rebekah, Jacob and Rachel, and Manoah and his wife, the parents of Samson. But the gentleness of Zacharias is to be noted: he did not complain about his wife's barrenness, but said courteously that she was well stricken in years.

The day that these things shall be performed: that is, the birth of John the Baptist, for eight days after it Zacharias spoke. So "the day" means the time or period of his birth, and not specifically the day of birth.

Because of Zacharias' doubt he lost his ability to speak, as the archangel Gabriel, meaning "the might of God," declared to him; he is one of the seven archangels who stand before God. His silence was the natural result of not believing the voice of God. The silence of Zacharias declares the silence of the Old Testament, so that the New Testament might begin with Jesus Christ; Jewish worship fell silent and became meaningless after the coming of Christ and the cessation of the prophets among them.
The people were waiting for Zacharias to bless them according to the custom of Jewish worship, but the vision took a long time, so the multitude marveled, asking the reason for his delay.

When Zacharias came out unable to speak, content only with signs of his hands, they understood that he had seen a vision inside the sanctuary as used to happen with the prophets of old. So they rejoiced at the divine revelation, although they longed to know this revelation, which remained obscure because of Zacharias' silence.
Zacharias remained in the Temple until the week of his service ended, then returned to his house, which was outside Jerusalem in the hills surrounding the city.

When Elisabeth felt that she had conceived, she and her husband Zacharias rejoiced greatly and thanked God who had blessed them, and Elisabeth was finally relieved of the women's reproaches against her for barrenness and unworthiness of blessing. But she hid herself for five months from appearing before people so as to be certain of the miraculous conception, for she had shared her husband in the sin of doubt.

But this period in which Zacharias was silent was an opportunity for a deeper conversation with God, in which repentance was mingled with thanksgiving, and also meditation on God's earlier works with His people and with them.

Take advantage of the opportunity of illness and of your being sometimes apart from people to review yourself and offer repentance, thanksgiving and meditation on God's works with you. You can feel this if you take a weekly retreat.

entries.section: (6) The annunciation of the birth of Christ

paragraphs.text: Six months after the archangel Gabriel's announcement to Zacharias, at the beginning of the sixth month, he appeared in a small town called Nazareth, which is in Galilee, that is, the northern part of the land of the Jews, and is more than 80 miles from Jerusalem. It lay on a trade route and was visited by Gentile merchants and Roman soldiers, so it was known for its distance from Jewish worship because of the many Gentiles in it. There, in a small house, was a virgin about fifteen years of age named Mary, living in the care of an old man named Joseph of the tribe of David [so that the prophecies would be fulfilled that Christ would be the son of David (Ps 132:11)], and he worked as a carpenter, but his livelihood was poor because of his old age and weakness for work. Betrothal in Jewish society was considered a formal marriage bond, but without the beginning of the physical relationship, as is the case now among our Muslim brethren in what is called "writing the contract," which is a formal marriage without the physical relationship.

entries.section: (6) The annunciation of the birth of Christ

paragraphs.text: The angel gave peace to the Virgin, and it is God's gift in which His children alone are distinguished from the rest of the world: "There is no peace, saith my God, to the wicked" (Isa 57:21). He described her as full of grace (as in the Coptic and Greek text, which was mistranslated in the Beirut edition as "highly favored"), unlike the rest of mankind, who are favored with His blessings, whereas the Holy Spirit came upon her and filled her with grace so that the Holy God might be born of her, and He made her blessed and blessed her among all women. And as sin entered the world through Eve, so the good news of salvation came through a woman, the Virgin Mary.

entries.section: (6) The annunciation of the birth of Christ

paragraphs.text: The sight of the angel was majestic, so the young Virgin was afraid of his splendor and light, and thought in herself about the reason for his appearing, his greeting and his blessing her.

entries.section: (6) The annunciation of the birth of Christ

paragraphs.text: The angel reassured her of God's love for her and His intention to bestow on her the greatest blessings because of her holiness and her attachment to God. The angel also announced to her the good news of the divine conception, and the name of the God who became man, which is Jesus, and the meaning of His name is Savior.

entries.section: (6) The annunciation of the birth of Christ

paragraphs.text: He described Him with an attribute of God, which is "greatness," and even named Him "the Son of the Highest," that is, the Son of God, of His essence and nature, and in Him all the prophecies are fulfilled, for He is the awaited Messiah of the seed of David.

entries.section: (6) The annunciation of the birth of Christ

paragraphs.text: So that Christ may be King forever over Jacob, that is, God's people who believe in Him.
Christ wants to reign over your heart and let you enjoy His love forever, if you believe in Him, submit to Him and obey His commandments.

entries.section: (7) The Virgin's dialogue with the angel

paragraphs.text: The Virgin Mary accepted the divine good news and believed, as Elisabeth later testified (Lk 1:
45), but she had vowed virginity, so her question was whether God wanted her to give up her virginity, for she said to the angel, "I know not a man."

entries.section: (7) The Virgin's dialogue with the angel

paragraphs.text: The angel's answer confirmed that she would keep her virginity, so that she would be ever-virgin, because God had prepared a miraculous way to accomplish this divine conception, which is the coming of the Holy Spirit upon her to form the first complete cell of the embryo within the womb, and the power of the Highest overshadowing is the embrace of the Father for accomplishing the divine begetting. Then he clearly declares the eternal attribute of the One to be born, for He is the Holy One, that is, God and the Son of God, being of His nature and essence.

entries.section: (7) The Virgin's dialogue with the angel

paragraphs.text: When God saw her wonderful faith and her submission to the good news, despite the many sufferings she would endure, because she would be accused of fornication by all those around her, He supported her with the good news of the conception of Elisabeth her aged kinswoman, to confirm her faith in God's miraculous power; for He is able to make the aged barren woman pregnant, and He is also able to do all things, so that He makes the virgin conceive.

entries.section: (7) The Virgin's dialogue with the angel

paragraphs.text: The Virgin's answer at the close of this dialogue was submission to the good news in complete surrender and wonderful humility. She did not boast that she was the Mother of God, but declared that she was His handmaid.

To the extent that you obey God's commandments and rely on Him in surrendering your life to Him, the blessings of heaven overflow upon you, and God supports you and confirms your faith, and you behold God in your life, so that you are reassured and rejoice and become worthy to behold the heavenly things while you are on earth.
In those days, that is, a little after the angel's announcement to her; that is, she prepared herself for the journey immediately after the annunciation.

Into the hill country: the Virgin traveled a long distance from Nazareth in Galilee, north of Judea, to the region of Jerusalem, to a city near it belonging to the tribe of Judah, and bore the hardships of the journey, crossing the mountains to reach Elisabeth.

Since the Virgin Mary was filled with the divine good news, and the divine Child had come to dwell in her womb, she who was full of grace hastened with spiritual zeal, climbing the mountains, in search of someone to whom she might give her love, which she would offer to all humanity through her only-begotten Son. She went to Elisabeth not only to congratulate her but to serve her, because she was pregnant and aged and needed someone to help her. She is the Church that preaches Christ the Savior of the world.
When the Virgin entered the house of her kinswoman Elisabeth, the wife of Zacharias the priest, she gave her the peace which is God's gift to His children.

When Elisabeth heard the greeting, the child in her womb bowed down before Jesus who was in the womb of the Virgin, and leaped with joy at this meeting, and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit, who revealed to her many things: (1) That the Virgin was pregnant with the awaited Messiah, that is, Jesus Christ.
(2) That the movement of the child in her womb was worship and joy at the meeting of Christ and the Virgin His mother.

Elisabeth said to the Virgin that she was worthy of blessing more than all the women of the world, and that the child in her womb was also blessed. With evident humility Elisabeth declared her unworthiness that the Mother of God should visit her. This was a support and confirmation of the Virgin's faith in the divine good news, which she had told to no one, and it was also a declaration by the Church, represented in Elisabeth, of the Virgin's position as the Mother of God.
Elisabeth offered the proof of the Virgin's greatness, which was the movement and worship of the child John in her womb when the Virgin greeted her.

In humility also, Elisabeth confessed her sin and her husband's in not believing the angel's good news, whereas the Virgin was distinguished from them by her wonderful faith in a good news the like of which had never been heard before, a virgin conceiving. Elisabeth knew of the angel's announcement to the Virgin through the Holy Spirit who came upon her. May you be humble, confessing your sins before others and esteeming them above yourself in honor, so that you may deserve God's blessings and blessed fruits may come forth from you like John, that is, holy virtues.
If sin entered the world through Eve, now women, Elisabeth and the Virgin, come forward with joyful prophecies about the blessed Christ, the Savior of the world.

As the Virgin meditates on God, His image grows great and magnified within her, and she rejoices in Him as her personal Savior from her sins; for she needed salvation like the rest of mankind, even though she is the greatest of the saints and even above the angels because of her holiness and virtues.
The Virgin showed God's wonderful grace which He gave her, declaring her humility as God's handmaid, whom He condescended to regard and granted to be His mother; therefore all mankind praises her.

God who is almighty gave me, while I was a virgin, to conceive; and it is likewise among the greatness of His works that He united with humanity in the mystery of the Incarnation when He is as a child in my womb, and He is also able to bind Satan on the Cross for the redemption of mankind; and despite His humbling Himself by His Incarnation, He is the Holy God.

In the preceding verse the Virgin described God as mighty and holy, and here she speaks of His mercy which He grants to everyone who believes in Him and fears Him, not only in this generation but to the end of days, for His salvation He offers to all mankind.

God's power appears in making the humble Virgin conceive, and likewise the aged Elisabeth, whereas the proud, such as Herod, He scatters all their power and evil, and they cannot harm the Christ who is born, just as He scatters the demons and binds them with His Cross.

Everyone who is proud and esteems himself, He brings down from the material position in which he has placed himself, like Herod who was eaten by worms (the son of Herod the Great); and at the same time He glorifies the humble, like the Virgin and Elisabeth.

Everyone who hungers for righteousness, He satisfies with His most holy Body and Blood and every spiritual gift, but those who rely on their riches and the money of the world receive no blessing from Him and have no share in the Kingdom of Heaven.

The Virgin adds to her glorification of God a fourth attribute in Him, which is His faithfulness to His promises to His people Israel, whom she calls "servant," that is, a son whom God his Father cares for and supports, so He offers him salvation through His Incarnation and redemption, and then the children of God remember His mercy and thank Him at all times.

And the people of God are not only the old Israel but the new Israel, that is, the Christians who believe in Him, whether Jews or Gentiles. The fulfillment of the promises He gave to Abraham and the fathers, that is, salvation, lasts forever with His children who believe in Him, so that they rejoice with Him in His heavenly Kingdom.

The shortest road to God's heart is humility, by knowing your sins and your need of Him; then all the heavenly blessings pour down upon you. So hold yourself to account, offer repentance before Him every day, and humble yourself also before everyone, and He will raise you above all with inner peace and happiness on earth, and then with heavenly glories in the age to come.

The Virgin Mary remained for three months humbly serving the aged Elisabeth, who was in the last months of her pregnancy, forgetting her great position. And since the child John had leaped for joy in Elisabeth's womb merely at meeting the Christ-child in the Virgin's womb, how great was the joy and fulfillment of Elisabeth and John when they enjoyed the company of the Virgin and her Son for three whole months!
After that the Virgin returned to her home in the town of Nazareth in Galilee, where her pregnancy became evident and Joseph discovered it, as Matthew the Evangelist mentions (Mt 1).

entries.section: (10) The birth and ministry of John

paragraphs.text: At last Elisabeth's nine months were completed and she bore her son, and when her loved ones heard of it they rejoiced greatly, because the Lord's miracle had been accomplished in the conception of the aged barren woman.

entries.section: (10) The birth and ministry of John

paragraphs.text: On the eighth day, when a male child of the people of Israel is circumcised, which is a proof of sonship to God and was a type of Baptism. It was the custom to name the child on the day of his circumcision, so the relatives who had gathered called him Zacharias after the name of his father.

entries.section: (10) The birth and ministry of John

paragraphs.text: But his mother, who was filled with the Holy Spirit, said that he should be called John. She had learned that name from his father Zacharias, according to what the angel had declared to him; so he must have written this name for her, and even the details of the vision, so that she might rejoice with him in it.

entries.section: (10) The birth and ministry of John

paragraphs.text: The relatives who had gathered objected, since this name was foreign to the names of the family; for it was customary to use certain names in each family so that they might be blessed and imitate their forefathers, and so that no one afterward would doubt the new son's belonging to his family.

entries.section: (10) The birth and ministry of John

paragraphs.text: Those present made signs to his father, who was mute and had probably also lost his hearing; therefore they did not speak to him but made signs to him, asking him what he wanted his son to be called.

entries.section: (10) The birth and ministry of John

paragraphs.text: Zacharias asked for a writing tablet and wrote on it John, and those present were greatly astonished at the agreement of the parents on one name. Perhaps it was also a revelation from the angel to Zacharias of the child's name. They usually used tablets of wood covered with wax on which they wrote with a stylus pointed at one end to engrave in the wax and flat at its other end to erase what they wished to erase.

entries.section: (10) The birth and ministry of John

paragraphs.text: Immediately after he wrote the name John, God healed him and his tongue was loosed, praising God, and the fear of God fell on the hearts of those present when Zacharias spoke. His opinion agreed with his wife Elisabeth about this strange name, John, and the news of this miracle spread throughout Jerusalem and the hill country of Judea surrounding it.

entries.section: (10) The birth and ministry of John

paragraphs.text: Everyone felt that this child was no ordinary one and would be great; and as they recalled the events of his wonderful birth, they began to think about the manifestations of spiritual greatness that would appear in him when he grew up. Observe God's works with those around you, and try to learn something from them for yourself that will bring you closer to God, for they are messages from Him to you every day.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: During the nine months of silence, Zacharias enjoyed many prayers and meditations with God, so he became worthy to be filled with the Holy Spirit, and speaks to us about Christ and the salvation that He would accomplish on the Cross and declare by the power of His Resurrection.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: Zacharias blessed God and called Him the God of Israel to declare His fatherhood and care for His people, for He had finally fulfilled His promises to Abraham and the fathers by the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption on the Cross.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: Christ the Savior is the Son of David, who established a strong spiritual kingdom symbolized by the horn (which is the strongest thing in an animal), which defeats our enemies, that is, the demons who hate us.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: By the mouth of his holy prophets: God is the One who speaks through the mouth of the prophets, so submission to the word of God is necessary. Since the world began: from the beginning of creation, that is, from Adam until this time.
By this the prophecies of all the prophets about Christ, and all of God's oaths and promises, were fulfilled.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: From this verse to v. 75 he begins to describe the effectiveness of Christ's salvation and its effect on those who believe in Him. He declares that He frees us from the dominion of sin, to which the demons draw us, for it hates us and tries to ensnare us, but by His power we repel its attacks.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: The salvation of Christ is not only for the living who believe in Him, but also mercy and redemption for all the fathers who died in hope, believing in the awaited Messiah.
For God remembers His promises to the fathers, that is, He carries them out and transfers them from Hades to Paradise, by His salvation which He accomplishes on the Cross.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: The covenant or divine oath which He promised to Abraham the father of the fathers (Gen 22:16, 17), He now fulfills in Christ our Savior.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: Christ gives those who believe in Him peace and assurance, so that they are not troubled by the wars of the demons, nor do they fear them, because He rescues them from them; and as they enjoy this peace, they go forth in spiritual worship of God.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: The worship we offer to God is to be in holiness, that is, inward purity and righteousness that appears in the purity of our conduct, because we offer it to God who searches the hearts and reins and who sees all our works throughout our lives. Remember, my brother, that if you have received freedom and the new nature in Baptism, your only goal in your life is to worship God and walk in righteousness, and any evil you do is a departure from your life, which is devoted and consecrated to the love of God and doing good.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: Zacharias continues his prophecy and addresses the child John, calling him the prophet of God, whereas Christ called John more than a prophet (ch. 7:26); and the function of John the Baptist is to prepare the way of Christ in the hearts of his people.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: The Jews thought that Christ would save them from the slavery of the Romans, so John came to make known to them the true salvation, which is salvation from sin by repentance so that they might receive the forgiveness of their sins. So John makes known to them salvation and calls them to repentance, while Christ is the One who accomplishes this salvation on the Cross.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: Zacharias returns to speak about Christ the Savior, and declares God's deep love, which is expressed by the mercy springing from His bowels. This mercy visited mankind in the fullness of time to rescue it from the darkness of sin, by the Incarnation of Christ, who is the Sun of Righteousness coming from heaven.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: Christ is the light of the world; He shines on sinners who are preoccupied with the lusts of the world, expressed by darkness, and as He lights for them the way of life with Him, He guides them to the way of the Kingdom, so that they enjoy inner peace when He frees them from sin, and they even remain in this peace forever.

God visits you today with His tender love, you who sit in the darkness of sin. May you repent of your beloved sin, and may your heart be lifted up with feelings of love in repentance and thanksgiving, prepared to receive His love poured out on the altar in His most holy Body and Blood.

entries.section: (11) The prophecy of Zacharias about John

paragraphs.text: After the prophecy of Zacharias, St. Luke concludes his account with the growth of John, bodily and spiritually, with God's help in the wilderness. Tradition tells us how, at the killing of the firstborn of Bethlehem, Zacharias carried him to the altar in the Temple of God, and an angel came and snatched him away to live in the wilderness in the care of the angels.

As for Zacharias, whom the Roman soldiers were pursuing, they seized him and killed him between the Temple and the altar (Mt 23:35). In the stillness of the wilderness, John's love, prayers and meditations grew, and God prepared him to be His forerunner. He remained there until the age of thirty, which is the legal age for beginning ministry among the Jews, when he began his preaching. The birth of Jesus, His circumcision and His entry into the Temple
In those days: that is, the birth of John the Baptist.
Caesar Augustus: this is a title of the Roman emperor, whose name was Octavius.
All the world: the whole Roman kingdom, which included most of the world.
Syria: it includes the whole region of the Levant and Iraq, including Judea.

St. Luke takes care to determine the time of the birth of Christ. It was in the days of Caesar Augustus, emperor of the Roman state, when he issued a general census for his whole kingdom. This was the first census of his era, because he did this every ten years, and as a courtesy to the Jews he ordered that the census be taken by each one returning to his own homeland, because the Jews care about their lineage. This was by divine providence, to show that Jesus Christ is the son of David as the prophets foretold.

St. Luke also specifies the time of the general census, which was when Cyrenius was governor of Syria. The purpose of the census for the state was to collect tribute, but God's providence was to record the name of Jesus in history as a man and of the seed of David.
Went up: because Jerusalem and Bethlehem are higher in elevation than Galilee, in addition to the fact that one who goes to the capital is said to have gone up.

The Virgin Mary was living with her betrothed Joseph the carpenter in the city of Nazareth in Galilee, in the north of Judea near the Sea of Galilee. They had to register in Bethlehem, which is in the south of Judea near the Dead Sea and next to Jerusalem, a long distance of about 130 kilometers. How hard it was for the Virgin, pregnant in her ninth month and a girl of sixteen, and for the aged Joseph the carpenter, to make such an arduous journey, which took about four days.

In the city of Bethlehem, the city of David, in which the prophets foretold that Christ would be born (Mic 5:2), the Holy Family found no place to stay because of the great crowding, in addition to their poverty, which did not allow them to obtain reasonable shelter. The situation was made harder when the Virgin felt that her hour to give birth had come, so the family was forced to enter a cave where animals were kept. In this filthy stable the Virgin found no better place to lay her newborn than a small manger in which animals' food was put, after she had wrapped Him in some cloths.
Thus Christ found no place for Himself in the houses of men, so He was born in a place not for the dwelling of people but of animals, to break by His humility the pride of men.

And He was laid in the manger to be food not for animals but for the whole world, by His most holy Body and Blood. When St. Luke mentions her firstborn son, he means that He was her first child, and this does not mean that she had other children; rather the first child to be born is always called the firstborn, regardless of whether his mother will bear another after him or not. And of course the Virgin did not bear after Christ, since her womb was reserved for Christ alone, as Ezekiel the prophet mentions: "This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall enter in by it; because the Lord, the God of Israel, hath entered in by it, therefore it shall be shut" (Ezek 44:2).

Do you accept, my brother, to give up some of your comfort and needs in order to hold fast to God and to love others? Look at the humility of Christ and His endurance of people's refusal to receive Him, so that you will not grieve if people refuse to help you.

In the darkness of the night a great angel appeared with a strong light, and the simple shepherds were afraid; then the angel reassured them, and even declared that he was bringing good news for them and for all mankind.

The angel declared that the fullness of time had come, and that the awaited Messiah, the Savior of the world, was born. This is a clear declaration from heaven of the divinity of Christ, since he calls Him the Lord. The angel appeared to shepherds because they tend the sheep that were offered as sacrifices in the Temple to take away the sins of the people according to the Law of Moses, to announce to them the birth of Christ, the true Lamb to whom these sacrifices pointed, so that He might take away the sins of the whole world; for He is not merely a lord but the Lord, and none other.
The angel gave them a sign to confirm his good news and to make it easy to find Him: a child wrapped in swaddling clothes and lying in a manger in Bethlehem, that is, the city of David.

After this good news, heaven proclaimed its glorification of the holy Lord in the form of a multitude of angels who appeared with the angel, giving glory to God who was born in the manger, and who is also glorified by the heavenly ones, and who gives peace to man by taking his sins away from him; and then man worships God and his heart rejoices, after having angered Him in the Garden of Eden and being separated from Him for a long time, so that God is pleased with him and rejoices in him.
God is glorified in His angels, so keep vigil with the shepherds to praise Him in your prayers and share with the angels, and you will experience His work in your heart and rejoice in Him.
Enjoy the praises from the Book of the Midnight Praise along with the prayers of the Agpeya every day.

entries.section: (3) The shepherds' visit to the manger

paragraphs.text: The shepherds' joy at the angels' good news was great, so they hastened to Bethlehem, near which they had been keeping watch, searching all the stables and caves for the great Child.

entries.section: (3) The shepherds' visit to the manger

paragraphs.text: How great was the shepherds' joy when they found the Child in the manger with His mother the Virgin Mary and the aged Joseph, and they told Joseph and Mary of the angel's good news to them about the birth of Christ the Savior.

entries.section: (3) The shepherds' visit to the manger

paragraphs.text: Because of the shepherds' abundant exultation, a number of Jews, with whom Bethlehem was crowded because of the census, gathered and heard the shepherds' good news, but they could not grasp the mystery of the Incarnation although they witnessed it, and were content with wonder and astonishment.

entries.section: (3) The shepherds' visit to the manger

paragraphs.text: The Virgin kept the shepherds' good news with faith and spiritual understanding, pondering its meanings, which confirm the divinity of Christ. This means that St. Luke drew his Gospel from the Virgin Mary, who told him what she felt in her heart.

This also shows the Virgin's distinction from the people of Bethlehem, who were content with wonder, and also from the shepherds, who praised God, for she meditated deeply, and her faith in the divinity of Christ was confirmed.

Do you meditate on the words of the Holy Bible and apply them in your life every day as the voice of God to you? And do you see God in the events around you and in people's words, so that everything leads you to repentance and the knowledge of God?

entries.section: (3) The shepherds' visit to the manger

paragraphs.text: The shepherds returned to the place of their folds outside Bethlehem, but with hearts changed from material preoccupation to praising God because of what they had heard from the angel and what they had seen inside the cattle stable, namely Christ who was born.

entries.section: (4) The circumcision of Christ and the purification of the Virgin

paragraphs.text: Since Christ condescended by His Incarnation, He also humbled Himself in submitting to the Law, though He had no need of it, but He fulfilled all righteousness on our behalf. So He was circumcised on the eighth day as God commanded Abraham, as a sign for him and for all his descendants in their bodies, declaring their allegiance to God and their distinction from unbelievers.

Circumcision is a type of Baptism, in which there is a cutting off of the evil nature and the beginning of a new life with God; and circumcision is called in our colloquial speech "purification of males."
It was the Jewish custom to name the child on this day, so He was named Jesus, that is, Savior, as the angel Gabriel declared in his good news to the Virgin Mary.

entries.section: (4) The circumcision of Christ and the purification of the Virgin

paragraphs.text: The Law of Moses decreed (Lev 12:5, 1) that the woman who has given birth should not enter the Temple for forty days in the case of a male child, or eighty days in the case of a female child, and she was considered unclean during this period. In the New Testament the Church has also kept this period, considering it a period of bodily rest and spiritual repentance ... but of what is she to repent?!?
The woman must not forget, amid the joys of her giving birth, that she has borne a child who carries the sin of Adam and Eve, in which the woman was a direct cause.
And her period of repentance ends with her newborn child's attaining salvation in the holy sacrament of Baptism, and then she presents herself with him for the communion of the divine Mysteries.

entries.section: (4) The circumcision of Christ and the purification of the Virgin

paragraphs.text: Openeth the womb: that is, firstborn.
Holy: sanctified and consecrated to God.

The firstborn was presented for the service of the Lord, or was redeemed by presenting a sum to the Temple, because when God killed the firstborn of the Egyptians He said to His people that their firstborn, whom He had redeemed by the slaying of the Passover lamb on their behalf, had become His own (Ex 13:2, 12). The tribe of Levi was consecrated to Him, but as for the firstborn of the rest of the people, each one gave a ransom for himself, a sum of money, to the Temple.

entries.section: (4) The circumcision of Christ and the purification of the Virgin

paragraphs.text: For her purification the mother offered a lamb and a young pigeon, the first as a burnt offering and the second as a sin offering, a reference to Christ who by His Cross and death pleased God as a burnt offering and took away our iniquities ... but in the case of the poor, like the Virgin and Joseph, they offered a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons. The pigeon is a symbol of simplicity, and the turtledove of the beautiful voice, that is, the preaching of the word of God.

Christ emptied Himself and fulfilled the Law in order to be like us in everything. May you share the lives of those around you, so that you feel for them and show your love for them, even with few words that draw them to you, and they open their hearts to you and find rest from many troubles.

entries.section: (5) The song of praise of Simeon the elder

paragraphs.text: Near the Temple in Jerusalem there lived an old man named Simeon, distinguished by righteousness and goodness in his relationship with those around him and by devoutness in his worship of God, waiting for the Messiah of whom the prophecies of the prophets in Israel had spoken, to give salvation and consolation to his people. The Holy Spirit was upon him, for in the Old Testament He came upon some people for specified periods, which differs from His permanent dwelling in the New Testament inside the believers. Church tradition tells us that this Simeon was among the seventy-two elders whom King Ptolemy in Egypt chose to translate the Torah into Greek, and he doubted the words of Isaiah about the conception of the Virgin, "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel" (Isa 7:14), and wanted to translate it "a young woman," but God declared to him that he should translate it as it is, that is, "virgin," and even promised him that he would see with his own eyes the fulfillment of this verse.

entries.section: (5) The song of praise of Simeon the elder

paragraphs.text: One day the Holy Spirit moved Simeon the elder to go to the Temple, where a great number of fathers and mothers had gathered with their children, and large numbers of the people had come to offer sacrifices and to give a ransom for their firstborn children. The Holy Spirit guided him to the Child Jesus as He was entering the Temple with His mother for them to pay the ransom for Him according to the custom of the Jews, as we mentioned. So Simeon took Him and carried Him in his arms and raised his voice in praise and blessing to God, who was carried by him and who is in the highest.

entries.section: (5) The song of praise of Simeon the elder

paragraphs.text: According to thy word: because God had promised him that he would live until he saw the Virgin bear the awaited Messiah, so he lived longer than the usual span of men until he saw Christ, and he longed to depart to heaven.
Thy salvation: that is, Christ the Savior.
All people: because Christ is the Savior of the whole world, Jews and Gentiles.

Simeon declared in his song of praise that he had witnessed the fulfillment of the prophecy of Isaiah, for he saw Christ the Lord, the Savior of the whole world, not only as consolation and glory for Israel but as a light for the whole world, bringing them back from idolatry to faith in the true God, and saving all from their sins. And since he enjoyed the sight of God, he was satisfied and rejoiced, and no longer needed to live in this world but to depart to eternity, confident in the redemption of Christ. Because of the importance of this song of praise, the Church repeats it in the prayer of sleep in the Agpeya every day, and in the midnight prayer, and also in the Midnight Praise.

Come, my brother, to the Temple today to behold salvation in the Body and Blood of the Lord on the altar, as salvation for you from all your sins and as strength and light for your life, so that you are filled with vitality and satisfaction and your eyes are lifted up to the constant union with God in eternity; and to the extent that you enjoy Holy Communion you behold God, and you fear nothing, not even death.

entries.section: (5) The song of praise of Simeon the elder

paragraphs.text: Joseph the carpenter and the Virgin Mary marveled at God's declaring the good news of salvation to Simeon the elder, as the angel Gabriel had earlier announced to them the good news of the Nativity, and they were also astonished that this salvation is not limited to the Jews but is likewise for the Gentiles.

It is made clear here that the Virgin is the mother of Christ, and Joseph is not His father, though it appears so before people, and this is mentioned in (v. 27), that they are His parents as people suppose.

entries.section: (5) The song of praise of Simeon the elder

paragraphs.text: Simeon, who was filled with the Holy Spirit, also blessed Joseph and Mary, and declared to the Virgin, who would see with her own eyes the preaching of Christ (for Joseph would die before this), how some would believe and be saved and rise from their sins, while many would refuse to believe and be condemned, and how the sign of Christ would be spoken against, which is the Cross on which the redemption of the world would be accomplished.

entries.section: (5) The song of praise of Simeon the elder

paragraphs.text: A sword: the meaning is figurative, that is, severe sufferings.
Thoughts may be revealed: the evils of those who opposed Christ and crucified Him will appear.

Simeon also declared to the Virgin that she would suffer many pains when she would see the Jews' opposition to her Son, and would even see His sufferings and crucifixion, as the ninth hour prayer in the Agpeya recalls, and when she would see the thoughts and evils of the scribes, the Pharisees and the priests of the Jews who crucified Christ, who even opposed the Virgin until the end of her life.

entries.section: (6) The song of praise of Anna the daughter of Phanuel

paragraphs.text: St. Luke continues to tell us about God's announcements of the birth of the Messiah to those who were waiting for it and were concerned with His birth, for God reveals Himself to those who seek Him. And in the company of the elders Anna joins Simeon, for God announced the good news of His birth to the elders in appreciation of their wisdom and perseverance in spiritual striving with Him.

Anna means "God's grace," Phanuel "the face of God," and Aser "rich." Her name has a beautiful meaning that gives hope amid afflictions, since her life appears hard because of her husband's death after seven years of marriage; she was a young woman, probably no more than twenty-five years old, but she was able to fill her emptiness with the love of God. She lived near the Temple, occupied with prayers and worship, and in asceticism she even fasted much to free herself from everything and deepen her relationship with God. She lived 84 years in this life, and probably her earlier life was bound to God in preparation for a deeper relationship with Him.

She is a great picture of perseverance, an example for all widows and a hope for those who suffer from emptiness or afflictions. She had passed a hundred years and was still in much worship, waiting for Christ the Savior. Does affliction drive you to cling to God? And do you try to fill your emptiness with prayers, readings and service? Do you persevere in your striving even if God's answer to your prayers is delayed for many long years?

entries.section: (6) The song of praise of Anna the daughter of Phanuel

paragraphs.text: The Holy Spirit, who came upon her, led her to meet the Virgin and Joseph and to enjoy seeing the Child Jesus carried in Simeon's arms. She began to praise God and to speak prophecies about the redemption and salvation that this Child would accomplish. Many of those who offered worship in the Temple, waiting for the Messiah the Savior, gathered, and heard Anna's words and praise, and enjoyed seeing the Child Jesus Christ.

After they had completed what the Law commanded in Jerusalem, St. Luke mentions that they returned to Nazareth, but this did not happen quickly, as is understood from (Mt 2); it took several years, for they lived a period in Bethlehem where the Magi visited them, then came Herod's order to kill the children, so they fled to Egypt and stayed there for a time, then returned to Nazareth, passing through Judea.

St. Luke comments on the life of Christ from His early childhood to the age of twelve, which He lived in Nazareth, that He grew in His childhood like an ordinary human being. How wonderful it is that God emptied Himself to become man and grow like the rest of mankind, although in His divinity He is perfect from eternity.

We have no information about this period, but it is understood from the context of the verses that Joseph and Mary were concerned about the worship of God, and about visiting Jerusalem and offering sacrifices every year, so they brought Him up in a religious upbringing and taught Him the Holy Scriptures in the synagogue. But He was distinguished by His submission to the Holy Spirit in Him, so His growth, strength, spirituality and wisdom appeared, and grace overflowed upon Him as a perfect man, an example for all of us.
To the extent that you submit to God and the Church and are bound to her, God's grace and wisdom overflow upon you.

entries.section: (8) The boy Jesus in the Temple

paragraphs.text: The Gospel shows here Joseph and Mary's adherence to the worship of God, and their going to Jerusalem yearly at the official feasts, the most important of which was the feast of the Passover, which they first kept in Egypt and after which they went out into the wilderness. It is a clear type of the redemption of Christ on the Cross and of partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord.

entries.section: (8) The boy Jesus in the Temple

paragraphs.text: After the custom of the feast: that is, they completed the rites of the feast of the Passover.

When Jesus reached the age of twelve, which is the age at which a person is bound to complete all the religious rites according to the law of the Jews, since it is the age of discernment after the stage of childhood in which discernment is partial, He went with Joseph and Mary, as was their custom at the feast of the Passover, to Jerusalem.
During the feast a great number of teachers would gather in circles inside the Temple, and around them the Jews would ask them about various fields of worship and the spiritual life.

After completing the rites of the feast, they departed, returning to their city Nazareth, and the custom was to travel in caravans for fear of robbers. The caravan was divided into two parts: in front the women with the small children, and the second part the men, while the youths, of whose age Jesus was, would walk at the front or the rear. Jesus lingered in the Temple among the teachers, asking them, conversing with them and answering them, and Joseph and Mary did not know this.

entries.section: (8) The boy Jesus in the Temple

paragraphs.text: After a day's journey from Jerusalem to the north on the road to Nazareth, that is, about twenty miles, they had to spend the night and rest, so Joseph asked Mary about her son Jesus and did not find Him with her, and she also discovered that He was not with Joseph. They began to look for Him among the relatives and acquaintances in the caravan, but unfortunately did not find Him, so they returned another day's journey to Jerusalem and kept searching for Him everywhere.

They suffered greatly because of Joseph's old age and the physical strain on them. They did not suspect that an accident might have befallen Him, because of the angel's good news and the many heavenly announcements, but perhaps they thought that He had lost the way and wandered far away somewhere, or that He had ascended to heaven and deprived them of seeing Him for a time, and this tormented them greatly. At last, at the end of the third day, they found Jesus in the Temple, sitting among the teachers.

entries.section: (8) The boy Jesus in the Temple

paragraphs.text: The Virgin, with Joseph, noticed Jesus' distinction and His superiority over the teachers in His questions and answers, and all who heard Him were amazed and marveled with them.

entries.section: (8) The boy Jesus in the Temple

paragraphs.text: How great was the joy of the Virgin and Joseph when they found Him! The Virgin expressed the extent of the suffering she had endured with Joseph in feeling His loss, and the Virgin's humility appears in her putting Joseph before herself when she said, "Thy father and I"; here it means his responsibility for Him as a father, although He was not of his seed, as the Gospels make clear.

entries.section: (8) The boy Jesus in the Temple

paragraphs.text: Jesus alerted His mother and Joseph to the heavenly announcements they had heard about Him and His work as Savior, and His eternal sonship to God, and that He must accomplish His purpose, that is, the aim for which the Father sent Him into the world.

entries.section: (8) The boy Jesus in the Temple

paragraphs.text: These words were hard for her to understand, but the Virgin realized the importance of these words and kept them in her heart until God would interpret them to her later.

Jesus' concern for His sonship to God and His accomplishing His purposes does not mean His neglecting His sonship to His mother; rather He submitted in obedience to her and to Joseph to give us a wonderful example in obeying parents. The Virgin also gives us an example of true motherhood in breadth of heart and leaving children to live according to their gifts and abilities, and not according to a fixed picture of what fathers and mothers want.

Honor your elders, especially your parents, and submit to them and offer your love to all, and do not force anyone to behave as you want, and give freedom to everyone, and to your children, as long as their behavior is not evil.

entries.section: (8) The boy Jesus in the Temple

paragraphs.text: Here is the last mention of Joseph the carpenter, and he probably died in the following years, about which we have no details except this verse, from the age of 12 to 30, for he is not referred to at the beginning of Christ's preaching ministry, but only the Virgin. This means that Christ began to work as a carpenter and bore responsibility for His mother after Joseph.
Luke speaks about His life as a man, how He continued to grow in all aspects, psychological, bodily and spiritual, and this was evident before people, but rather before God.
The announcement of the Baptist and the Baptism of Christ

entries.section: (1) The beginning of the Baptist's ministry

paragraphs.text: St. Luke specifies the time of the beginning of the ministry of John the Baptist by the kings and governors belonging to the Roman Empire, and it is also the time of the beginning of Christ's ministry, because the Baptist preceded Him by six months. Tiberius Caesar: the Roman emperor at that time.
Pontius Pilate: who judged Christ, and was the Roman governor over all of Judea.
Judea: the southern part of the land of the Jews.
Herod: this is Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, the killer of the children of Bethlehem.
Tetrarch: the Romans divided the region into four provinces.
Galilee: the northern part of the land of the Jews.
Philip: son of Herod the Great and husband of Herodias.
Judea: this is Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, the killer of the children of Bethlehem.
Ituraea, Trachonitis, Abilene: places adjoining Judea and Galilee.

As a historian, St. Luke also mentions two rulers over neighboring regions, namely Philip the son of Herod the Great and Lysanias. The date, as the Fathers established, is approximately AD 26, on the basis that the birth of Christ was about 4 BC, and from this his precision as a historian appears.

entries.section: (1) The beginning of the Baptist's ministry

paragraphs.text: The word of God came unto: that is, the work of the Spirit in John the Baptist to begin his ministry, and to declare the word of God to the crowds and call them to repentance.
The wilderness: that is, the desert of Judea.

According to the law of the Jews the high priest remained so throughout his life, but the Romans intervened and deposed Annas and brought in Caiaphas, the husband of his daughter, and Annas kept his authority, therefore Luke mentions him.

entries.section: (1) The beginning of the Baptist's ministry

paragraphs.text: The baptism of repentance: John's baptism was accompanied by people's confession of their sins, so it was a preparation for the sacraments of Baptism and Confession.

John was brought up in the wilderness for about thirty years under God's care, then began his ministry in the regions around the Jordan, calling for repentance and return to God, and whoever accepted his word he baptized in the river Jordan to begin a new life with God. This was a preparation for Christ's preaching of repentance and His baptizing with the Holy Spirit, so that men receive the new nature from Christ the Redeemer and their sins are forgiven.
It is understood from the verse that John moved about among the regions around the river Jordan, and was not settled in one place.

Repentance and the sacrament of Confession are two essential conditions for the forgiveness of your sins, so hasten to your father of confession to be freed from the dominion of sin and begin a life of righteousness. Repeat this with insistence in daily repentance before God and confession every month in the Church, and your life will always be renewed.

entries.section: (1) The beginning of the Baptist's ministry

paragraphs.text: Thus the prophecy of Isaiah (Isa 40:3-5) is fulfilled about John the Baptist, who goes before and prepares the way of Christ by his preaching in the wilderness and his calling the crowds to repentance and an upright life, just as the kings' messengers used to go before them, calling on the people to remove the obstacles in the road the kings would travel. What is meant here is repentance from the sins that obstruct God's way within people's hearts.

entries.section: (1) The beginning of the Baptist's ministry

paragraphs.text: All flesh: a prophecy of the acceptance of all the nations into faith and salvation in the name of the Lord Christ (Isa 40:3-5).

Isaiah prophesies that the Gentiles, sunk in sin like valleys, will be filled with the Holy Spirit through their faith and their return to God. And as for the Jews, lofty in their pride and in their boasting of their origin and their Law, like mountains and high hills, when they come to repentance and faith in the humble Christ they too will be humbled, and everyone who was crooked or rough (rough ways) in the life of sin will be made straight by accepting the salvation of Christ.
When John proclaimed repentance and baptism for the forgiveness of sins, great crowds of Jews went out to him to be baptized by him, for they felt that he was a great prophet.

God gave him a strong awe in their hearts, but the Baptist was not preoccupied with their multitude, knowing that they had not repented with all their hearts, and that they had undergone baptism because they were children of the prophets and children of God, so he was compelled to rebuke them that they might truly repent, and described them as a generation of vipers, because the viper crawls on its belly on the ground, so it signifies attachment to earthly things, and it is also poisonous and harms everyone around it. Some kinds of them eat their mother's belly so that she dies and they come forth to life, so it signifies selfish conduct and wronging others, even those who are close. And he warned them of the wrath of God the Judge that was coming upon them if they did not repent.
He called them to do good to everyone, for this is the proof of true repentance.

And he surprised them by saying that they should not rely on the honor of their sonship to Abraham, for this would not stop God's wrath against them, and even more than this, he declared to them that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. What is meant by the stones is the stony hearts in the children of the Gentiles, because of the hardness of their hearts like stone; He is able to make them hearts of flesh that believe in Him and love Him. Thus the Jews perish because of the hardness of their hearts and their lack of repentance, and the Gentiles are saved by their faith in Christ and their walking in righteousness.

Do not rely, my brother, on the fact that your name is Christian, for this will not protect you from God's wrath; rather you must offer tears of repentance and regret your sins every day, and leave your evil works and do good to everyone and become a true son of Christ, who loved all and gave Himself for them.

The Baptist grew more severe, and declared that the hour was near, for Christ would begin His preaching shortly; and if they did not repent and believe in Him, the axe, that is, the word of God, which is like a two-edged sword, would judge everyone who does not believe in Him. By the root of the trees are meant the leaders, priests and teachers, whom the word of Christ condemns before the rest of the Jews because of their lack of repentance, and nothing awaits them but the eternal fire.

Remembering death and judgment is necessary for our lives, so that we may awaken from our laziness and pride and our delight in the evil lusts of the world and our persistence in the sin that we have justified so as not to repent.

entries.section: (3) The Baptist's answers to the questions

paragraphs.text: The Baptist's words affected the hearts of his hearers, so they inquired about the practical application of his words, and the crowds of poor Jews asked him about the meaning of repentance and its fruit, and he spoke to them about love and giving. He that hath two coats (that is, a poor man who owns only two garments) let him give one to him that hath none. The coat is what is worn inside beneath the outer clothes, that is, the least a person needs. Likewise whoever has food, even a little, let him give part of it to the hungry. Thus we find ourselves moving in John's words from the Old Testament to the New, preparing for the self-giving love of Christ and the life of fellowship in the Church, and that giving is required not only of the rich but also of the poor.

entries.section: (3) The Baptist's answers to the questions

paragraphs.text: The tax collectors: they were a group of Jewish farmers, but richer than ordinary people, who undertook to pay the Roman taxes for a specified Jewish district and then collected them from individuals with the help of Roman soldiers, and whoever paid more to the Roman state was chosen to collect the taxes. They would add to the required taxes and so became rich, but they were an example of love of money and exploitation of the weak, however needy they were. John did not ask them to leave their jobs, but declared to them the importance of justice and leaving the love of money, that is, to collect only what they had paid or a little more by which to support themselves.

entries.section: (3) The Baptist's answers to the questions

paragraphs.text: Among those who went out to the Baptist were some soldiers, who, since they had authority over everyone, exploited it in wronging others and extorting their money, and whoever did not obey them they would fabricate charges against and complain of to the Roman authority, so they too fell into exploiting their work to collect money. So John asked them to be content with their wages (their rations).

Do you feel for those around you and hasten to help them, even if you have little money or effort? Do you exploit your work, position and connections for your own benefit, or for the love of others and helping them? Remember that Christ used His position as God to give you His full love on the Cross, and what have you given Him?

More than 400 years had passed during which no prophet had appeared in Israel, and they believed that the coming prophet would be the Messiah. Therefore, when John appeared calling to them like the prophets to repent so as to be saved from divine punishment, in addition to his asceticism regarding material things and his boldness in speech, they thought that he was the Christ.

The humility of the Baptist appears, for he declares himself a servant preparing the way for Christ, and his baptism with water is a symbol of the cleansing from sin that would be accomplished in the baptism of Christ with the Holy Spirit, and this is joined with fire because the Holy Spirit burns up sin like fire. Here is a prophetic declaration about the Holy Spirit, who would work on the day of Pentecost through the hands of the disciples and then their successors the bishops and priests in baptizing the believers, and he declares his unworthiness to stoop down and unloose the latchet of Christ's shoes, for this is an honor greater than he can receive.

St. Cyril the Great proves the divinity of Christ from this verse, because Christ here gives the Holy Spirit, that is, His own Spirit, so He is God; and only one who has a body can wear shoes, so He is the incarnate Christ and the God who became man, and this is also a proof of His Incarnation.

St. Gregory the Great says that the shoe signifies the humanity of Christ, so John declares that he is not able to unloose its latchet, that is, to uncover the mysteries of the divine Incarnation; how wonderful is God's condescension to become incarnate for our sake!
Do not attribute the glory to yourself, my brother, but to God with thanksgiving, especially when people praise you.

John speaks about Christ the Judge, and compares the day of judgment to the day of winnowing wheat, that is, separating its grains from the husk surrounding them, which is called chaff, in a wide place called the threshing floor. The fan, that is, the winnowing fork, is a wooden staff with several prongs at its end like a fork, which lifts the grains of wheat into the air, and by the action of the air or the wind the light husk surrounding the grain flies far away, while the grain falls in its place because it is heavier, and thus the grains are separated from the chaff. Then the wheat, which is the believers filled with the grace of God, is gathered into His garner, that is, the paradise of delight, having been tested by the wind, which signifies trials, and their strength and steadfastness were revealed; but the empty husks in which there are no grains signify the people who are empty of God's grace and faith, and trials expose them as mere chaff to be burned with fire, that is, eternal torment.
And the One who holds the fan, that is, the winnowing fork, is Christ the Judge, who rewards His children with bliss, but the wicked He casts into the eternal fire.

Do not neglect Christ's call to you to repent; enjoy His holy Mysteries, and remain steadfast in His Church, and you will not be troubled by the winds of trials, and thus you secure your happy eternity.
The original aim of John's preaching was calling them to repentance, in preparation for the preaching of Christ and His declaring the greatness of His salvation which He offers to mankind.
To this were added many teachings and exhortations, that is, consolations with which John encouraged the souls of his hearers, which the Holy Bible cannot contain to write.

The Baptist's ministry did not stop at the common people but extended to all classes, even to King Herod himself, who is called Herod Antipas, who was distinguished by many evils and wickedness, especially in his seizing Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, to be his wife during his brother's lifetime.

Herod could not bear John's bold rebukes and wanted to silence this voice, so he shut him up in prison, and afterward killed him; but the voice continued to cry out, rebuking his conscience, so that when the preaching of Christ spread, he said that it was the Baptist whom he had killed who had risen again.
Herod imprisoned John after he had baptized Christ, but St. Luke mentions the imprisonment here because it is connected with John's rebuke of him.
Added yet this above all: he added to all his evils for which he was notorious that he shut up the great prophet beloved by the people, John the Baptist.

Do not reject the voice of God that rebukes you for your sins through the tongue of those around you, for even if you silence them by your anger and authority, your conscience continues to rebuke you, and if you silence it, judgment awaits you .... Now is an opportunity for repentance, so you may recover your peace and purity through your humility.

John's baptism showed mankind's need of repentance and salvation, and Christ, the representative of mankind, came to be baptized although He was without sin, but to bear our sins and fulfill all righteousness on our behalf, and to be an example for us in coming to baptism, but the baptism that is with the Holy Spirit in the New Testament; and He prayed to be an example for us in prayer also, so that heaven is opened to us and we have a relationship with God.

Here the Holy Trinity appears clearly: the Son in the water, and the Holy Spirit, who has been in the Son from eternity, appearing in bodily form, which is a dove, and the voice of the Father from heaven declaring that the One in the water is the one true Son, in whom is all His pleasure; therefore the Church calls the Feast of Theophany the Feast of the Divine Manifestation.

If Christ fulfilled all righteousness on our behalf, may we make up for the shortcomings of others and cover their faults and do what they ought to do for the sake of God and out of love for them, so that we are truly children of God and deserve the heavenly praise and divine blessings.

After the baptism of Christ and the appearance of the Holy Spirit upon Him like a dove, this was a sign of the beginning of Christ's ministry, so here He declares His being full of the Holy Spirit and led by Him, although the Holy Spirit is His own Spirit from eternity; but here is a declaration to us to make us know the Holy Trinity and the importance of the Holy Spirit's leading of our lives. If the servant is not first filled with the Spirit, through his attachment to the holy Mysteries, prayer and reading the Holy Bible, and also his humble submission to God's guidance, he cannot serve successfully.
Christ fasted forty days before the beginning of His ministry to declare the importance of the goal, which is the spiritual life, accompanied by renunciation of material things.

He was tempted throughout the forty days by the devil, and the devil could not prevail over Him, because His asceticism in fasting and His solitude for prayer in the wilderness nullify every power of the devil, as Christ Himself said about Satan, "This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting" (Mk 9:29).

Christ fasted only forty days, like Moses and Elijah, so as not to do anything beyond human capacity, and He hungered to confirm His true humanity in which He is like us. Therefore we can imitate His fasting and His prayers with quiet retreat, and so overcome all the devil's wars.
There were many temptations throughout the forty-day fast, but at its end the strongest temptations appeared, and they are these three mentioned here.
So Satan came to Christ in the wilderness of Judea, after He felt hunger from fasting forty days, and focused his words on Christ's need of food.
The devil always chooses the points of need and weakness in us to fight us with them, so that his words may seem reasonable and we accept them and fall into sin.

Here he wanted Christ to use His divine power for the benefit of His comfort as a man, and this of course is rejected, because Christ came to be like us in everything, and to bear the hardest sufferings for our sake and to triumph over the devil while in this human weakness, that we too may triumph in Him.

If thou be the Son of God: the devil's words are doubting and provoking, as is his habit in his wars against us through the tongues of those around us, and by this question he wanted to understand the truth about Jesus: if He turned the stone into bread he would know that He is the Christ and keep away from Him, and if He said "I cannot," he would know that He is a mere man and fight Him and defeat Him.

The Fathers say that the devil offers only stones and not bread, so that our hearts become stony and hard. And they say that what may be meant by the stone is heresies, which become to us a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense instead of the word of God, the true food.

In His answer Christ turned attention to a more important matter, which is spiritual nourishment by the word of God. He relied in this on what is written in the Torah (Deut 8:3), to teach us to rest our lives on God's commandments. If a person is satisfied by the word of God and by partaking of the Mysteries, he can bear the sufferings of life and the weakness of the body, and is content with what he has even if it is little.

The second temptation is the desire to possess the material things of the world, and in order to dazzle Christ in his temptation, the devil took Him up to a high mountain, so that vast areas of the surrounding countries appeared in all their glory.

With audacity and deceit the devil declared his dominion over all the earth and his ability to give it to whomever he wishes, although he rules only over the wicked; but he is a liar from the beginning, and he deceives us to shake our faith if we believe his lies.

He asked Christ to worship him, which is the worship of devotion and submission, and then He would give Him to reign over the earth and mankind without enduring the sufferings of the Cross. He always calls us to the easy life and immersion in pleasures and love of possession, so that we give up our vigilance against sin and our spiritual striving, preoccupied with the delights and splendors of the world. This is the worship that he asks of us, and consequently we abandon our prayers and our love for God.

The Lord Christ did not discuss with the devil his lies in claiming authority over the earth, to teach us to flee from dialogue with Satan's thoughts. He answered him with what is written in the Holy Bible, which is worshiping God alone (Deut 6:13), and Jesus' word "Get thee behind me," that we may learn to drive away all his thoughts, however pleasant, tempting or convincing they may seem.
Where is your heart? ... If it is in the love of God and attachment to Him, you will not be affected by any of the devil's enticements of money, lust or possessions.

The third temptation was in Jerusalem, in the Temple, that is, the holiest place. The devil fights in every place, even in the Church. The pinnacle of the Temple is its highest place, and he repeats his doubting and provoking of Christ, so that He would use His power for His personal glory, by throwing Himself down from the highest place with the crowds massed below in the Temple, and then the angels would appear carrying Him, so that He would come down among the crowds and begin His ministry. The devil's words seem convincing, but their reality is drawing Jesus into pride, love of display, and people's glorifying Him.
And the sin of pride fights everyone, especially those in office or authority, and it also fights the servants and priests who are in the holy place.

When Satan found Jesus relying on what is written, he too relied on what is written, but with deceit and wrong interpretation, for he took part of (Ps 91:11, 12), which applies to God's keeping of His children if any problems and temptations from the devil befall them, as verse 13 makes clear: "Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder: the young lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under feet," that is, God keeps them by His angels and they triumph over the devil, the old serpent. These verses do not mean a display of our power to obtain honor from people.

Jesus answered him with the words of the Holy Bible from (Deut 6:16), which is that it is not right to tempt God to test His truthfulness, but rather we trust in His promises if a temptation meets us.

Beware of pursuing honor and love of display, trusting in God's promises and His support for you, and to the extent that you hide yourself, you are raised in God's sight and He rewards you, not only in eternity but with peace and joy in this life.

After Christ spent forty days in the wilderness of Judea, He returned to Galilee, where He was brought up in one of its cities, Nazareth. The Evangelist stresses that He was led by the Holy Spirit, to teach us submission to the work of the Spirit in us and not to our own thinking.

Christ went to Galilee twice: the first is the one mentioned here after His baptism, then He returned to Judea, and after about a year He visited Galilee after the imprisonment of John the Baptist, as Matthew and Mark mention (Mt 4:12, Mk 1:14), and John mentioned both visits (Jn 1:43, Jn 4:3).
This means that He visited Nazareth also twice: the first Luke mentions here and the second Matthew and Mark mention at His visit to Galilee (Mt 13:54-58, Mk 6:1-6).
