Jesus began to teach in the synagogues of the cities of Galilee, and likewise the villages around Capernaum, the center of His preaching in Galilee, where He taught and performed many miracles, which aroused the jealousy of the people of the city of Nazareth because He had not begun with them. He taught with authority and power, and the hearers were amazed and glorified Him.

V. 16 As his custom was: Christ was accustomed to attend the synagogue during His stay in Nazareth from His childhood, and likewise He was accustomed to attend the synagogues in every town where He preached, keeping the Jewish order and seizing these opportunities to preach. Synagogues were spread throughout Judea wherever ten families gathered, and readings from the Holy Scriptures and preaching were offered in them. Christ entered as was His custom to interpret the prophecies that referred to Him, for He did not come to destroy but to fulfill.

It was the custom in the synagogue that after the reading from the books of Moses, there would be a reading from the prophets, so He chose from the book of Isaiah these verses (Isa 61:1-2), which are like the speech from the throne announcing the beginning of the ministry of the awaited Messiah.

Isaiah spoke in the spirit of prophecy about the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the Messiah, who begins His ministry by preaching to the poor, whom the devil has humiliated and kept far from God; and everyone whose heart is broken because of his inability to fulfill the commandments, and likewise everyone whom the devil has bound with sin and who longs for the freedom of the glory of the children of God. And He opens the eyes of those whose eyes have been darkened by evil, and gives all the crushed and weak new life in Him.

The acceptable year of the Lord is the year of jubilee, which comes every fifty years (Lev 25:10), in which the land rests and is not sown, and slaves are set free. It refers to the time in which Christ preaches and redeems mankind to receive eternal life.
The beginning of Christ's preaching in Nazareth coincided with the year of jubilee among the Jews.

V. 20 He closed: the Holy Scriptures were written on skin parchments and rolled around a stick, so they were in the form of a cylinder; so after the reading he rolled it around the stick, that is, closed it.
The minister: the person responsible for keeping the Holy Scriptures in the synagogue.

He sat down: the custom in the synagogues of old was to stand when reading the Scriptures and then to sit for preaching, and the eyes of the people were fastened on Him, as He read the words with authority and power.

The Lord Christ interpreted the words of Isaiah about the Messiah, declaring their fulfillment now in Him, and thus He announced to them the beginning of the New Testament and the salvation that they had awaited.
Christ came for the sake of the weak to give them strength and freedom. So do not be disturbed by your weakness, and be confident that Christ loves you and supports you and has come for your sake.

Despite the amazement of the people of Nazareth at Christ's powerful words, they despised Him because He was the son of Joseph, the village carpenter. Because of their pride they looked at His social origin and did not benefit from His teachings.
Do you despise others, being haughty about your lineage or your abilities, and do not accept the word of God from their mouths or learn from their virtues?
V. 23 Done in Capernaum: it is understood that He visited Capernaum before Nazareth, and performed many miracles in it that St. Luke did not mention.

The divinity of Christ appeared in His exposing their thoughts that blamed Him, because He had performed many miracles in Capernaum, but when He came to Nazareth He performed only a few miracles, for they felt, selfishly, that they were more entitled than any other town to His miracles, and they considered this a weakness in Him and an inability to perform miracles among them.

Christ declared the reason for His not performing miracles among them, which was the weakness of their faith because of their pride and their not esteeming the power of their townsman, as happened with the prophets in the Old Testament, for their knowing the origin of the prophets in their childhood and youth made them despise and disbelieve their prophecies and teachings, so this became a common proverb among the Jews.
Do not be distressed if those close to you reject your word, but humble yourself and continue in your love, your prayers and your invitation to them to draw near to the Church.
Christ showed His acceptance of the Gentiles as well as the Jews, confirming that with events from the Old Testament.

In the days of Elijah, when famine spread, he performed the miracle with a Gentile widow from the city of Sarepta of Sidon, a city on the coast of the Mediterranean next to the city of Sidon, and he stayed with her and not with any Jewish widow, and blessed her house, preferring her over all the widows of the Jews, because of the readiness of her heart for faith (1 Kgs 17).
Likewise Elisha healed Naaman the Gentile, who was one of the enemies of the Jews, although there were many Jewish lepers whom he did not heal.
By this Christ confirmed His concern to perform miracles in Capernaum among the Gentiles because of their readiness for faith, whereas in His own town Nazareth He did not, because of their unbelief.

Examine yourself, lest the weakness of your faith and your not seeking God be the cause of hindering His work with you. And open your heart with love to all people and pray for them because they are children of God. And do not be vexed at God's helping them more than you, but let this drive you to draw near to Him with humility and supplication.

Christ exposed the thoughts of the people of Nazareth, and revealed their sins and declared the superiority of the Gentiles over them, and consequently that they deserved salvation like them, and even performed more miracles among them, so they were very angry instead of repenting, because of their pride; and in the hardness of their hearts they led Him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, to cast Him down headlong and kill Him.

Know that "the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God" (Jas 1:20). So do not make a decision in your anger, for it is wrong however right it may seem in your sight, and accept the counsel and rebuke of others, for it may be a message from God that you may repent.
Christ did not resist them, but with all confidence left them and went His way while they were occupied with one another in their anger, and thus He escaped from evil.
Wisdom requires you to flee from useless arguments, which may develop into anger and many insults. So seek useful speech and beneficial works for the salvation of your soul and others'.

entries.section: (7) Casting out a demon in Capernaum

paragraphs.text: Jesus returned to Capernaum, which was a large city and a center for many Roman commanders, so idolatry spread in it, and corruption likewise.
The city of Capernaum is low, below sea level, while Nazareth is high on a mountain, therefore it says "came down."

Nazareth represents the pride that refuses to submit to God, while humble Capernaum accepts His word, therefore He performed many miracles in it. The meaning of the name Capernaum is the city of comfort and rest.

The sabbath days: the Jews used to gather on the Sabbath day in the synagogue to hear the readings and preaching, and Christ seized these opportunities to teach them, and when His fame spread they followed Him everywhere, so He taught them every day.

entries.section: (7) Casting out a demon in Capernaum

paragraphs.text: The teachings of Christ, and likewise His miracles, were distinguished in that He performs them with authority, and not like the prophets who ask God's power to accomplish their miracles; therefore the crowds were astonished at hearing Him and seeing His miracles in Capernaum.

entries.section: (7) Casting out a demon in Capernaum

paragraphs.text: Present in the synagogue was a man into whom a demon had entered, who could not bear the power of the teaching and was afraid of being in the presence of God, who has authority to judge the whole world, so he cried out in terror in the midst of the synagogue, declaring his weakness and fear, and bore witness to the divinity of Christ.

entries.section: (7) Casting out a demon in Capernaum

paragraphs.text: Christ refused to hear a testimony to Himself from Satan, and with authority commanded him to come out of the man, so he fell to the ground convulsing like epileptics, and the unclean spirit came out of him, and he regained his calm after the evil and tension had gone out of him. And the devil was not able to harm any member of him because of his fear of Christ. Do not accept the praise and flattery of the wicked, for it is false, and refuse dialogue with them, so that you keep your purity.

entries.section: (7) Casting out a demon in Capernaum

paragraphs.text: Those present marveled at Christ's authority over the demons, for none can do this but God, so how does this authority appear in a man living in their midst? ... But this was a motive, gradually, to their faith in the divinity of Christ.

entries.section: (7) Casting out a demon in Capernaum

paragraphs.text: The news of Christ's teachings, authority and divinity spread in all the regions around Capernaum, because, as we mentioned, it was a large city surrounded by many smaller cities.
Live uprightly with God, and be faithful in your service, confident that God's light and His work in you will affect many without your feeling it, and draw them to Christ.

entries.section: (8) The healing of Simon's wife's mother

paragraphs.text: The custom was to go to the synagogue on the Sabbath fasting, so Peter invited Christ and the disciples to eat the main meal in his house. Because of this love, Christ also gave him love, for his wife's mother had been seized with a great fever and was suffering, so the people of the house asked Him to heal her.
Show love, and you will find a greater love from God.

entries.section: (8) The healing of Simon's wife's mother

paragraphs.text: Simon's wife's mother was lying on a bed on the ground, so Jesus stood on the ground beside her, and so was higher than she, that is, above her, and commanded the disease to leave her, as He had commanded Satan in the synagogue with authority to come out of the man, and the fever left her at once, and she regained all her strength so that she was able to rise and minister to Christ and the guests who were in the house.

Simon's wife's mother signifies the human soul weakened by sin and having lost its ability for spiritual work; but if Christ comes to it and responds to the intercession of others for it, it regains its spiritual strength and even serves them. The gift of Christ and His grace are complete, more than we ask or think.

entries.section: (8) The healing of Simon's wife's mother

paragraphs.text: When the sun of the Sabbath day set, it became permitted for the Jews to travel, as the day of rest had ended. So they hastened from Capernaum and the surrounding regions to the house of Simon Peter, carrying and leading their sick with their various diseases. Christ laid His hands on them, and a power went out from Him that gave them healing. Such is Christ's love for everyone in need.

entries.section: (8) The healing of Simon's wife's mother

paragraphs.text: In addition to the sick, they brought to Him many into whom demons had entered and humiliated them, and He cast them out of them, and as they came out they cried out in shame and fear, declaring that He was the Christ, but He forbade them to continue speaking thus because:
(1) He does not need the testimony of demons.
(2) It was not the right time to reveal Himself, lest this provoke the leaders and they crucify Him before He accomplished His ministry on earth.
(3) Because He does not seek glory from men, and by this He teaches us to flee from praise.

Christ spent the night in Capernaum. And early in the morning, without the crowds' knowing, He went out to a desert place in the wilderness to pray, to teach us the importance of retreat and prayer, so that we are satisfied with God's love and do not get lost amid worldly occupations, even if it is the service of God.

When the crowds looked for Him and did not find Him, they searched until they reached Him and asked Him insistently to stay with them out of their love for Him and admiration of Him, because He had healed their diseases, and they had heard from Him very great teachings.

Despite Christ's appreciation of their love and their holding on to Him, He declared to them the necessity of preaching in the other towns, for this was His mission for which He became incarnate, to save the whole world. He made clear that He was sent from God, to confirm that He is the awaited Messiah and not a new god independent of the old, well-known God. It is good that you care for all those around you and not only the people of your household, and call them all to the love of God and His holy Mysteries.

And Christ actually began to travel about the land of Galilee, the northern part of the land of the Jews, making use of the Jews' custom of welcoming itinerant preachers, to preach in the synagogues and proclaim salvation. Miracles of healing the sick and a catch of fish
Wherever Christ moved, the crowds followed Him because of His moving teachings and His care for them in healing their diseases and freeing them from demons.
On this day He came to the lake of Gennesaret, whose meaning is "garden of delight," which is sometimes called the Sea of Galilee or the Sea of Tiberias.

It was morning, at the beginning of the day, when the fishermen had returned with their boats from fishing at night, and had washed their nets of the clinging weeds in preparation for fishing at sundown, and were about to go to their homes to rest.

There were two boats, one belonging to Simon and his brother Andrew, and the other to James and John the sons of Zebedee. Christ entered the boat of Simon Peter and asked him to thrust out a little from the land, where the crowds were pressing, and He stood teaching from the boat His moving spiritual teachings. Simon had known Him before and Christ had visited his house, but he had not yet left everything and followed Him.

God may come to you and call you to prayer, or to reading His Holy Book, or to doing some good and serving others at a time you do not expect or when you want to rest; so do not refuse, that you may enjoy God's abundant graces.

Simon and his brother Andrew were grieved because they had caught no fish that night, and consequently were in need of food for that day. After they heard Christ's teachings, their hearts were at rest, but Christ would not forget their material need, so He asked them to put the boat out into the deep of the sea.
If you give time to worship and service, be confident that God solves your material problems. Hold fast to Him and rely on Him and go deeper in knowing Him.
Christ's command was strange to Simon for two reasons:
(1) He had toiled all night and found no fish in the sea in the places he knew from his experience, and at the proper time for fishing, which is night.
(2) By experience in fishing, in the deep one does not catch with nets but with a hook some of the fish that are found on the bottom.

But his being moved by Christ's miracles and teachings made him obey Him more than his own mind and experience. May obedience rise above your mind and your feelings, for the word of God in the Holy Bible and the Church is more important than anything, so you obey it despite how hard it is for you.

When Simon obeyed, he was surprised that the net filled with a great many fish that he had not expected, and as the net was about to break because of the abundance of fish, they unloaded some of them from it into the boat, and it filled. And they called to their partners James and John, who came with their boat and filled it also. The two boats were almost sinking because of the abundance of fish, and they also drew in the net with the fish remaining in it, and with difficulty reached the shore with their great catch. Your toil alone without Christ does not benefit you, but if you obey Him in your spiritual striving, be confident of His abundant, unexpected blessing that satisfies the spirit and the body (the two boats). And if you achieve great success, thank God, the One to whom credit is due, throughout your life.
All that were with him: that is, Andrew and the hired men who helped him in fishing.

Before the power of Christ and His divinity, evident in His command to the fish and their obeying Him contrary to the laws of nature, Simon felt his weakness and sins, so he bowed down before Christ, declaring his unworthiness to have Him in his boat, and said to Him, "Depart from me," since he felt that His place is glory in heaven, and not being on earth in a lowly boat like this one.
Do God's benefactions lead you to thank Him, to humble yourself before Him and to repent of your sins?

The same awe came upon the sons of Zebedee, who were in the boat accompanying the boat of Simon and Andrew. And since Simon had qualified through obedience, repentance and confession of Christ's power, he deserved to be called by Christ to discipleship under His hands so as to serve souls. For these are the qualifications of service.

It seems that the first call of Simon and some disciples, mentioned in Jn 1:35-42), made them follow Christ at times, then return to their work, which was fishing, at other times. Christ may have allowed them to toil and catch nothing, so that they might know their weakness and their need of Him, and at the same time He worked the miracle of the great catch of fish so that they might be reassured of the ease of providing for their material needs if they followed Him.

In any case, after the call was confirmed here a second time, in which He called not only Simon but also Andrew and James and John the sons of Zebedee, as is shown by the words "they followed him," then they forsook all with faith and new obedience, and even rejoiced.

God is longsuffering with you until you trust in Him and follow Him and enjoy His blessings and His service. So do not let your material attachments, projects and responsibilities hinder you from serving God, for nothing in the world equals it. It is a clear test of the extent of your love for Him: is it more than for the world?

Leprosy (similar to what is now leprosy and vitiligo) was a contagious disease, and signifies uncleanness because it results from sin. Whoever was afflicted with it, according to the Law of Moses, was isolated outside the community and no one touched him lest he be defiled. But when this leper heard of Christ and His healing of disease, he believed and pushed through the crowds, although the leprosy, as Luke the physician states, was spread over his body, and he bowed humbly before Him and asked Christ with gentleness ("if thou wilt") and faith ("thou canst") to cleanse him.

Christ could have healed him with a word, but He touched him to show His divinity in His authority over disease and His tenderness toward the leper. At the same time He is not against the Law, for He sent him to the priest to fulfill the Law.

Offer for thy cleansing: the Law required the leper to present a sacrifice as a declaration of his repentance and his resolve not to return to sin, and as a type of the redemption of Christ, who takes away all our sins. Because Christ does not want display and fame, He told the leper to tell no one, but to fulfill the Law, which required that when a leper was healed, he go to the priest to examine him and make sure of his healing and give him a certificate of it before he mixed with anyone.
Here Christ's saying appears that He did not come to destroy but to fulfill the Law (Mt 5:17).

But when the crowds heard the news of the leper's healing, they felt that this was the Messiah, because the prophets had prophesied that among His works would be healing precisely this disease because of its difficulty, and so also Christ said in reply to the two disciples of John the Baptist who asked Him whether He was the Messiah, He told them that He cleanses lepers (Lk 7:22-23); so the crowds pressed around Christ seeking healing of their diseases.

Despite Christ's concern for healing the sick and serving the crowds, He teaches us not to be so occupied that we neglect prayer and being alone with God in quiet away from people, for this is the spiritual provision that strengthens us so that we can serve others and face the problems of life.

If you believe in God's power, which is able to solve your problems, then take refuge in Him with humility and be confident that He will remove all your troubles, and be ready to leave all your sins by repentance, and He will also support you until you are rid of them however hard they are. He loves you and has come for your salvation.

Christ entered one of the houses of Capernaum, as we know from the details of this incident mentioned in (Mt 9:2-8, Mk 2:1-12), and among those gathered around Him was a group of Pharisees, that is, the separated ones, who felt that they were the best spiritual class in Jewish society and were characterized by pride; and also a group of teachers of the Law, who were literalists in their adherence to the Law without its essence. They had come from different lands to examine Christ's teachings and judge them, so they were sitting proudly watching Him. A great number of Jews had gathered from the villages of Galilee around Capernaum, and even from the villages of Judea, which lie south of Galilee, and they brought many sick to Him and He healed them, so the people marveled at the power of God in Him.
Do you listen with humility to the teachings of the Church, or do you listen in order to judge the preacher with pride?
Let every word you hear or book you read be a spiritual message from God for you to apply in your life, and you will find the salvation of your soul.

Among the many sick who crowded around Christ, four men (as mentioned in Mt 9) came carrying a paralytic on his bed, and because of the crowd around the door they found no way to reach Christ except by going up onto the roof by the back stairs. There was an opening in the roof which they covered with wood in winter and removed in summer, so they removed these wooden boards that were among the baked bricks (the burnt bricks that cover the roof to prevent rain water from penetrating), and tied the paralytic's bed and let it down through the roof, and he came down before the Lord of glory Jesus.

How much great effort these four men spent, which declares their faith in Christ and their love for the sick man! They signify the classes of the Church coming with faith to Christ (bishops, priests, deacons, people) to find salvation in Him; or the four Evangelists, who by their Gospels carry us to faith in Christ. Show your love and faith by practical striving, and you will rejoice the heart of God and receive His blessings.

When Christ saw the practical faith of these four friends, He cared greatly for their practical intercession for their friend, so He granted him the forgiveness of his sins, which was the real cause of his illness. For He cuts off the disease from its root and origin, and this confirms His divinity and His authority to forgive sins, for none can do that but God. This does not mean that the paralytic had no faith; rather his inability to move and speak did not give him an opportunity to express his faith, but his accepting, in this bad state of health, to leave his house and enter into the crowd, and that they should take him up to the roof and tie the bed and let him down, bearing this toil and the risk of falling while being let down ... all this confirms his desire for healing and his faith.
Your enduring sufferings with contentment confirms your love and faith in God. Intercede through the saints your friends, for this rejoices God's heart and He answers their requests.
The scribes and Pharisees were vexed at Christ's words, declaring that the One who forgives sins is God alone, so how does Christ command the forgiveness of sins?
Christ knew their thoughts without their speaking them, and none knows the inner thoughts of man but God, so this is a proof of the divinity of Christ, who rebuked them for their doubts.

Christ asked the scribes and Pharisees which is easier, forgiving sins or bodily healing? .... Of course bodily healing; for Christ had done the greater, which is the forgiveness of sin, but to answer their doubts and confirm His divinity and authority, He gave healing to the paralytic with one word, to rise up and take up his bed.

God's love for you is strong and constant, and you feel it clearly in the Holy Bible, prayer and the holy Mysteries, but He confirms it to you with many gifts, that perhaps you may understand His infinite love for you.

The disease left him at once and he recovered his full health, so that he was able to take up his bed and return to his house, and as he made his way through the crowds he was thanking God and praising Him.
God's giving to us is generous, beyond what we expect or ask, therefore we ought to thank Him at all times for His gifts, and join with the Church in praising Him.
Before this great miracle, everyone marveled and glorified God, who had performed these miracles among them, bewildered at the power of the miracle and the authority of Christ.

In the place of tax collection sat Matthew the tax collector, whom Luke the Evangelist calls here by his other name, Levi, as an honor to him, to return him to his first great function, which is service; for the whole tribe of Levi was devoted to the service of the Temple. Christ called him to follow Him, so he left his job with all the material gains connected with it and his great position, and followed Christ, preferring spiritual gain to material.
In order to free time for God, you will be compelled to give up some of your comfort, your preoccupations and your material gains. Is Christ in your eyes worth this?

Since Levi (Matthew) rejoiced in following Christ, he also thought of his fellow tax collectors and his sinner friends, whom Luke here refers to as "others," and how to draw them to follow Christ. So he made a feast in his house in which he gathered all these, and invited Christ to it, confident that His teachings would surely affect them and lead them to repentance. Do you feel your responsibility toward the members of your family, your friends, your neighbors and your colleagues at work? How do you try to draw them to the love of God and attachment to Him?

The Pharisees and scribes, who were the spiritual leaders of the Jews, were vexed at Christ's mixing with sinners and said so. But because of their embarrassment to say this to Christ, they said it to His disciples, thinking only of their own appearance and people's opinion of them and not the salvation of others.
Bear the opinion of opposing people if the weak and despised need your service, as long as your aim is to offer Christ's love to all.

Christ made clear here that sin is weakness and sickness, so sinners need us to have compassion on them and treat them, and not to keep away from them. He is the true Physician who came into the world to heal all who have fallen into the sickness of sin.

But those who think in their pride that they are healthy or righteous, these have no benefit from Christ's teachings unless they first repent of their self-righteousness, and this may come if they fall into a severe temptation.
Have compassion on sinners and pray for them even if their sin is wronging you, and may you even offer them your love, which shames them and draws them to Christ.

The Jews asked Christ why His disciples did not fast, while the disciples of John and the Pharisees held to it. This was either a question of inquiry, or it shows their burden and complaint about fasting, or an objection against Christ and His disciples for their lack in this matter.

In His answer Christ gave a parable of the bridegroom and the wedding. As the people of the wedding rejoice in their bridegroom, so also Christ's disciples rejoice spiritually in beholding Him, but when the bridegroom is taken away the children of the bridechamber can fast. Likewise Christ's disciples, when He ascends to heaven, will feel their weakness and need, and will fast with asceticism and many prayers, and God will give them the knowledge of Him and the vision of Him spiritually. In application of this we keep the fast of the Apostles after the Ascension of Christ and the feast of the descent of the Holy Spirit.

Then Christ addressed the problem of the Pharisees and lawyers who held to the letter of the Law without its essence, and how their spiritual practice is not acceptable as long as their heart is not pure. He made this clear by an example, which is mending an old garment by putting a new patch on it, for this does not benefit it but harms it, because the new piece's cloth is strong while the fabric of the old is weak, so it tears when the new patch is sewn into it, and the old garment becomes worse and more torn.
Likewise, if a person's life is not renewed by repentance and faith in Christ, his spiritual practices, prayers, fasts or any spiritual work do not benefit him.

Then He confirmed the same meaning as in the previous verse with a new example, which is putting new wine into old bottles. The bottle is a vessel in which wine is put, made of goatskin, and resembles a waterskin; and when wine is left for a time in the bottle it ferments and expands, so if the bottles are old they are dry and have lost their elasticity, and then they burst and are ruined, while the wine is spilled and poured out and lost. Therefore they put new wine into new bottles, which have the elasticity and expansion if the volume of the wine inside them increases.
So also the soul renewed in Christ in a spiritual life benefits from the spiritual practices and is in harmony with them.
Purify your heart by repentance and forgive others, and you will be able to enjoy your fasting and your prayers.

He confirms here also the difficulty of renewal and change for the soul that is accustomed to the material life, in moving to repentance from sin and fellowship with God, like one who tastes new wine and says the old is better, although the old wine has a high percentage of alcohol, but habit makes him hold to it though it has a strong effect on the body. Persevere in your striving to reject the beloved sin and the old life, and force yourself in spiritual striving until you become accustomed to it and enjoy it.
The call of the Apostles and the Sermon on the Mount

entries.section: (1) Christ, the Lord of the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: The second Sabbath: most likely the Sabbath following the feast of the Passover, and it was a day of regard among the Jews.
As Christ and His disciples were passing through the fields, they were hungry, so they took some green ears of grain and rubbed them in their hands and ate.

entries.section: (1) Christ, the Lord of the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: The Pharisees objected to the disciples because they broke the laws of the Sabbath, which were laid down by the elders of the Jews and were not the original Law, since in their interpretation of the Sabbath they forbade the process of reaping and winnowing, so the Pharisees considered plucking the ears of grain a process of reaping and rubbing them a process of winnowing. From this their attempt to catch a fault and their severity in condemning Christ and His disciples appear.
Do not look for how to condemn others, but rather seek excuses for them.

entries.section: (1) Christ, the Lord of the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: Christ answered the Pharisees with an incident recorded about David their great king (1 Sam 21:1-6), how when he was hungry he and those with him were compelled to eat of the showbread, that is, the bread of the Presence, which it was not lawful to eat except for the priests, to confirm that necessity has a special status and that the Law was made for man to benefit him and not to harm him. For a person's devoting himself to spiritual work on the Sabbath day does not mean that he should fall faint with hunger when he finds no food except some ears of grain at the edges of the field, which the poor and travelers are permitted to eat.
Take care to walk by the spirit and not the letter in carrying out all the commandments, so that you may draw near to God and feel fellowship with Him.

entries.section: (1) Christ, the Lord of the Sabbath

paragraphs.text: Then He declared to them about Himself that He is the Son of Man, confirming His humanity, while He is the God who became man, the giver of the law of the Old Testament, and He is the Lord of David and the Lord of the Sabbath, who has the authority to permit in special cases small works on the Sabbath like these, as David by his authority permitted those with him to eat the showbread. This is a confirmation of His divinity and His humanity.

entries.section: (2) The healing of the withered hand

paragraphs.text: Christ continued His spiritual teachings in the synagogues of the Jews on the Sabbath days, and present was a man whose right hand was withered and dry, that is, its nerves were dead. The hand signifies movement and work, especially the right, so he is a type of the Jews' inability for spiritual work, and Christ came to heal their inability. As for the Pharisees, in their wickedness they watched Christ so as to catch a fault in Him according to their thinking, namely His healing this man on the Sabbath, on which work is forbidden, since they considered healing the practice of the work of medicine, which is forbidden to the physician on the Sabbath day.

entries.section: (2) The healing of the withered hand

paragraphs.text: Because Christ is God, He knew the thoughts of the Pharisees without their declaring them. And Christ was not afraid of their wickedness, but boldly took the initiative to do good by setting the sick man in the midst of the synagogue to show his weakness and his need of healing, but the hard hearts of the Pharisees were not moved to sympathy for him.

Do you hasten to do good however much the wicked oppose you? Be confident that good is stronger than evil, and continue in it so that you do not waste your effort in being disturbed by the evils of others or repaying their evil with evil.

entries.section: (2) The healing of the withered hand

paragraphs.text: Christ reasoned with the Pharisees to guide them to the truth, asking what is fitting for the day of the Lord in their view, which is the Sabbath: to do good, that is, healing this sick man, or to do evil, which is their malicious thinking by which they try to find an accusation against Him.

And by healing the sick man Christ means saving his soul and not only healing him, for when he is healed he believes and thanks God and begins to do good by moving his hand, but if He left him and did not heal him, he would remain in his bodily weakness and not know Christ, in whom he finds his salvation.

entries.section: (2) The healing of the withered hand

paragraphs.text: Jesus looked at them, awaiting an answer, but all were silent, unable to reply, then He commanded and the sick man was healed. This is considered a miracle of creation, for He created living nerves, and the withered hand was changed into a normal hand able to work.

entries.section: (2) The healing of the withered hand

paragraphs.text: Despite the clarity of the miracle, which calls all to glorify God, evil dominated the hearts of the Pharisees, so in ignorance they sought how to get rid of Christ.

When evil fills a person's heart it drives him to harm others, and while he thinks himself wise he is in the utmost ignorance. So if your heart is troubled and you become angry, stop to repent first before you do anything.

Christ's love of retreat and prayer appears here, for He went up the mountain alone to get away from people and enjoy prayer. As a man He needed prayer as He needed food, for He is not only God but also man at one and the same time.

His going up the mountain signifies rising above earthly things and thinking of heavenly things. The Church took the rite of keeping vigil all night from Christ, as in the Midnight Praise and the night of the Saturday of Light and in the ordination of the priestly ranks and of monks.

After praying all night, the day began and He met His disciples, who were many, and He chose from them twelve to be disciples especially His own more than the rest, and called them Apostles because He would send them into the world to preach His salvation.
Christ's concern for prayer before important works and great decisions is clear here, to be a rule for us in our lives, that we take no important decision except after a sufficient period of prayer.

The way of the call to service also appears: it must be from God Himself and not from the person himself; that is, the Church chooses her servants and no one calls himself a servant of his own accord.

It is noticeable in the calling of the Twelve that He called them two by two, and the number two shows the importance of partnership and cooperation in service. He changed the names of some of them, and in general their names have beautiful meanings, namely: James = the persevering; John = God is gracious; Andrew = the brave.
Peter = rock.

Philip = the mouth of the lamp, that is, the enlightener. Bartholomew (called Nathanael in Jn = 1), son of Harith, that is, the one who goes deep. Thomas = the twin, that is, the one who clings. Simon = the one who hears.
Matthew (called Levi) = gift.
Judas the brother of James, son of Alphaeus (also called Thaddaeus) = he who praises and gives thanks.
Iscariot = a title meaning "a man from Kerioth," the village in which Judas the traitor grew up

After appointing His disciples He came down from the mountain to a plain, which was probably the foot of the mountain; for Christ comes down to our weakness to raise us up to Himself, and around Him were three groups:
1- His disciples, including the Twelve and the rest, from whom He afterward chose seventy apostles.
2- A multitude of those who loved to hear His teachings.
3- Many of the sick and their acquaintances, and also those with unclean spirits.
It is noticeable that those gathered around Him were Jews and Gentiles (the coast of Tyre and Sidon), for Christ came for the salvation of the whole world.

And He taught them many teachings and then healed their sick. The healing of diseases was out of His tenderness and to draw them to faith. But sadly, many even until now have a utilitarian relationship with God, based on benefiting from His power in healing their diseases and meeting their needs.

May your relationship with God be built on your love and your sonship to Him, and likewise your friendship with the saints, so that you imitate them, and not merely on meeting your needs and solving your problems.

The healing of the sick took place by Christ's touching them, and a power went out and healed them; and He was not content merely to command their healing, because they are human beings and need something tangible accompanying the spiritual work. For this reason God placed for us in the Church the holy Sacraments, which are the work of the Holy Spirit under a tangible form, because we are in the body and need spiritual things through a material form.
This is the most famous of Christ's sermons, which Matthew the Evangelist mentioned in (Mt 5-7) in greater detail. Luke directs it to the disciples, but it is addressed to all the believers.

The word "blessed" means happiness or felicity. And the one who receives this happiness is the one whom people think far from it because of his weak appearance. The first of these blessed groups are the poor, whom Matthew describes as the poor in spirit, that is, the humble, and because of their humility God's mercies overflow upon them and He grants them His heavenly Kingdom, whose happiness cannot be expressed.
The hungry are those who long for righteousness and a good life; these God satisfies with the knowledge of Him and fellowship with Him, so that they are filled with every virtue.
Those who weep are those who weep over their sins, that is, the repentant; these God forgives their sins so that they receive true joy, and they laugh from their hearts, that is, they rejoice.

Enduring people's hatred, rejection, reproach and false accusation of evil against us, God rewards with heavenly joys. And we are not troubled, because in every age the devil stirs up the wicked against the children of God, as the Jews used to do with the prophets of God in the Old Testament, beating them and reviling them and even killing them. Humble yourself, remembering your sins in repentance, and your longings for God will be stirred, and then you will make light of every pain for His sake, looking to the glories of eternity, confident of His help and His consolation of your heart.

What is meant here are the rich who rely on their wealth and are attached to it, for they have received their pleasure in these passing material things, and have no share in the glories of heaven because they neglected them.

Those immersed in the lusts of the world will hunger in eternity for the enjoyment of God and will not find it. And those who play in the laughter and mockery of this world, reckless and plunged in sins, will regret in the end when they are cast into Hell with unending sorrow.

After speaking in the preceding woes to the crowds, which include the Pharisees and all those far from the knowledge of God, He directs His speech here to His disciples and all who believe in Him, warning them of the sin of loving praise, because it necessarily requires hypocrisy to please everyone and obtain their praise, as the false prophets in the Old Testament gave false reports according to the wish of the hearers in order to obtain their praise and gifts.
May you have a pure conscience, so that you declare the voice of God to those around you, seeking the glory of God and not your personal comfort.

Christ presents the essential characteristic of Christians, which is love for everyone, even enemies and those who wrong us. It is not limited to a heart open to others, but goes beyond it to positive acts, whether before God, such as prayer, or before enemies, such as blessing them with kind words, or offering them deeds of goodness and kindness. For we feel that the one who hates us is a beloved brother who has been subjected to pressures from the devil, and by our love we help him, and he returns to his natural state, that is, he loves us.
Have compassion on the one who wrongs you, and offer him love, even if at the very least a prayer for him.

Christ presents practical examples of love for those who wrong us, such as forgiveness and enduring insults from one who assaults us with blows and insult. Then giving to the one who seizes our money, so we do not limit ourselves to leaving what he seized but also give him more love, such as giving the coat and not only leaving the cloak that was seized. In sum: considering everyone to be in need and giving to all, for the extortioner and the enemy need our love, and we give him more than he asks because we are not attached to material things, and we care about winning souls by love.
To make it easier for the hearers, who felt the difficulty of this love, He said to them: you wish that people would treat you with self-giving love, so take the initiative with it toward them.
Think, in every dealing with others, if you were in their place, how would you want them to treat you?

Christ presents here a truth, which is that the natural thing is for a person to love his friends and loved ones who love him, and this is also what sinners do. And lending to others and getting everything back from them is also a matter that does not exceed natural human dealing, but Christ presents true love, which is higher than human love ... love of enemies and those who wrong us, and by this we prove that we are children of God, who is love.

If we are children of God in love, we imitate Him in His kindness and mercy toward those who murmur against Him. So we offer mercy to all like God our Father, and look with a spirit of fatherhood and motherhood at all around us however much they are against us. Meditate on God's mercy to you in your past life, and this will drive you to do mercy with everyone.

Christ encourages us to love by the blessings that we receive from it: if we forgive others and pardon them, God will forgive us, and if we give material and spiritual gifts, God will give us more. He compares God's overflowing gifts to the measure of grain that was used in ancient times, and this measure is characterized by being good, with no excess at its bottom so that it holds as much as possible, and pressed down, that is, the grains are pressed within it so that the greatest amount is put in it, and likewise shaken together to fill all the inner gaps, and running over, that is, if any amount is put on it, it falls off because it is completely full. Then the person receives these grains in his garment, so that they come into his bosom. To the extent that we give generously, God gives us even more generously.

And on the other side, if we wrong others by condemning and judging them, we shall also be condemned and judged. Your giving to others shows the extent of your love for them and your detachment from love of material things and your appreciation of God's love for you, and these three drive you to generous giving. And if you possess love and giving, you will keep away from condemning even if you notice the faults of others; you will look for what you can offer them.

He continues His warning to us against judging, alerting us to the multitude of our sins that blind our sight. And while we are blind, trying to judge others and lead them on the way of life, we have nothing before us but that we and they fall into the pit of problems and greater errors.

On the other hand, we ought to imitate our good teacher Jesus Christ, who went about doing good and did not condemn others, even the woman caught in adultery He did not condemn. And the perfection we strive for is to imitate Christ our teacher in love and in not judging.

And in mockery of the one who judges, Christ makes clear that the sin of any person is like a mote or a small straw, but the sin of judging is like a beam. And He asks whether it is possible for a person with a beam in his eye to take a mote out of his brother's eye? ... Of course not, but wisdom says: let me first cast the beam out of my own eye, by repenting of judging, and let love take its place, by which I help others to be rid of their sins, that is, the mote in their eye.

At the end of Christ's sermon, He stressed the importance of carrying out His commandments and not merely hearing them, or speaking with Him with many requests such as the healing of diseases and the casting out of demons. For practical love is the foundation on which the whole of life is built, and it is what confirms our sonship to God and our conviction of His word.

He gives a practical comparison, which is that a man dug until he reached the rock, and laid the foundation on it and raised a building, so that it is strong. And another building was raised on the earth, which is sand or weak dust easily moved, so when the winds blew and the water of the river rushed like a flood and struck these two houses, the building on the rock was not affected, but the building without a foundation on the earth collapsed and fell. Likewise whoever carries out God's commandments and lives practically by love will not be shaken by the winds of trials and the devil's wars, but the other falls into sins and his end is eternal destruction.

Let love be in your heart before you speak or do anything, for it is the only aim in our relationship with others, that we may win their souls for Christ, because God is love and on Him we build all our actions.
The centurion's servant, the son of the widow of Nain, the talk about the Baptist, the sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

entries.section: (1) The healing of the centurion's servant

paragraphs.text: After Christ finished His teaching on the plain, He entered the city of Capernaum, one of the largest towns of Galilee, north of the land of the Jews, in order to show the practical application of His commandments about love and compassion toward others.

entries.section: (1) The healing of the centurion's servant

paragraphs.text: The centurion: a rank in the Roman army, the one responsible for commanding a hundred soldiers. He had a servant who was struck by a severe illness that nearly cost him his life; Matthew mentions that he was palsied, that is, paralyzed. The centurion was distinguished by his love for his servants. Here St. Luke addresses the problem of slavery that prevailed at that time, in which domination and cruelty appeared. Here, however, he declares to us the ideal situation in the love of a master for his servants, as the love of the head of a household for his servants, or of a superior for those under him, ought to be: a love that shows itself in a special care no less than a father's love for his children.

The Gentile centurion asks Christ to heal his servant, and we shall see Christ's welcome of this, and even His praise of the Gentiles because they are His children. St. Luke took an interest in this story because he writes to the Gentiles.

entries.section: (1) The healing of the centurion's servant

paragraphs.text: The centurion felt unworthy to meet Christ because he was a Gentile, so he sent the elders of the Jews, that is, their leaders, to intercede for him before Christ so that his servant might be healed.

Here the importance of intercession appears, and it carries within it the humility of the one who seeks intercession, which gladdens the heart of God. The faith of this centurion in the power of Christ to heal also appears. The centurion's love for his servant is shown as well by his sending the elders of the Jews to Christ.

entries.section: (1) The healing of the centurion's servant

paragraphs.text: The elders of the Jews interceded before Christ, beseeching Him to come and heal the servant, although the centurion had not asked them for Christ to come, but only for the servant to be healed. They showed that this centurion was worthy to receive the blessing of his servant's healing from the hand of Christ, because his heart was full of love, not only for pagans like himself but for the Jews also; for he had built them a synagogue in Capernaum for the reading of the Holy Scriptures, spiritual sermons and prayers.
Love gives you grace in the eyes of all and opens closed doors for you, so help those around you as much as you can.

entries.section: (1) The healing of the centurion's servant

paragraphs.text: Christ went with the elders of the Jews toward the centurion's house. When He drew near and the centurion learned of it, he sent his friends to Christ to make clear his request. He did not mean for Christ to come to him, because he was not worthy of that, and because he knew that the Law of the Jews decrees that a Jew who enters the house of a Gentile is defiled until the evening. So he only begs that Christ command, and the servant will be healed.

Here the difference between the faith of the centurion and the faith of the elders becomes clear: he trusts that the word of Christ is sufficient for healing, whereas the elders believed that the touch of Christ's hand heals. The Gospel of Matthew mentions that the centurion met Christ (but it means that his friends met Christ), for they represent him and speak his words.

entries.section: (1) The healing of the centurion's servant

paragraphs.text: The centurion explains his faith that the word of Christ is sufficient for healing, because by virtue of his position he knows that his commands are sufficient to move the soldiers under him so that they carry out the work required of them. Therefore he believed that Christ is able, by His authority, to command the sickness and it will depart from his servant, and this is a clear faith in the divinity of Christ.

entries.section: (1) The healing of the centurion's servant

paragraphs.text: Christ glorified the faith of this centurion and esteemed it above the faith of the Jews themselves, to whom He was sent, and this glorification proclaims Christ's love and His concern for the salvation of the whole world. And He commanded the servant's healing, as is understood from the following verse.

entries.section: (1) The healing of the centurion's servant

paragraphs.text: The centurion's friends, together with the elders of the Jews, returned to the house after Christ had departed, and found the servant, who had been about to die, restored to health, and they rejoiced at the work of God.

entries.section: (2) The raising of the son of the widow of Nain

paragraphs.text: After the healing of the centurion's servant, which signifies care for the salvation of the Gentiles and love for strangers, Christ moved from Capernaum toward the village of Nain, which is 25 miles from it, and with Him were a large number of His disciples and the crowds who loved to hear His teaching. God's purpose in taking this crowd along was to show them a great miracle to confirm their faith, namely, the raising of a dead man.

entries.section: (2) The raising of the son of the widow of Nain

paragraphs.text: The Jews were accustomed to bury their dead outside the cities, so as not to catch diseases and not to be defiled by them. An only son of his mother, who was a widow, had died, and her grief was intense, because after losing her provider, who was her husband, her hope, who was her son, had died also. Hearts sympathized with her, and a large number from the city went out to comfort and support her. She is a symbol of the soul that has lost its Bridegroom, who is God, and then lost its life and itself, which is its only son. So Christ's concern for her is concern for the weak soul that has no support or hope.

entries.section: (2) The raising of the son of the widow of Nain

paragraphs.text: Christ showed His tenderness to this woman with words that reassured her so that she would not weep, but He was not content with words, as human beings are; He accompanied them with a positive deed, raising the dead man.
Try to join your kind words with deeds by which you help others in their needs and troubles.

entries.section: (2) The raising of the son of the widow of Nain

paragraphs.text: Because of Christ's majesty when He touched the bier, the bearers stood still, understanding that He wanted something. Then, by the authority of His divinity, He commanded the dead young man to rise. For He is the Resurrection and the Life, who is able to grant salvation and life to everyone over whom sin has gained mastery and who has lost the ability to live the spiritual life. And because the woman was very weak and the young man was dead and unable to ask anything of God, Christ took the initiative and performed the miracle without anyone asking Him.
Be confident that God loves you and meets your needs even if you do not ask Him, how much more if you ask Him and persist in asking.

entries.section: (2) The raising of the son of the widow of Nain

paragraphs.text: The dead man rose and sat up, and showed that he had regained his life by speaking with the crowd, and perhaps he thanked Christ and glorified God. Everyone was amazed at what happened, including his mother, so Christ helped her by bringing the young man to her embrace. For He is God, who alone is able to restore life to every grieving and despairing soul like this woman.

entries.section: (2) The raising of the son of the widow of Nain

paragraphs.text: From the power of the miracle, the crowds felt the fear of God, and remembered the prophets Elijah and Elisha, who raised the dead, so they glorified God, seeing in Christ a prophet like the prophets of old; yet Christ commanded the young man by the authority of His divinity and he rose at once, whereas the prophets asked God and so raised the dead.

entries.section: (2) The raising of the son of the widow of Nain

paragraphs.text: Because of the greatness of the miracle, news of it spread throughout all the surrounding land of Judea.

entries.section: (3) Christ's discourse about John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: John spoke with his disciples about Christ, His works and His teachings, to bind them to His love. Then he asked them whether He might be the Christ who was awaited, and they did not know the answer. So he said to them, Let us send two of you to ask Him plainly whether He is the Messiah. Two went to Christ and asked Him as John had commanded them. John was certain that He was the Christ, for the Holy Spirit had revealed it to him at His baptism, but he intended to declare this to his disciples so that they would follow Christ. This shows the humility of the Baptist and his emptying of himself.
Would you accept that another be honored and you not be honored? And do you seek to put others forward in honor in your place?

entries.section: (3) Christ's discourse about John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: When the two disciples reached Christ, they saw Him healing many of the sick (infirmities = diseases or defects) and casting out demons, and they heard from the crowds the reports of His miracles, such as the raising of the son of the widow of Nain. When they asked Jesus, He did not first answer them with a yes, but offered clear proof that He is the Messiah through the miraculous works that He does, which the prophets had foretold that the Messiah would do: healing the sick, raising the dead, and preaching to the poor the salvation that the Messiah would bring.

entries.section: (3) Christ's discourse about John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: Christ warned the two disciples and all who heard, lest they doubt Him because of His being in the flesh or His coming sufferings and death. For He is God, able to do all things, as His miracles prove, and if He humbly bears being in the flesh, and His sufferings and death, it is for the sake of the salvation of mankind.

entries.section: (3) Christ's discourse about John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: After John's two disciples departed, having become sure from His many miracles that this was the awaited Messiah, Christ seized the opportunity and began to speak to the crowds about John the Baptist. He asked them about his person and his standing, and imagined with the crowds, as they went out to the wilderness, that they would find some reeds of the wild cane swaying with the winds. He asked whether John was merely an ordinary person living in the wilderness like one reed among the wild reeds, and so He denies of John this comparison, that of a reed shaken by the wind, for he is not a man wavering in his thoughts and principles, but strong and steadfast.

Then Christ asks about John again, when the crowds went out to the wilderness: was it, one wonders, to see a man living in luxury, occupied with the delights of life, which He indicates by soft raiment? .. And Christ strongly denies this, for those who live delicately dwell in the palaces of kings which are in the cities, not in the austerity of the wilderness, thereby showing the Baptist's asceticism. Then He asks a third time about John, the distinguished man who lives in the asceticism of the wilderness: is he a prophet because of his powerful teaching and his self-denial? .. And Christ answers, saying that he is greater than the ordinary prophets known among the Jews.

Do not be merely a person living in the world, eating and drinking and doing the material worldly works, moved by the currents of the world. Rather, you are the light of the world and the salt of the earth ... an image of Christ in all your words and works.

entries.section: (3) Christ's discourse about John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: Christ refers to the prophecy of Malachi 3:1), (which spoke of John as an angel, that is, a messenger who prepares the way for the proclamation of Christ and His redemption.

entries.section: (3) Christ's discourse about John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: Christ declares that the Baptist is not only a great prophet but the greatest of the men of the Old Testament. Then He adds a new truth, namely the loftiness of the grace of the New Testament above life under the Law in the Old Testament, since Christians in the Church receive the Holy Sacraments and the Holy Spirit also works in the means of grace to a greater degree than the sons of the Old Testament longed to see and behold these glories. So the least believer in the Church has God reigning over his heart and delighting him with His grace more greatly than what the sons of the Old Testament received, including John the Baptist.
There is another opinion, that the one meant by the least is Christ, who is younger than John by six months, and yet He is greater than John and than all mankind.

entries.section: (3) Christ's discourse about John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: Then Christ speaks of the Baptist's popularity, and refers to it as all the people, that is, people generally, and even the greatest sinners such as the tax collectors, who declared their repentance, glorifying the righteous and holy God and their need for the baptism of repentance which they received from the hand of John.

entries.section: (3) Christ's discourse about John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: Sadly, none departed from the consensus of the people except the leaders of Jewish religious thought, namely the Pharisees and the lawyers, who held to the Law literally. They became proud and boasted of their knowledge and their literal fulfillment of the Law, and so rejected repentance and the baptism of John, that is, the voice of God and His counsel which He had sent to them by the mouth of the Baptist.

entries.section: (3) Christ's discourse about John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: The Pharisees rejected repentance and the baptism of John, and likewise the teachings of Christ, so Jesus gave them an illustrative parable to show them the hideousness of their rejection and the ignorance into which they fall. It is as though children were playing in the town market-place and divided themselves into two groups, one of which sang in the hope that the other would rejoice and dance, but it was not moved; then the same group tried to mourn so that the other group would weep, and again it was not moved, that is, it refused to respond to joy or to sorrow. What is meant here by the songs is the joyful spiritual teachings, that is, the good news of the New Testament that Christ brought, over which hearts should dance with joy in a spiritual dance and not a bodily one; as for the mourning, it is the Baptist's stern teachings which call people to repentance and to weeping over their sins.

entries.section: (3) Christ's discourse about John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: The Jews rejected the teachings of John the Baptist and considered him wicked, having a devil, because of his severe asceticism, although he lived a life of austerity in order to proclaim the vanity of the world and the importance of repentance and of life with God.

entries.section: (3) Christ's discourse about John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: On the contrary, Christ lived in the city, eating and drinking like the others around Him, and lived in righteousness an ordinary life like ordinary human beings, to make the possibility of the spiritual life easy for them, and He mingled with everyone, even sinners and tax collectors. So the Pharisees rejected His teachings also, because of His lack of asceticism, and they even insulted Him and described Him as a lover of food and drink, who loves to mingle with sinners because He is a sinner.

entries.section: (3) Christ's discourse about John the Baptist

paragraphs.text: As for true Wisdom, that is, the hypostasis of the incarnate Word, He was glorified and justified only by those who repented through John's baptism and those who believed in Christ, for the children of Wisdom are the children of God who believe in Him. Do not hasten to condemn, but give heed to the voice of God which you hear and learn from others, however different their personalities may be.

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: Because of the importance of this passage, the Church places it in her daily prayer, in the Second Watch of the Midnight Prayer in the Agpeya, for the deep spiritual meanings needed by everyone who keeps vigil and cares for his spiritual life. The Pharisees' hostility to Christ had not yet increased at the beginning of His ministry, so this Pharisee thought to become acquainted with His person, and therefore invited Him to a feast in his house; and Christ did not refuse, but seized it as an opportunity for service and preaching.

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: This woman was famous for her sin, which was probably adultery, and she came without invitation to the Pharisee's house to offer her love to Christ, of whom she had heard, and she may have seen and heard Him before, and she brought with her a flask of sweet perfume. She is, of course, not Mary the sister of Lazarus, who poured the ointment on Christ in Bethany near Jerusalem, because the place here is in Galilee and the woman here is a sinner, and those present objected to her approaching Christ because of her sin, whereas those present objected to Mary the sister of Lazarus because of the high value of the ointment and the poor's having a greater claim to it than Christ. And here it is in the house of Simon the Pharisee, whereas the other was in the house of Simon the leper (Mt 26:6-13; Mk 14:3-5; Jn 12:3-8).

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: At feasts the Jews were accustomed to have each person sit on a couch or sofa (a bench or a divan) while they ate at the table, so these couches were placed around the table and a person reclined, leaning on the elbow of his left arm on the table with his head resting on his left hand, and ate with his right hand, while his legs stretched out in front of him on the couch, and since he bent his knees, his feet were behind him and not in the direction of the table. So when this woman entered, she went toward Christ and stood before His feet, then knelt and began to weep in repentance for her many sins, feeling unworthy to draw near to Christ the Righteous, and with the abundance of her tears she wet His feet. Here she is a symbol of the repentant soul, which wants to know the way of the new life through the footsteps of Christ, and even wants Him to enter and walk within her heart, and when He is soiled with the filth of her sins, she offers the tears of her repentance so that God may accept her and remove from her all her evils.
These tears point to the water of Baptism, which washes away all of man's defilement, and to the tears of repentance in the sacrament of confession, which remove sin.

And the woman found nothing more precious than the crown of her head, that is, her hair, with which to wipe the feet of Christ, declaring her lowliness and humility before Him; her crown is the feet of Christ.

And the longings of her love stirred toward Christ, whose love, forgiveness and tenderness she trusts, so she began to kiss His feet. She also expressed her love by pouring the perfume on His feet and anointing them with it, since she did not feel worthy to pour it on His head, as was the custom of the Jews in welcoming their guests, but with humility she anointed His feet with it.

If you offer your repentance with humility, faith and love, you receive the forgiveness of your sins, and even Christ's honoring of you. Examine yourself every day about your sins, so that you may return in humble repentance, and the feelings of your love toward God may be stirred, and you may receive His mercies.

When the Pharisee saw this sinful woman touching Christ, who was probably an adulteress as we mentioned, because her sin was known in the city, and found no objection from Christ, although this is contrary to the Law and to the prevailing custom that the righteous keep away from the wicked, he said within himself that Christ was an ordinary person, because if He were a prophet He would know that she was a sinner and would refuse to let her touch Him, forgetting a more important matter, namely that the awaited Messiah would come to save sinners and not to keep them away from Him, and that sinners, if they repent and touch Him, are cleansed of their uncleanness.
Do not be hasty in judging others, and lift up your heart in a short prayer that God may guide you, so that you may see all sides of the matter and the truth may be revealed to you.

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: Christ knew what was in Simon's mind, and this proves His divinity, but He did not embarrass him by declaring what was in his mind; rather, with gentleness He asked his permission to say something to him, that is, to make clear to him his error, but through a practical parable that brings the spiritual idea near to his understanding.
If others wrong you, do not be angry, but with gentleness you can persuade them and win them.

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: The creditor is God, and the two debtors, one of whom owed ten times the other, and by the one with the great debt is meant the sinful woman because of her many sins known in the city, while the one with the small debt is Simon the Pharisee, because he held to the Law but fell into pride, condemnation and failure in the duties of hospitality.

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: When the owner of the money found that the debtors were unable to pay their debts, he forgave them both out of love, for all human beings are unable to pay their debts toward God because everyone has fallen into sin. Then Christ asked Simon: Which of the debtors, do you think, loves and feels the love of the owner of the money more than the other?

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: Simon gave an answer, namely that the one with the greater debt would feel the forgiveness and love of the owner of the money more than the other, and so would love him for his great kindness to him. And Christ commended his answer.

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: After the introductory parable, Christ made a comparison between the love of the Pharisee and the love of the sinful woman for Christ, to show her greatness and distinction. So He said to Simon that among the duties of hospitality is the washing of the guest's feet, because walking in open shoes, that is, sandals, on dusty ground must make the feet dirty, so the first thing the guest needs is to have his feet washed. But Simon did not do this, whereas the woman washed Christ's feet, not with water but with something greater, namely the tears of her repentance, and wiped them not with an ordinary towel but with the crown of her head, which is her hair. She made up for the Pharisee's lack and shortcoming in the duties of hospitality by her distinguished love.

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: Among the duties of hospitality is showing love by kissing the guest on his head or cheek, and in this too Simon fell short, and this woman made up for it with great humility by kissing the feet of Christ, not only one kiss but many kisses declaring her love and longings.

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: Among the duties of hospitality also is anointing the guest's head with oil, that is, fragrant perfume, which refreshes him, and this too Simon did not do, and this woman did it, pouring the perfume on the feet of Christ with humility. The most precious thing she had she offers at His feet, because she feels unworthy to place it on His head as is customary.

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: Because of this distinguished love of the sinful woman, God granted her great forgiveness that removes her many sins. But as for one whose love is little like Simon, who confined himself to giving a feast for Christ and whose pride hindered him from believing in Him, only a little of his sins will be forgiven.

God values your love even if it is little like Simon's, and He is ready to bless your life and your house by entering them. But if you have great love like the sinful woman, then whatever your sins, they will all be forgiven. For Simon was not justified from his sins, but merely received a blessing from Christ, whereas the woman received complete forgiveness and glorification from Christ.

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: Christ declared, by the authority of His divinity, the forgiveness of all this woman's sins, so that afterward she would be famous in the city and all the world not for her sins but for her great love by which she received complete forgiveness.

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: Those reclining at table, who were Pharisees and friends of Simon, objected with pride to Christ's forgiveness of the woman, despising His words, because the one who has authority to forgive is God alone, whereas Jesus in their eyes was merely an ordinary man and not even a prophet. Their pride prevented them from understanding the parable of the debtors and what Christ showed of this woman's love for Him.
Beware of pride, for it blinds the heart, so that a person is unable to understand God's words and His guidance sent through those around him.

entries.section: (4) The sinful woman in the Pharisee's house

paragraphs.text: Since the Pharisees did not understand, Christ blessed the woman, declaring the greatness of her faith, which the Pharisees were unable to attain, and which appeared in practice in the tears of her repentance and humility at His feet, and in her love in the perfume she poured out, so she received forgiveness and salvation, and deserved to have her heart filled with peace with which to go on and complete her life. It is practical faith, joined to repentance, humility and love, that saves you, and not merely theoretical faith, which the demons share with you.
The parable of the sower. The rebuking of the winds. The demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes. The woman with the issue of blood

After Christ left the house of Simon the Pharisee, He began His second preaching tour in Galilee, in the early part of the second year of His ministry. He called people to repentance so that God might reign over their hearts, whether in the cities or the villages, caring for the rich and the poor, and His twelve disciples accompanied Him so that they might learn from His words and conduct and then preach in the same manner afterward when He commissioned them to do so; that is, it was an opportunity for them for spiritual discipleship.

Here Christ's care for women appears, for He allowed them to follow Him and hear His teaching, contrary to the custom of the Jews, which diminished their worth and did not give them an opportunity like that of a man; among the Gentiles also the status of woman was lower than that of man.

Among these women who loved Him because of their healing from diseases or evil spirits was Mary Magdalene (Magdala is a village on the Sea of Tiberias), who suffered from the domination of seven demons over her, and Christ cast them out of her and healed her, so she followed Him to the Cross and the burial, and was the first to visit His tomb at the dawn of the Resurrection, and He appeared to her, and she remained with the disciples and the believers until the end of her life.

As for Joanna, she seems to have been a rich woman who followed Christ until His burial, and carried spices to lay on His body. Some think that Chuza her husband was the king's officer whose son Christ healed, and so he and all his household followed Christ.

Then He mentions Susanna and others whose love was shown in providing money for the needs of Christ and His disciples. From this the humility of Christ appears, for He feeds the multitudes with five loaves, yet He needs food from the gifts of men, and is not troubled that some women spend on Him. This also shows Christ's concern for the service of women in the Church in what is suitable for them.
Accept with humility the love and service of others toward you, and even thank them for it, for this does not diminish your worth but adorns you with virtues.

Christ spoke in parables to bring the meaning near to the minds and hearts of the hearers, who were awaiting the Messiah as an earthly savior and material leader and not a Savior of their spirits; for this reason He used material parables so that through them they might understand His spiritual teachings.

This parable was explained earlier in (Mt 13:3-23; Mk 4:3-20), and one may refer to them. It appears in the parable that as the sower was moving toward the good ground, some of his seed fell by the way side, and the feet of people trampled it and the birds of the air ate the rest. Some other fell on ground full of stones with thin, shallow soil, and the seeds that sprang up found no moisture for their roots to absorb, so they withered away. Some seeds fell on ground full of thorns, and they sprang up with the good plants and choked them, shading them and absorbing the nourishment from the soil around their roots; but the seeds sown in the good ground produced perfect fruit, expressed as a hundredfold, because a hundred represents perfection. This parable is clear and easy to understand for whoever wants to hear the word of God.

Christ made clear the reason for His use of parables, which is that perhaps by this He may break into the hard hearts that hear Him and see and yet do not want to believe in Him and understand His words. But to the simple disciples who believe in Him, He explains the parable and offers direct spiritual teaching, that is, the mysteries of life with God, and how we give Him an opportunity to reign over hearts.

The interpretation of the parable is that God is the sower, and the seed is His word, which He wants to give to all even if He knows by His foreknowledge that they will refuse. So He offered the seed to the people who are like the way side, that is, those who do not open their hearts to receive His word, so the devil takes away the word and tramples it, and they gain nothing from it. The second class of people, represented by the rocky ground, receive the word but do not strive deeply to carry it out, so they leave God in the hour of temptation and fall back from Him to the world and its lusts. The third kind of people are those absorbed in their lusts, so even if they hear the word of God it does not affect them, because their lusts cover and choke the word. The last kind are the believers who understand the word of God and strive to carry it out with perseverance, and so they bring forth good fruit of spiritual virtues.
