I wish you would regard the words of God that you read every day in the Holy Bible as a personal message to you from God, so that you respond to it and carry it out.

If a person wants to dispel the darkness of a place by lighting a lamp, it is unreasonable for him to cover it with a vessel that hides its light, or to put it under a bed so that its light does not appear; on the contrary, he puts it in a high place like a lampstand so that it gives light to the whole house or place.

What is meant by the light is the work of the word of God in us, so that the warmth of the Spirit within us appears in good works that draw many to love Christ. It is unreasonable to hide the light with a vessel placed over it, which is a symbol of the lusts of the world and the love of acquiring various material things that quench the warmth of the Spirit, or to put the light under the bed, which points to slackness, negligence and laziness; on the contrary, it is put in a high place, that is, we lift our lives above earthly things, so that we give light to all who are in the house, that is, the Church, and even to the whole world in which we live.
Consider what weakens you after you have been moved by the word of God or have made promises for the new life ... try to rid yourself of these hindrances and rise above them by giving them up.

This saying is also mentioned in (ch. 12:2; Mt 10:6). The "hid" thing is the word of God, which must be made known to all people; if you hide it by your sins, it will appear in the lives of others and reach you, but you will lose the grace of its being manifested in your own life. This saying is followed by the parable of the sower so that Christ may stress the necessity for those who believe in Him to apply His word in their lives, so that it appears spontaneously and affects those around them, and they do not hide His word as information inside them, but apply it and so receive the blessing of carrying it out, and others also are evangelized through them by His word.

Beware of hypocrisy, by which you hide some things within you and show the opposite, for the matter will be uncovered in spite of you with time and will appear for what it is, and you will be judged by God and men.

Christ stresses an important principle, namely that whoever is ready to obey God and strives in spiritual striving will be given more abundant blessings and his light will increase, so that he is satisfied and draws many to God. But whoever has no faith and spiritual striving, that is, does not apply the word of God in his life, the gifts of God to him, which in his pride he thinks are his own possession, will be taken from him and he will fall into doubts, because his knowledge is merely theoretical knowledge about God.
His mother is the Virgin Mary.
His brethren are the sons of His mother's sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas or Alphaeus. In Jewish custom the sons of an aunt are regarded as brothers.
These reached the place where Jesus was sitting, and could not enter to Him because of the crowd surrounding Him, so they stood outside.

Those around Him told Him that His mother and His brethren wanted to see Him, and this was a good intention on their part, and Christ rejoices in His relatives, and He cared for His mother even while on the Cross, but He wanted to raise everyone to the level of kinship with Him as His mother and brethren. How?
Christ declared that whoever hears His word and carries it out in his life has been raised to the level of kinship with Christ, and hearing alone is not enough but doing also.

It is to be noted here that after the parable of the sower, He stressed the importance of applying the word of God in the parable of the lamp, and then stressed it a second time when His mother and His brethren visited Him.

The humility of God calls you to be a brother to Him by keeping His commandments, for the word of God brings you near to Him so that you may enjoy fellowship with Him. So be diligent in reading the Holy Bible every day.

entries.section: (5) The rebuking of the winds and the waves

paragraphs.text: Christ left the crowd and His relatives, and got into the ship with His disciples to cross from the western shore of the Sea of Tiberias to the eastern shore.
This is a symbol of Christ's bringing those who believe in Him across from darkness to light by means of His Cross or His Church, which is symbolized by the ship.

entries.section: (5) The rebuking of the winds and the waves

paragraphs.text: A storm of wind means violent winds, because the surface of the lake is 600 feet below the surface of the Mediterranean Sea, and the land surrounding it is high, so the air coming from beyond the hills around the lake is violent and stirs up the waters so that its waves rise.

It is mentioned here for the first time that Christ slept, to confirm His humanity. His sleep is a symbol of His rest in the hearts of His children and servants. The ship was exposed to violent winds that raised the waves, and they struck the ship and even the water entered it, and it was in danger of sinking, and consequently of the destruction of all who were in it.

The affliction may grow more intense while God is long-suffering, not out of neglect on His part or lack of feeling for you, but that in the end He may be glorified by a great miracle that shows His love for you.

entries.section: (5) The rebuking of the winds and the waves

paragraphs.text: The disciples used all their experience in steering ships and failed, and finally they had recourse to Christ in great agitation, declaring their helplessness and even their exposure to death. Then Christ arose and commanded the winds and the waves to be calm, and they obeyed at once, and this proves His divinity and His authority over nature.
The reason for the delay in solving the problem may be your not having recourse to God.

entries.section: (5) The rebuking of the winds and the waves

paragraphs.text: After Christ solved the problem, He reproved them for the weakness of their faith in Him and the delay of their recourse to Him, while to the disciples His authority and divinity became plainly evident, and they marvelled greatly at His power.
Help others first, then reprove them and guide them.

entries.section: (6) The demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes

paragraphs.text: The country of the Gadarenes is one of the ten cities in Galilee, in which many Gentiles lived with the Jews; they are cities in the north of Judea at the Sea of Galilee, and this city is about 30 miles south-east of the Sea of Galilee.

entries.section: (6) The demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes

paragraphs.text: St. Luke describes to us here the wretched state of a man in whom demons had dwelt for many years, so that they robbed him of his mind, stripped him of his clothes and drove him from living among people, so that he lived in the tombs. He is a symbol of mankind far from God, which has been stripped of the garments of righteousness and has lost its humanity and its love for people, and has even become dead while alive, since it dwells among the dead in the tombs; and this man left the tombs and came toward the city by the providence of God to meet Christ.

Consider what sin does to you, and how it makes you lose your loftiness as a human being and your love for those around you, and makes you like one dead in the sight of God, so that you may reject it by repentance and confession.

entries.section: (6) The demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes

paragraphs.text: Despite the harshness and violence of the demons, they submitted in weakness and fear before Christ when this man worshipped Him, and the demons asked Christ not to torment them, since their rest is in tormenting human beings and their torment is the salvation of people from them.

entries.section: (6) The demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes

paragraphs.text: Christ commanded the demons to come out of this tormented man whom they had deprived of living among people, and all human attempts to bind him, even with chains, had failed, for he would break them by the power of the demons within him and flee to the desert. For demons are not resisted by human thoughts and works but by prayer and the power of Christ.

entries.section: (6) The demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes

paragraphs.text: Legion is the name of the largest division in the Roman army system, numbering from 3,000 to 6,000 soldiers.
St. Mark mentioned in his Gospel that the number of the demons in this man was two thousand, and the demons' answer to Christ means that they were a very great number.

entries.section: (6) The demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes

paragraphs.text: The demons know that their end is eternal torment, and they also know Christ's authority over them, so they begged Him not to send them into the abyss, the place where the wicked wait until the Day of Judgment, when they will be cast into eternal torment.

entries.section: (6) The demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes

paragraphs.text: There was a great herd of swine feeding in the mountains around the city, and this is contrary to the Jewish Law, which commands not to raise or eat swine, because they are a symbol of uncleanness and evil, since the swine wallows in dust and filth (in the New Testament, now that we have been taught the spiritual meaning, eating swine is no longer forbidden, but is ordinary food that God created for it). So the demons asked Christ to allow them to enter the swine, and they rushed down into the lake and were drowned, choked. Christ permitted this to declare His anger at disobedience to His law.

entries.section: (6) The demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes

paragraphs.text: When the herdsmen saw their swine drowned, they were afraid and hurried to tell the people in the city of the Gadarenes and the surrounding area, and they all went out to see Christ, and found the one who had been mad and naked in the tombs clothed and seated, learning at His feet.

Thus grace restored his mind to the madman, and he settled in humility, loving spiritual discipleship in the teachings of Christ. And they were very afraid at the greatness of the miracle, because everyone knew the problem of this madman.

entries.section: (6) The demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes

paragraphs.text: The people of the city heard from those who had seen the miracle its details, which showed the power and authority of Christ, and sadly they did not believe in Him but feared Him and asked Him to depart from their city, so He got into the ship and went away. Thus we find that fear deprives a person of enjoying fellowship with God: at the very time when the one who had been mad enjoyed fellowship with Christ by submitting at His feet, fear deprived the people of his city of this because of their unbelief.

entries.section: (6) The demoniac of the country of the Gadarenes

paragraphs.text: Since the state of this wretched man had changed to joy after he came to know Christ, and he saw the ignorance of the people of his city in sending Christ away, he begged Him to let him follow Him so as to enjoy His fellowship. But Christ, contrary to His custom, told him to proclaim this miracle in his city. He did not fear, as in Judea, that they would make Him an earthly king over them, since this city was full of Gentiles, as we mentioned, so this was an opportunity for them to believe in God more than they believed in the power of the demons.
Be wise in speaking of God's work with you, so that it may be done with humility and concealment of yourself, and so you benefit others and are not fought with pride.
Jesus returned from the country of the Gadarenes to Capernaum, the city of Galilee in which He performed most of His miracles and gave His teachings, and found its people awaiting Him with longing.

The synagogue is the Jewish religious center in the city, in which the Holy Scriptures are read and preaching and teaching take place, and the ruler of the synagogue was a great religious rank. So it was a wonderful thing for Jairus to humble himself and hasten to Christ, falling down and beseeching Him to come and heal his daughter of twelve years who was dying, and this shows his humility and faith. But his faith was less than the faith of the centurion, who asked Christ to heal his servant by a word only from His mouth, whereas Jairus asked Christ to come to his house to heal his daughter. Jairus also is a symbol of the Jewish nation, to whose house Christ comes, that is, is born among it to save it, whereas the Gentiles, in the figure of the centurion, believe only in His word.
The twelve years signify the twelve tribes of Israel.

By faith you can obtain your needs from God your loving Father, who rejoices in your requests and wants to give you more than you ask or think, especially if your faith is joined with humility in the form of lowliness, tears, prostrations, fasts and continual prayers.

entries.section: (8) The healing of the woman with the issue of blood

paragraphs.text: This woman was struck by an illness that made her bleed, and the doctors' attempts to treat her failed, and the illness lasted twelve years, a long time. She spent all her money and gained nothing. By this the weakness of human beings in healing themselves and their need of Christ appears.

entries.section: (8) The healing of the woman with the issue of blood

paragraphs.text: The woman knew that she was unclean, according to the Jewish Law, because she had an issue of blood, so it was not fitting for her to touch Christ, but her faith and her need drove her to come secretly and touch the hem, that is, the edge of Christ's garment, to be healed, and she was healed immediately.

The garment of Christ is a symbol of His apostles and His Church, because of their clinging to Him, and the woman is a symbol of those who have received healing from their sins through their faith in Christ as a result of the preaching of the apostles and the Church.

entries.section: (8) The healing of the woman with the issue of blood

paragraphs.text: Christ wanted to glorify this woman, so He said, Who touched me? The woman was afraid at first to declare herself, and everyone denied that they had tried to touch Him, while Peter and the disciples were astonished at His question, since they saw the crowds pressing on Him, so how could He say, Who touched me? But He made clear that it was not an ordinary touch but a miraculous touch, since power went out of Him to heal one in need.

Do not hasten to judge according to appearances, for God may have a wisdom that you will understand afterward. In every situation learn to pray that God may reveal to you His will that is hidden from your eyes, and to the measure of your humility and faith in prayer you will understand the wisdom of God.

entries.section: (8) The healing of the woman with the issue of blood

paragraphs.text: When Christ announced that a miracle had occurred, the woman found no way but to declare what had happened to her, and she told her story before the crowds. And here Christ glorified her in three ways:
1- He declared His fatherhood to her when He said, Daughter.
2- He declared the greatness of her faith in touching His garment, since many touched Him and did not receive power because of their unbelief.
3- He gave her inner peace, which is the greatest gift a person can receive.
To the extent that you hide yourself in humility, Christ glorifies you, and to the extent that you glorify yourself, you fall into pride and are deprived of His grace.

entries.section: (9) The raising of the daughter of Jairus

paragraphs.text: Christ delayed on the way to proclaim the miracle of the healing of the woman with the issue of blood so that the faith of Jairus might be strengthened, and then the wars of the demons began with despair, for one came from his house announcing to him the death of his daughter, and Christ encouraged him, declaring that she was sick and would be healed, to confirm him in his faith. Christ said this because death is a sickness that has struck mankind, and Christ is able to heal it.

entries.section: (9) The raising of the daughter of Jairus

paragraphs.text: When Christ came to the house of Jairus, He went into the room of the dead daughter and took with Him His three close disciples, Peter, James and John, and also the girl's father and mother, so that they might see with their own eyes and understand and grasp the power of this miracle, so that their faith might increase and they might become witnesses of what they saw.

entries.section: (9) The raising of the daughter of Jairus

paragraphs.text: Christ tried to quiet the mourners in the house by saying to them that she was asleep, and they laughed Him to scorn because of their certainty that she was dead, and because they did not have faith like Jairus, his wife and the disciples. The weakness of your faith deprives you of understanding God's words and His work with you.

entries.section: (9) The raising of the daughter of Jairus

paragraphs.text: Christ took the girl by the hand and commanded her to arise, to show His divinity in a tangible way so that Jairus might understand it, and the girl arose immediately. And to confirm that her spirit had returned to her, Christ commanded that something be given her to eat, and she ate before them, and they were assured that she had returned to life.

entries.section: (9) The raising of the daughter of Jairus

paragraphs.text: The girl's parents were greatly astonished, while the faith of the disciples was stronger because of the miracles they had seen before and the teachings they had heard. And Christ commanded her parents not to spread the news of the miracle, because He does not want glory from men but wants the healing of souls by His teachings, and His miracles are to confirm His teachings so that they may believe in Him and be saved, and so that they would not be occupied with the material miracle and make Him an earthly king over them. For their idea of the awaited Messiah was mistaken, since they supposed Him to be an earthly king who would deliver them from the Romans and not eternal salvation. The mission of the disciples, the feeding of the multitudes and the Transfiguration

Before Christ sent His disciples out to serve, He gave them authority over the demons and all their works in human beings, so that they might cast them out and deliver people from them, and also heal all diseases.

If God calls you to His service, be confident that He gives you His power first, and no obstacle stands before you, not even the demons, because our God is able to do all things, and it is He who works in you when you serve Him.

The aim of the service is to proclaim God's reign over hearts and repentance from every sin, so that the heart may become pure and fit for God to dwell in. He joined this proclamation with the healing of diseases as a confirmation of the power of these teachings, and because we are in the body and not spirits only, we need spiritual teaching joined with support for the body, that is, its healing from diseases.

Christ declared to His disciples that they have no need of material resources in His service, because God, who gave them authority over the demons and diseases, is sufficient for all their needs. So they do not need a (staff) to lean on or to defend themselves with, because Christ defends them with His Cross, the true staff. Nor do they need a (scrip) in which food is put, because Christ is their true food and gives them their needs of material bread. Nor the money of the world (silver), for He enriches them, and they have no need of (coats), for He clothes them with the garment of righteousness, and preserves their material garments, and compensates them for everything material that is lost.

He also commanded them not to move from house to house for the sake of courtesies and hospitality, but to stay in one house in order to concentrate on their aim, which is preaching, and in this there is no burden on that house because they stay only a short time in each village.

Christ warned them that some would reject their teachings, and they should not be disturbed, but shake off the dust from their feet, that is, take nothing material from them, not even the dust, and continue preaching to others.

The beautiful thing is that they cared for every village or small place and offered it the service of preaching and healing. Do not neglect anyone, however small or weak he may seem, but offer the love of Christ to all, for among them are the brethren of God, and this rejoices His heart greatly.

Herod Antipas was tetrarch of Galilee, the son of Herod the Great, and he heard of the preaching of Christ and His disciples and was perplexed because of some sayings spread among the people that John was risen from the dead, while others said that Elijah, who had ascended to heaven, had appeared on earth, and others thought that Christ was one of the old prophets, such as Isaiah, who had risen and begun to preach.

Herod admitted his crime, which was the killing of John, and wondered whether he had truly risen from the dead. His fear of John's rebukes of him was still great, and he desired to see Christ to be sure of this. I hear of Him such things -: that is, the mighty miracles of Christ.
Sin troubles the sinner, and the word of truth goes on echoing even after the death of the one who spoke it; so regain your peace by repentance so that you are not disturbed by the truth.

After the disciples returned from the service on which Christ had sent them, they came to Him and told Him all that had happened to them, and then Christ withdrew with His disciples by way of the sea to the city of Bethsaida, and came to the plain adjoining the city to rest with His disciples in this desert place.

It is important that you give a report of your service to the One who sent you, that is, God, with prayer and thanksgiving, and also to the one responsible for your service, so that he may follow you up and guide you.

The crowds of the Jews heard of His presence, and hurried to Him, and He welcomed them, and neither He nor His disciples sought their own rest, but He seized it as an opportunity to satisfy them with His life-giving word and to heal those who sought healing from their diseases. We notice that Christ prepared the crowds by His word, and cleansed them of their weariness and diseases, before they ate of the food He blessed (the fish and the bread).

As happens today in partaking of the Holy Mysteries, we must prepare ourselves with spiritual teachings through the Liturgy of the Catechumens and all the prayers of the Liturgy, and be cleansed in the sacrament of repentance and confession; then we are made worthy to receive the Holy Mysteries.
God gives you, if you feel your need of Him and ask of Him.

From the sweetness of Christ's word and His care for healing all diseases, the time lengthened until sunset, and the disciples felt the hunger of the crowds and their need of rest, so they asked Christ to send them away so that they might return to their villages where they would find food and a place to rest, because the plain where they had gathered was outside the cities and villages. Here the care of the servants, that is, the disciples, for those they serve appears.

Christ responded with concern to the crowds' need of food, and asked His disciples to look for food to feed the crowds. They searched and found only five loaves and two fishes with a lad, and then they told Christ that they had no food, and that if He wished, the disciples could go and buy food for the crowds from the surrounding villages. This is the last of human capabilities, namely weakness and helplessness before the greatness of the problem; they recognized it but had no solution, since they also did not have the money to buy this food.

The number of the crowds was great, five thousand men besides women and children, and the number of women and children was not mentioned because the man is the head of the family and so points to it; that is, those who ate were 5000 families.

The omission of women and children is not out of contempt for them, but symbolizes spiritually that the woman points to the life of luxury and the child to immaturity, while the man points to the serious life and the bearing of responsibility. The number five points to the five books of Moses, that is, all the Jews, and a thousand points to eternity and the heavenly life, so the five thousand point to the Jews who believe in Christ and live with a heavenly mind. The five loaves point to the five senses, as the scholar Origen says, that is, the completeness of human effort. The two fishes are a symbol of the Old and New Testaments, so they offered to Christ human effort in its great weakness in the two Testaments, and He by His blessing made it abundant and sufficient to satisfy.

As the weakness of man appears, the power of Christ and His divinity appear, who began to solve the problem, and He commanded the disciples to divide the crowds into companies, each company of fifty, and by this order the food could reach everyone, and the greatness of the blessing appears in their being satisfied.

The number five, as we said, points to human effort, and ten is the number of perfection, so fifty signifies the perfection of human effort, which is merely dividing them into companies, while the satisfaction comes from the grace of Christ.

The disciples and the crowd obeyed, and here the importance of order and obedience appears. Then Christ took the two fishes and the five loaves, that is, the small gift of men, and looked up to heaven to lift hearts to the heavenly life and to declare that He is God who came from heaven to redeem them, and then He blessed the food and broke it, and the blessing continued until they distributed it to all the crowd.

All ate and were filled, and there was more than enough, so Christ commanded that the fragments be gathered, to make them feel the overflow of the blessing so that we do not neglect it or throw it away, and the fragments were many, so that they filled twelve baskets, corresponding to the number of the disciples or the number of the tribes of Israel, that is, the blessing is sufficient for all believers, and as each disciple carries a basket on his shoulder while returning to the city, he is assured in his heart of the power and blessing of the miracle.

Christ was alone with His disciples in a quiet place, and offered a prayer for their faith in Him and to teach them the importance of prayer and solitude. In proportion to the importance of the service, it ought to be preceded by prayer and solitude to be filled with God. Then Christ asked His disciples what people thought of Him, to show human thought and its limits, and to encourage them afterward to declare their faith in Him, which is higher than the faith of the crowds.

The opinions of the Jews differed, for some thought He was John risen from the dead or Elijah come down from heaven, because of His power in declaring the truth like theirs, and because of His profound words others thought He was one of the prophets of the Old Testament who had risen and begun to preach again.
The Christ of God: the One anointed by God for the redemption of mankind.
Christ asked His disciples about their faith in Him, after they had been discipled at His hands and understood Him more than the crowds, who still lived with a limited, earthly human mind.
So Peter, being bold, declared the thought of the disciples about Christ, that He is the awaited Messiah, of whom the prophecies spoke.

Christ forbade them to declare this to the crowds so that they would not be occupied with Him as an earthly king, since the mistaken belief of the Jews about the Christ was that His kingdom was earthly and would deliver them from the Romans, and He made clear to His disciples that He must suffer and die and afterward rise victorious, for the Messiah is the Redeemer and Savior who dies for us to raise us up in Him.

Accept to suffer with Christ first, so that you may enjoy His power and resurrection in your life, and do not be occupied with people's opinion of you lest you be hindered from your aim, which is the Kingdom.

After Christ declared to His disciples the necessity of His suffering and death for mankind, it seems that He reached one of the villages with His disciples and the crowds came out to meet Him, and He declared to them also an essential condition for His followers, namely taking up the cross, through humility and denial of self, and then bearing sufferings and afflictions also, not only at certain times or at the beginning of life with God, but as an essential mark of the believer's life every day.

Whoever saves his life is concerned with satisfying his lusts and his bodily comfort and running after honor. He loses it: by this he draws away from God and is enslaved to his body, and nothing awaits him but eternal destruction. Christ gladdens the hearts of His hearers in that taking up the cross is the salvation of the soul, for to the extent of bearing the cross and crushing the self, the soul is delivered from sin and enjoys fellowship with Christ, and then receives eternal salvation.
The meaning of taking up the cross is giving up the corrupt pleasures of the world, because the soul and its salvation are more precious than the whole world

Whoever refuses to take up the cross and is ashamed to bear disgrace, insults and sufferings, Christ also will be ashamed of him on the Day of Judgment before the angels and the saints, that is, he will be cast into torment and lose all the glory of the children of God. So taking up the cross is an essential condition for salvation and eternal glory.

Christ concludes His words by saying that His salvation will soon be made known by His death and resurrection, and everyone who accepts taking up the cross will believe in Him and He will reign over his heart, and so many of His hearers will see the Kingdom of God in the hearts of believers. There is another interpretation, that He means the revelation of His glory on the Mount of Transfiguration to three of His disciples. And a third interpretation, the spread of the Gospel throughout the whole world within not many years at the hands of the Apostles, so that God reigns over the hearts of believers spread throughout the whole world.

The meaning of this is to encourage His hearers to take up the cross to obtain His reign over their hearts and then the eternal Kingdom. Accept the sufferings that meet you, for they are by God's permission for the growth of your spiritual life and your deliverance from many sins, and have recourse to God in the midst of these sufferings, so that your faith is established and you experience fellowship with Him more than before.

Eight days after His talk about the sufferings and the crucifixion (counting the day on which He spoke of the crucifixion and the day on which He was transfigured, and so this is two days more than Matthew and Mark mention, for they said after six days (Mt 17:1).

The number 8 points to eternity, because the days of the week are 7, so the day after them brings us into what lies beyond this life, that is, eternity, and this is because the Transfiguration is a glimpse of the glories of heaven.

Christ took His three close disciples, because of their special spiritual readiness to receive great divine revelations and their eagerness and joy to be with Christ as much as possible, and He went up with them to a mountain, which was most likely Mount Hermon.

The mountain is a symbol of carrying out the commandment, so spiritual striving is needed to rise from earthly things to heavenly things, by carrying out the commandment and bearing the toils of the ascent, to enjoy God's blessing and His revealing Himself to us as we carry out His commandments.
The purpose first declared to the disciples was prayer in solitude with Christ, and since they loved solitude and prayer, Christ revealed His glory to them in the Transfiguration.
God is ready to reveal Himself to you if you love to be with Him in prayer and strive to carry out His commandments.
Christ did not leave His humanity, but was changed, that is, became glorified, for He is God incarnate, and His divinity did not cause Him to lose His humanity.
Christ's raiment is a symbol of the Church, which clings to Him, and so becomes white from the brightness of His glory and His work in her. So our glory comes through our clinging to Him.

Moses and Elijah appeared with Christ in His transfiguration in the form of two men. Moses represents the Law and Elijah represents the prophets, for Christ is the end of the Law and the prophets and the hope of those who have fallen asleep like Moses, and of the living who strive like Elijah.

Moses and Elijah appeared with Christ transfigured in inexpressible glory, in order that Christ might reveal something of His eternal divinity and the glory of His saints in Him, and the subject of the conversation was the redemption that He would accomplish by the Cross at Jerusalem, since this is the aim of the Law and the prophets and of Christ's Incarnation. The Transfiguration does not distract us from the Cross, but the Cross is the way to complete the divine love for mankind so that it may be glorified in Him.
If you want Christ to be transfigured in your heart, bear His sufferings so that you may experience His love.

The three disciples could not bear the greatness of Christ's glory in His transfiguration, and His light, which is brighter than the sun in its shining as Matthew and Mark mention in their Gospels, so they slept through the weakness of the flesh and heard only a little of Christ's conversation with Moses and Elijah, and when they awoke they found the scene as it was, that is, Christ in great glory.

The disciples noticed that Moses and Elijah were about to depart, and from the excess of their joy at the sight of the Transfiguration they wished they could remain in it always. So Peter, expressing this, wished to make three tabernacles for Christ, Moses and Elijah, so that they might remain before the disciples in this great sight.

A person makes a shelter to protect him from the heat and light of the sun, but now the light was shining from Christ Himself, so how would He need a shelter? But Peter did not grasp all this, because the glory of the Transfiguration had overwhelmed him, for it is beyond the understanding of the mind.

Enjoying Christ in solitude and His transfiguration to you does not make you forget to return to your service and bear sufferings; rather, the Transfiguration is a divine revelation that supports you in the toils of service and the sufferings of life.

The glory of the Transfiguration was too great for the three disciples to bear any longer, so a cloud overshadowed them, and they feared as they entered into it and lost sight of everything around them. The cloud points to the presence of God, as happened with Moses on the mountain when he received the Law.

What increased their awe was hearing the voice of God declaring that Christ is His only Son, and commanding them to hear His teachings so that they might be saved, for He is the only Son in essence, revealed to mankind to redeem it, and this same testimony had preceded at Christ's baptism in the Jordan (Mt 3:17).

After that the disciples found themselves alone with Christ, for Moses and Elijah had departed and the cloud had vanished, and the disciples told no one of the Transfiguration until after His resurrection as Christ commanded them (this is mentioned in the Gospel of Matthew), because of the weakness of the crowds' faith, for they would not understand or grasp His divinity and His transfiguration.

entries.section: (7) The casting out of a devil from the only son of his father

paragraphs.text: The Transfiguration was probably at night, and on the morning of the next day Christ had come down from the mountain with the three disciples, and found the crowds who loved His teachings and needed healing from His hands waiting for Him with the nine remaining disciples.

entries.section: (7) The casting out of a devil from the only son of his father

paragraphs.text: A father came forward to Christ who had an only son whom the devil had entered, so that he lost his mind and balance and would cry out at times and at other times fall to the ground unconscious with saliva running from his mouth like the foam of the sea (froth), and this person would strike himself on the ground many times by the devil's action so that his body was full of bruises (bruising him), and with difficulty the devil would leave him for a little and then return and throw him down again, so his torment was severe and the father's heart was torn for his son, therefore he asked Christ to look upon him, confident of His fatherhood and tenderness. Trust in God's tenderness and set your troubles before Him in prayer, for His fatherhood answers you in proportion to your humility and faith.

entries.section: (7) The casting out of a devil from the only son of his father

paragraphs.text: The father complained to Christ of the disciples' inability to cast the devil out of his son.

entries.section: (7) The casting out of a devil from the only son of his father

paragraphs.text: Christ revealed the reason the devil did not come out, which was the weakness of this father's faith, like the weakness of the faith of the rest of the crowds, in addition to the weakness of the disciples' faith; He also revealed the reason the devil enters people, which is their wickedness and their distance from God. Then He told the man to bring his son before Christ that He might heal him.

entries.section: (7) The casting out of a devil from the only son of his father

paragraphs.text: While they were bringing this son, before he came near to Christ, the devil threw him down, and he fell on the ground in a faint, and here Christ rebuked him by the authority of His divinity, and the devil came out and the son was healed, and He gave him back to his father.

The miracle of casting out the devil was great because of the evil state the son was in, and the disciples were amazed together with the crowds. Perhaps the disciples' thinking turned to the nearness of Christ's declaring Himself a king and savior of the Jews from the Roman occupation, so Christ drew their attention to the aim of His Incarnation, which is redemption and not the display of His glory, because He is God glorified from eternity.
Christ reminded His disciples of His earlier talk with them about His sufferings and His crucifixion at the hands of men, for this is the purpose of the Incarnation.

The disciples did not understand the reason for Christ's suffering, being absorbed in their wish that Christ would reign on earth and glorify them with Him, and from their amazement at His authority over the demons they were afraid to ask Him the meaning of His being delivered into the hands of men and His bearing many sufferings even to death.

Do not immerse yourself in your material ambitions and the lusts of the world, lest the sight of the truth and the knowledge of God and sound conduct be hidden from you, and then you become exposed to distress from many things.

entries.section: (9) Teaching humility by setting a child

paragraphs.text: Sadly, the disciples did not understand Christ's words about His sufferings and crucifixion and the necessity that His followers take up the cross after Him, because of their being influenced by the Jewish thought about the Messiah, that He reigns a material kingdom and glorifies them with Him. Therefore they reasoned and discussed who would be greatest in this earthly kingdom.

entries.section: (9) Teaching humility by setting a child

paragraphs.text: They did not tell Christ what they had discussed, since they were ashamed of it, but Christ by His divinity knew their thoughts and their fall into the sin of pride in seeking material greatness, so He offered them a solution by setting a child in their midst, who represents humility and innocence, for it is easy for a child to declare his need and weakness before all.

entries.section: (9) Teaching humility by setting a child

paragraphs.text: The least among you: the humble one, like the child.
Great, glorified and exalted in the sight of God, and he will have a higher place in heaven.

Christ honored childhood, which the Romans and Greeks despised at that time, and the Jews also, for He regarded receiving and honoring a child as receiving Him, and whoever receives Christ receives Him that sent Him, to affirm that He and God are one. And receiving care for the child is an offering of the humility apparent in him, and this humility is the cause of true greatness in the sight of God.
Contemplate the qualities of children and learn from their conduct so that you may acquire humility.

entries.section: (10) Forbidding one who casts out devils

paragraphs.text: The beloved John thought that the working of miracles was confined to Christ's disciples, so when he saw with the rest of the disciples a person casting out devils, they forbade him because he was not one of the disciples. This shows that the love of preeminence and pride, which Christ tried to cure in the preceding verses, was still within the disciples.

entries.section: (10) Forbidding one who casts out devils

paragraphs.text: Christ answered John by declaring an important principle in Christianity, namely love for all and appreciation of every good work, such as giving relief to a person by driving demons away from him even if the one who does this work is not connected with us. For God works in whomever He sees fit, but this does not mean that we follow everyone who does good without discernment. We do not attack heretics, for example, except in their heresy, but as for the good that they do, we do not stand against it, while taking care not to be deceived by them.

I wish you would learn a virtue from every person you meet, even one who is far from the Church, for God works in all to draw all to Himself, and your learning virtues from others moves you to love them, teaches you humility and makes you grow spiritually.

When the end of Christ's life on earth drew near, through His crucifixion and death and then His resurrection and ascension, He set out traveling from Galilee to Jerusalem where He would suffer, for His being taken up is His being lifted up on the Cross, and then His being lifted up by the Ascension.

And He did not travel directly to Jerusalem, but spent a few months in Perea east of the Jordan, and the events that took place in this period are recorded in the following ten chapters, and the Gospel of Luke alone records them, except for a few events that Luke mentioned but at another time, because Luke does not concern himself with chronological order.
If sufferings await you, do not draw back from your responsibility so as to fulfil your aims, and be confident that God supports you in every good work you do.
Christ drew near to Samaria, and sent some of His disciples before Him to one of the villages of Samaria, to prepare a house in which He might stay and preach.

The Samaritans refused to let this Jew (Christ) enter and stay with them, because they hate the Jews, since from the eighth century before the birth of Christ they had mixed with the pagans who migrated to them from the lands of the Assyrian kingdom, and had turned away from the worship of God in Jerusalem. Perhaps they rejected Christ because of His concern for worship in Jerusalem and not on Mount Gerizim, where they pray.
And God permitted them to reject Him so that He might complete His journey to Jerusalem and accomplish redemption by His sufferings and crucifixion.

James and John were enraged by the Samaritans' insult to Christ in refusing His entry among them, so they thought to take vengeance on them by fire coming down from heaven to consume them, basing this thought on what Elijah did to the servants of King Ahaziah, when he brought down fire that consumed them as they came to arrest him (2 Kgs 1:10-11)

Christ rejected the words of James and John, that is, rejected the spirit of vengeance in them, and made clear that He had become incarnate to save the world, whereas in the case of Elijah in the Old Testament, God wanted to show by his hands the weakness of idol worship, and that He is the only God able to destroy all the wicked who follow the worship of idols. Then Christ departed to continue His preaching quietly in another village far from Samaria.
Be concerned with positive action and gentleness in dealing with others, even if they wrong you, finding excuses for them.

Many were influenced by Christ's teachings, and one of them said to Him that he wanted to follow Him, that is, to become one of His disciples, but God, who knows what is in hearts, answered him, revealing what was in his heart, since he regarded Christ, like the rest of the Jews, as an earthly king, and wanted to follow Him to obtain glory and wealth.

Christ said to him that the foxes and the birds have places to which they resort, but He has no particular house in which to lodge, that is, He does not even own a place like the animals and the birds, and consequently whoever follows Him must strip himself of the love of money and earthly glory.

The foxes point to craftiness and the birds to pride, because they soar on high, so the spiritual person must be freed from craftiness and pride, so that Christ may find a place within him in which to rest.

Christ found a person who had a spiritual readiness for spiritual discipleship and service, so He said to him, Follow me, to reveal one of the hindrances of his following, since he answered Christ in the affirmative, that is, agreeing to follow Him, but first asked permission to bury his father and put off following Jesus.

What is meant here by burying is caring for his aged father until he dies and burying him, or what is meant is the rites of mourning for the dead, which may extend for months, and not merely the act of burial; for God commanded honoring parents and consequently attention to their burial.

Christ answered by rejecting this postponement, and made clear that caring for people more than God is a failure to appreciate His love, so God ought to be obeyed more than people, and the one who does not understand and appreciate the importance of salvation and service is dead spiritually; therefore He said, Let the dead (spiritually) bury their dead (physically), that is, those absorbed in material things are occupied with the rites of mourning or emotional relationships, but you ought to care for the salvation of your soul before everything, which is achieved through your service to God and preaching His Kingdom.

The third case is a person who wanted to follow Christ but was hesitating between following Him and his attachment to his family. The young man does not mean by farewell that he would greet them, for that does not take a long time, but means that he would spend many days with them, and he might not be able to leave them because of emotional attachment, and consequently would not follow Christ.

Christ's answer to him was the parable of the plowman, who cannot complete his work unless he concentrates on looking ahead to the end of the field that he will reach with the plow, pressing on it with his foot to do his work successfully; but if he looks behind him, the plow goes in crooked directions, and will not break the ground to the depth required.
What is meant here is that whoever is occupied with the world, material things and emotional relationships more than with God, they will make him hesitant and even hinder him from following Christ.

Christ rejoices in your following Him, if you seek no aim but Him and are not occupied with material things or human relationships more than with Him; then you are able to love God and love all people.
The mission of the Apostles and the good Samaritan

entries.section: (1) The mission of the seventy apostles

paragraphs.text: Others, that is, other than the twelve disciples, and each of them is considered an apostle and a general bishop in the service afterward for the whole world; but the seventy apostles did not receive any priestly rank, though some of them became deacons like the seven deacons mentioned in (Acts 6:3), and some of them were appointed by the Twelve as priests or bishops to help them in the service.

Christ chose seventy men from the crowds who followed Him, in whom He saw love for Him and for the service. St. Ambrose says that they were 72) (but St. Luke wrote the approximate number, that is, 70), (but the Church mentions them in her prayers by their full number, which is 72).(Christ had previously sent the twelve disciples, and then sent the seventy apostles.
The number twelve points to the twelve tribes of Israel, while the seventy apostles point to the seventy elders whom Moses chose to judge the people (Num 11:16-25).

In view of the breadth of the ministry that Christ would carry out and the shortness of the time, He sent them to the cities and villages in which He would preach, to prepare souls to hear His teachings, and He sent them two by two so that each might encourage the other. St. Luke alone mentions the seventy apostles and their mission, because they were sent to towns in the region of Perea, which is east of the Jordan, where the Jews were mixed with the Gentiles; for the Gospel of Luke was written to the Gentiles and so is concerned with their ministry.

entries.section: (1) The mission of the seventy apostles

paragraphs.text: Christ declares a permanent truth, which is the multitude of souls needing the proclamation compared with the number of servants, and He sets down the solution, which is prayer, that God may choose servants for Himself and stir their feelings to love Him and serve Him. It is good that you begin your service with prayer, relying on God in it and on His support by sending servants who will complete the work with you and after you.

entries.section: (1) The mission of the seventy apostles

paragraphs.text: The service seems difficult when the lamb is to preach to the wolf, but the power of God with the lamb makes it change fierce souls like the wolf into gentle souls like the lamb, so it supports the lamb and protects it from the attacks and persecutions of the wicked. And if God permits the servant to suffer or even die for His sake, He will give him a great place in heaven and use his endurance of sufferings to rebuke the wicked and bring them back to Him by repentance so that they believe and are saved. Do not meet evil with evil, because violence is a disturbance within a person. So be calm, relying on your mighty Christ, to absorb the rage of the violent and declare your strong love for the wicked, for even if they despise it at first, it will affect them afterward ... and so you keep your calm and win others.

entries.section: (1) The mission of the seventy apostles

paragraphs.text: A purse: in which they carried their gold, their silver and all their money.
A scrip: in which they carry their food.
Shoes: because they would not endure the much walking between the cities and villages during the preaching, so they rely on God, who provides for all their needs.

Salute no man: one must concentrate on the aim, which is preaching, so that no one is occupied with many greetings, and of course what is meant is not that they should not show a greeting to those they meet.
Christ stresses the necessity of relying on Him and not on material things.

entries.section: (1) The mission of the seventy apostles

paragraphs.text: The son of peace: the one who welcomes peace and is worthy of it.
Your peace shall rest upon it: he enjoys the good news of salvation, and so receives peace in his life.
It shall turn to you again: you keep the grace of peace and of the salvation that is in Christ, and it abides in you.

He commands them to offer peace and love to everyone they meet, and if anyone refuses, they are not to be disturbed, because those who refuse lose the peace offered to them, and God establishes peace in the hearts of the servants so that they may continue their service of bringing peace to all.

entries.section: (1) The mission of the seventy apostles

paragraphs.text: Christ encourages His apostles to take their necessary needs from those to whom they preach, namely food, drink and a place to stay, the fewest necessities. And they are to eat whatever is set before them, not refusing the foods of the Gentiles which may be forbidden to the Jews, because this prohibition was a symbol of rejecting sins, not because of any evil in this food, and so that they would not cause the Gentiles to whom they preach to stumble.

The labourer is worthy of his hire: the servant deserves to receive his necessary needs from the service, and not be occupied with providing them, so as to concentrate all his effort on the service and the preaching.
And He commands them not to move from house to house seeking a better place or food, but to stay in one place, concentrating on their aim, which is the service.
Eat such things as are set before you: be content with the food set before you, and do not ask for other kinds.

entries.section: (1) The mission of the seventy apostles

paragraphs.text: The aim of the preaching is to alert people to the nearness of the Kingdom of God, that is, to prepare for it by repentance and a holy life, and He supported them by the working of miracles of healing to confirm their message and to draw souls to hear their teaching.

entries.section: (1) The mission of the seventy apostles

paragraphs.text: Go your ways out into the streets of the same: proclaim to all the crowds of the city.
Even the very dust of your city, which cleaveth on us, we do wipe off against you: that is, we took nothing from you, not even the dust, for we seek no material gain.
Be sure of this: a specific and clear warning that they may repent.
The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you: Christ wants to reign over your hearts, so do not persist in rejecting Him, because the end of your life is near and you will face God the Judge.

entries.section: (1) The mission of the seventy apostles

paragraphs.text: The city of Sodom was famous for evil and God burned it (Gen 19). And the cities of Tyre and Sidon, God commanded the destruction of both for their evils in ancient times (Isa 23), but the cities that reject the teachings of Christ and His apostles, like Capernaum (whose people were characterized by pride and refused to believe in Christ, who had done among them many miracles and many teachings), and like Chorazin and Bethsaida, their punishment in the judgment will be heavier than that of the cities destroyed in ancient times.

Because whoever knows more is asked to give more, whoever enjoyed the ministry of the New Testament and refused will have a greater punishment than one who refused God's teachings in the Old Testament, because the teachings of the New Testament are clearer and more powerful.

entries.section: (1) The mission of the seventy apostles

paragraphs.text: Christ made clear that the apostles represent Him, so His teachings are on their lips, and whoever receives the teachings of the apostles has received Christ Himself, and whoever despises their teachings has despised Christ, and consequently despises God the Father who sent Him.
Do not reject the voice of God in every counsel you hear, not only in the Church, the Holy Bible and the father of confession, but pay attention also to the counsels of those around you.

entries.section: (2) The results of the apostles' mission

paragraphs.text: The apostles rejoiced at the success of their mission and at people's acceptance of their preaching, and perhaps they had healed many sick, but what drew their attention was the submission of the demons to them when they commanded them to come out of the people tormented by them.

entries.section: (2) The results of the apostles' mission

paragraphs.text: Christ confirmed His apostles' joy by declaring that He had seen Satan fall like lightning from heaven, that is, the beginning of the shattering of his authority, which would be completed by the Cross, since he was shaken as a result of their preaching and the casting out of his helpers the demons from many souls, and the beginning of people's return to God by repentance.

entries.section: (2) The results of the apostles' mission

paragraphs.text: Christ gave His apostles authority, not only over the demons, but over all their works and their stirring up of creation against human beings. In ancient times he moved the serpent in Paradise and brought down Adam and Eve, and he still stirs up animals like serpents and scorpions to harm man, and even stirs up trials and troubles to harm them, but all this has come under the authority of the apostles to prevent it by the power of God, as appeared in the lives of the saints and the children of God throughout history.

entries.section: (2) The results of the apostles' mission

paragraphs.text: Christ directed their sight to the more important joy, which is their being counted children of the Kingdom, by their spiritual conduct in faith, repentance and striving in every virtue. This is far greater than great gifts such as casting out demons or healing the sick, because a gift does not justify its possessor if he does not repent and live with God, whereas the fruits of the Holy Spirit and the virtuous life guarantee the Kingdom of Heaven. And if the names have been written, they must be kept and made firm by continuing in spiritual conduct until death so that they may not be blotted out.

Do not be occupied with gifts such as the ability to preach and teach, but rather live with God in repentance and love, for this is what guarantees your salvation. And if you are given a gift, use it to glorify God with humility lest you fall like the proud Satan.
Carry your cross in endurance and labor, and the lusts of the world and its fears will not harm you.
Christ offered a prayer to the Father, which is a conversation within the divine Being, just as a person speaks to himself in a dialogue within his mind.

This prayer was joy, exultation and thanksgiving for the grace that overflowed upon weak human beings who are humble like children, that is, the disciples and apostles, and they preached the Kingdom of God. At the same time this wisdom was hidden from the proud who are wise in their own eyes, like the scribes and Pharisees and the philosophers of the world. For God, the Creator and Ruler of all, rejoices to give His grace to the humble that they may become the wisest on earth.
To the extent that you humble yourself before God and people, God gives you wisdom, so that you know the way of your salvation, discern between matters and draw many to faith.

Here He declares the equality of the Son with the Father, for He has all the authority of the Father, and no one knows the essence of the Son but the Father, nor the essence of the Father but the Son, and then the Son gives His knowledge to the humble who love Him.

Christ praised His disciples by blessing them (how happy they are), because they saw Him and believed His good news, which the prophets and righteous kings of the Old Testament, such as David, longed to see, namely the Christ of whom they prophesied. Thank God every day that you were born a Christian and enjoy the Holy Sacraments; eternal happiness awaits you after the striving of this life.

The lawyer is one of the scholars of the Law, a class of the scribes distinguished by their deep study of the Mosaic Law, and he came to tempt Christ and to catch Him in an error, so his question was ill-intentioned and not of pure purpose. He asked Him about the way to reach the eternal Kingdom, hoping that Christ would point to other ways than the commandments and the Law, and so would be against Moses and the Old Testament. The lawyer's conversation with Christ is different from the ruler's question to Him mentioned in (ch. 18:18-30), though there is some similarity in their question about eternity.

Christ knew that the lawyer meant to tempt Him, so He answered his question with another question, namely, What is written in the law? how readest thou? that is, what is the summary of the commandments and the Law?
The lawyer's answer showed his knowledge of the Ten Commandments, and he summarized them in two commandments, the love of God and the love of one's neighbor, as mentioned in (Deut 6:5; Lev 19:18).
Christ praised the lawyer's answer although He knew that he was tempting Him, and told him to carry out what he had summarized, that is, this love, in order to inherit eternal life.
It is good to know much about spiritual things, but the more important thing is to apply them in your life in order to be with Christ.

entries.section: (5) The parable of the good Samaritan

paragraphs.text: Since the lawyer could not find a fault in Christ's words, he asked Him another question on which opinions differ, namely, who is the neighbor: is he the Jew only, or can others be added, or is it limited to some Jews and not all?

entries.section: (5) The parable of the good Samaritan

paragraphs.text: Christ answered the lawyer with a parable, which is the story of a Jewish man who was in Jerusalem, which stands on a mountain, and was traveling to the city of Jericho, which lies lower than Jerusalem by about 1000 meters (a thousand meters), and is seven hours distant from it by a stony road with no cultivation, full of caves and therefore much frequented by robbers, and called the Red Way because of the much bloodshed in it.
Robbers attacked this traveler and stole what he had, even his clothes, and beat him and wounded him, and left him in a bad condition near to death.

This man points to mankind, and Jerusalem is the place of peace and life with God, and Jericho, the city with low walls, represents the world and its lusts, while the robbers are the demons who fight human beings with sins, and steal from them the garments of righteousness, and wound them with iniquities, and leave them in a state of spiritual weakness near to death, because they left Jerusalem, that is, the Church, and went down to the occupations of the world .. that is, Jericho.

entries.section: (5) The parable of the good Samaritan

paragraphs.text: He saw him from afar: although his condition called for drawing near to him and helping him, he did not care and was content to look from far away and then left him.
The priest is a symbol of the Law and the statutes, which were unable to deliver mankind from its sins, but looked and judged it only with weakness.

One of the priests going down from Jerusalem to Jericho passed by this traveler, and stood and looked and saw his bad condition, but it seems that he feared to help him lest the robbers attack him, or because of his preoccupation with his own affairs, he left him and did not help him.

entries.section: (5) The parable of the good Samaritan

paragraphs.text: A Levite: the tribe of Levi was consecrated to the service of the Temple, and each member of it is a servant like the deacon or the servant in the New Testament.
Came and looked: he drew near him and saw his hard condition, which needed quick relief, but because of the hardness of his heart he did not care and left him and went on.
A Levite passed by going down from Jerusalem, and looked and saw this traveler, but he did not help him and left him and went on, probably for the same reasons that the priest thought of.
The Levite is a symbol of the prophets in the Old Testament, who declared the word of God to mankind but could not deliver it from the sentence of death passed upon it.

entries.section: (5) The parable of the good Samaritan

paragraphs.text: A Samaritan: one of the inhabitants of the northern part of the land of the Jews, who are Jews that separated from the worship in Jerusalem and worshipped idols, so a boycott arose between them and the Jews, and a Samaritan does not mingle with any Jew. After that a Samaritan man came, and passed along this road and saw the wounded man and his bad condition, and feelings of tenderness and compassion were stirred toward him.
The word Samaritan means keeper, and he is a symbol of Christ, full of tenderness, who had compassion on fallen mankind, and redeemed it with His blood and guarded it from the wars of the demons.

entries.section: (5) The parable of the good Samaritan

paragraphs.text: He set him on his own beast, which bore the toil of walking along the road, to give rest to the wounded man riding on the beast, and even supported him all along the way until he reached the inn.

The Samaritan drew near to the wounded man and gave him relief, for he bound up his wounds with pieces of his clothes after pouring oil and wine on them, which were the materials used for relieving wounds at that time, and then carried him on his beast and stayed beside him until he brought him to an inn, and took care of his food, drink and rest.

Christ covered our sins and treated them with His righteousness, and put on them oil, to soften the wound, and wine to cleanse it, the first soothing and the second painful; so the Holy Spirit treats our sins with gentleness and firmness. Then He set him on the beast, which represents the Body of Christ in which He bore all our sins and toils, and brought him to the inn, that is, the Church, where he finds all care and rest and food, which is His most holy Body and Blood.

entries.section: (5) The parable of the good Samaritan

paragraphs.text: After the Samaritan had watched over the wounded man's rest, he charged the innkeeper to take care of him and gave him two pence (enough to feed 50 persons one meal at that time), and promised to come after a while to visit him, and if he spent more than the two pence, he would give him all that he had spent.

After Christ accomplished redemption and rose from the dead, He charged His disciples, that is, the bishops of the Church, to take care of mankind, and gave them two pence, which point to the knowledge of the Father and the Son, or to love, because love is between two, or to the Holy Bible with its two Testaments, that is, the word of God, and then He promised to come at His second coming and recompense His Church and His servants for all their labor, however much they have spent.

entries.section: (5) The parable of the good Samaritan

paragraphs.text: After relating this parable to him, Christ asked the lawyer, Which of these three, who passed by this traveler, was neighbor to him?

entries.section: (5) The parable of the good Samaritan

paragraphs.text: The lawyer was compelled to declare the truth, which is that the Samaritan is the nearest person to this wounded Jew, though he did not mention the name of the Samaritan, but said, He that shewed mercy on him, because the Jews hate the Samaritans. Christ answered him that he should live by this love, and so be a neighbor to every person in the world. By this Christ changed the Jews' concept of kinship and love, so that in Christianity the heart is enlarged to love all, however far off or rejected they may be.

Do not neglect the needs of one who asks your help, and hasten to his aid before your preoccupations make you forget to attend to the work of mercy. And if he does not ask your help out of shyness, do not be slack toward him, but seek out the needy of every kind, especially the spiritually needy, that is, those far from God, to help them.
As they went: on the way of their journey toward Jerusalem.
A certain village: it is Bethany, and it is about three quarters of an hour from Jerusalem.

Christ was accustomed to go to the village of Bethany and rest in the house of Lazarus and his two sisters Martha and Mary, and it seems that Martha had precedence in leading and caring for guests, so she received Christ into their house.

Martha took care to prepare a splendid feast worthy of her great guest, the Lord Jesus, and Mary shared with her in the beginning, but when Christ began His life-giving teachings Mary felt that it was better to be content with some foods, and she took care to sit near Christ at His feet in humility to enjoy His teachings.

Hath left me: this means that Mary was helping Martha to prepare the food at first, and then left her because she felt that listening to Christ's words was more important than many dishes at the feast, and it was better to be content with what had been prepared first.

Martha continued preparing the splendid feast, and was not convinced by Mary's view. From the amount of work her nerves became strained, and she fell into condemnation of Christ and of her sister Mary, accusing Him of indifference to her many labors and of failing to tell Mary to share with her in preparing the great feast, and she asked Him to command her sister to leave listening to His teachings and help her.

Despite the importance of what Martha was doing, which is preparing the food necessary for bodily life, she was absorbed in it to an exaggerated degree, to the point that she became troubled, so Christ reproved her. He of course appreciates her love and her care to honor Him, but excessive preoccupation with honoring Christ materially can confuse a person and strain him.
One thing is needful: that is, attachment to Christ and learning from Him, and not excessive care for the needs of the body.

Christ made clear that one dish, or the necessary food, is enough. On the other hand, Mary chose the good part, which is hearing His teachings, over being absorbed in material works, and this choice is what satisfies the soul and saves it forever.
Shall not be taken away: for the love of Christ endures in the heart and brings the Christian to the eternal Kingdom, and does not perish like foods and material things.

Martha is a symbol of material services and useful human works in all fields of life, while Mary is a symbol of the love of the word of God and meditation on it, and this is the more important, and the soul is not saved without it. For although Christ appreciates useful worldly works and all material services, such as helping the sick and the elderly and supporting the poor materially, yet they do not exempt the servant or the spiritual person from his personal relationship with Christ in the Church through the Holy Sacraments, prayer, reading the Holy Bible and spiritual sermons.

Do not be absorbed in material works, even if they are service for Christ, to the neglect of the worship of God, and give priority to your prayers, your readings and your enjoyment of the Holy Sacraments. And even in service, learn and apply the spiritual meanings in your own life before you tell them to others.
Prayer and overcoming the demons. The Lord's Prayer (vv. 1-4):
The Lord's Prayer is mentioned in (Mt 6:9-15), and it is noted that Luke is not concerned with order, since it was said before this time that Luke mentions.

1- And it came to pass, that, as he was praying in a certain place, when he ceased, one of his disciples said unto him, "Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples." 2- And he said unto them, "When ye pray, say, Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth. 3- Give us day by day our daily bread. 4- And forgive us our sins; for we also forgive every one that is indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation; but deliver us from evil."

Christ was praying because He is a perfect man who needs prayer, just as He is perfect God, and He is also the representative of mankind who offers prayer on our behalf so that our prayers may be sanctified in Him, and so that He may give us a model to imitate in our spiritual life.

The disciples noticed the fervor of Christ's prayer, and wished that He would teach them this fervent prayer, especially since spiritual leaders such as John the Baptist and the Pharisees taught their disciples particular prayers.
And this disciple who asked Christ was expressing the feelings of all the disciples, for he said, Teach us how to pray.

In order to approach prayer, we must enter in the spirit of sonship to God as a heavenly Father, so that we in turn are heavenly in our thoughts and conduct, and our sonship gives us boldness and confidence in prayer that God answers us and cares about our words.
The Lord's Prayer is the example that we follow in all our private prayers, in addition to our repeating it because of the depth of the meanings it contains.

The Lord's Prayer includes two parts, the first being the glorifying of God mentioned in this verse, and the second the requests for ourselves mentioned in the following two verses, so that we learn to glorify God first before we ask for anything. The name of God has been holy from eternity, but our asking that His name be hallowed means its being sanctified in us in our words and good works.

Then we ask that God reign over our hearts, so that we come out of the bondage of sin and the lusts of the world. It is a prayer that expresses our longings to obey God and submit to Him, and even our longings for the eternal Kingdom.

Then, as we look at God's ordering in heaven and the obedience of the angels to Him, we long to surrender our lives to Him, so that His will leads us and not our own purposes, which are liable to error. The will of God in heaven and on earth also means in the spirit and in the body.

The daily bread means Christ, whether His most holy Body and Blood, or His life-giving word, because Christ is the bread that came down from heaven as He said in (Jn 6:58). And in other translations such as the Coptic it says our bread that is coming, or of tomorrow, or essential, all of which mean that Christ is our spiritual bread.

The daily bread also means that we ask God for our material needs day by day, because we rely on Him in all our affairs, so we are in need of Him and do not think that we are self-sufficient by our own ability.

This does not mean that we are absorbed in material requests, but our need of the necessities, that is, bread, because we are in the body, and that we are not preoccupied with the future and its needs, which trouble our thoughts.

We confess our sins that God may forgive them, whose power to forgive we trust, and we cannot obtain this forgiveness for our sins, which are great because they are directed against God, unless we first forgive others their sins against us, which are small because they are between human beings. The meaning of this is that unforgiveness deprives us of the forgiveness of our sins. Then, feeling our weakness, we ask God not to allow us trials, but this humility does not mean rejecting God's will if He wants to test us with a trial that benefits us spiritually; therefore we say to Him, if You allow us a trial, deliver us from the evil devil who wants to make us fall into sin and take us away from You.
I wish you would pray the Lord's Prayer calmly so that you grasp its meanings, and so submit to God and enjoy fellowship with Him, and love everyone and live in assurance.

Christ gave a parable on the importance of importunity in prayer, not because He does not know our needs or because repetition in itself is useful, but because it shows the faith of the one praying and his clinging to God, and his declaring his weakness and need, so that he receives God's mercies which He wants to pour out upon him.

The parable tells the story of a man to whom a guest came at midnight, that is, at a critical time, and he did not have the necessary food to feed him, so he went to his neighbor and friend, knocking at his door and asking him for food.

Midnight: a symbol of the time of affliction that a person passes through, so that he has recourse to others to help him, and he asks on behalf of a guest who has come to him from a journey, that is, he prays to God for the needs of others, to rescue these sinners or those in distress.
The three loaves symbolize the necessary food, which is faith in the Holy Trinity, and they symbolize also faith, hope and love, and likewise the need of the spirit, the soul and the body.

The friend answered from within, declaring that the time was not suitable for answering his request, since he was asleep with his children. This sleeper is selfish, thinking of his own comfort, and does not want to help his neighbor whatever his need. Our Christ did not love us from within heaven but became incarnate and came to us, and He is always awake and never sleeps, and His angels (His children) also are attentive, always praising Him and interceding for us, and the door is no longer shut through Christ's Incarnation and redemption, for His resurrection from the dead satisfies all our needs.

The friend within refused at first to answer his friend's request, but as a result of the importunity he rose and gave him what he asked. If the selfish, lazy sleeper moved because of importunity and gave to his neighbor, how much more God who is love, who rejoices in the importunity of His children in prayer and gives them their needs.
Something like this passage (vv. 9-13) is mentioned in (Mt 7:7-11), and Christ said it at another time than this occasion.

Our God, who is love, urges us to ask of Him and to persist, so that He may pour out His gifts upon us, for He wants to give and we do not want to ask, and His slowness in answering our requests is not neglect of us but a testing of our love and our clinging to Him. The threefold repetition of the asking is that it may be of thought, word and deed, that is, we think of God, and raise our voices in prayer and with it our hands also, and we prostrate many times beseeching Him, and it is noticed that the request increases until it reaches knocking with the hands vehemently because of the greatness of the need.

Christ gives another example of the answering of prayer, which is a son asking his father for bread, and it is expected that he will give it to him, and it is not reasonable that he would give him a stone instead of bread, because the tenderness of fatherhood refuses that.

The same applies if the son asks for a fish: he will not give him a serpent that harms him instead of the food he asked for, or if he asks for an egg, it is unreasonable that he would give him instead of it a scorpion that kills him with its poison.
Bread: a symbol of love, because it is the father's gift to his children that they may live.
The stone: points to hardness of heart, that is, lack of love.
The fish: a symbol of faith, since it swims out of sight within the water.

The egg: a symbol of hope, since despite its small size we hope that a bird will come out of it that moves and flies, and God cannot give us, instead of hope, what drives us away from Him and frightens us.
So the three requests symbolize the request for faith, hope and love, and show that fatherhood necessarily requires caring for the children's requests and fulfilling them.

Christ draws a proof from this parable, that fleshly fathers understand how to give good gifts to their children because they love them, how much more God the heavenly Father, the source of all fatherhood and tenderness, who gives to His children who ask of Him not only the material gifts they ask for, but rather the work of His Holy Spirit in them, to establish their faith, their love and their hope in Him, so that they believe that He answers their material requests by His fatherly tenderness, and likewise comforts their hearts and supports them throughout their lives.
