The tender God wants to give you many of the treasures of His love, so ask of Him with a faith that shows your perseverance and your importunity toward Him with the boldness of sonship, however hard the request, and even if God delays in answering, do not despair but rely on Him, because He cares for you until He answers your request. And if His will is something other than what you ask, He will give you rest and joy in His better divine ordering of your life.

entries.section: (3) The accusation of Christ with Beelzebub

paragraphs.text: A devil dwelt in a man and deprived him of the ability to speak, and Christ cast him out of him and he spoke again, and the crowds were amazed at the greatness of the miracle, even including the scribes and Pharisees who oppose Christ.
Sin deprives you of the ability to speak the word of God, and by repentance you regain good speech.

entries.section: (3) The accusation of Christ with Beelzebub

paragraphs.text: Beelzebub: the Aramaic pronunciation of Beelzebul, the god of the Ekronites, and it means lord of the flies, that is, the one who drives away flies.

Those who resisted Christ could not deny the miracle, and because they did not want to believe in Him and hardened their hearts, they accused Him of dealing with Beelzebub the prince of the devils so as to be able to cast out devils, and that this was not authority of His over Satan, but that by the authority of Satan He casts out devils.

entries.section: (3) The accusation of Christ with Beelzebub

paragraphs.text: Another group of those who resisted, who refused to believe despite the greatness of the miracle, asked for a new miracle in order to believe, and of course they would not be able to, because the spirit of doubt was within them, and therefore Christ did not respond to them.

entries.section: (3) The accusation of Christ with Beelzebub

paragraphs.text: Christ answered their doubts by making clear a logical truth, which is that division destroys any house or kingdom, and consequently the division of Satan's kingdom would ruin it, and this is proof that Christ has authority over the demons, and that it is not the prince of the devils who casts out devils.
How dangerous is division within the home, the Church or any society; so whatever the sacrifice, let us seek unity, to keep God within us and working in us.

entries.section: (3) The accusation of Christ with Beelzebub

paragraphs.text: Completing His answer He said, if we suppose that my power is the power of the prince of the devils, then your sons, that is, His Jewish disciples whom they know, by whose authority did they cast out devils? Surely not by a relationship with the prince of the devils, but by the authority I gave them, and by their faith they judge you and expose your doubts.

entries.section: (3) The accusation of Christ with Beelzebub

paragraphs.text: The finger of God -: by it He means the hand of God and His Spirit, that is, that Christ's authority is from Himself because He is God, and this means that the Kingdom of God has come near to the Jews by the Incarnation of Christ, so that He reigns over the hearts of His believing children and judges the unbelievers who reject His reign.

entries.section: (4) The parable of the strong man and the stronger

paragraphs.text: The strong man is Satan, who used to strengthen people by his evils and draw them to hell before the coming of Christ. Satan's arms are the lusts, his palace is hell, and his goods are the souls subject to him who walked in evil.

entries.section: (4) The parable of the strong man and the stronger

paragraphs.text: The stronger than he is Christ, who overcomes him by the Cross and takes his spoils, that is, the souls held captive in hell, and the risen Christ sets them free and brings them up to Paradise.

This is what happens when Satan makes any person fall into evil lusts, but if he has recourse by repentance to Christ, He forgives them to him and frees him from the bondage of the devil, and even establishes him in the new life by His most holy Body and Blood.

entries.section: (4) The parable of the strong man and the stronger

paragraphs.text: Christ here directs attention to the importance of positive action, for whoever refuses to gather souls with Christ gives Satan an opportunity to scatter them, and by this shares with him in drawing people away from God and so is against God. Do not fear the power of the devil or his threats and wars, for they are nothing before the power of God who is with you. Seek God with humility and importunity in all your afflictions, and when the devil fights you, or even after you fall into sin, He frees you and supports you and drives the devil away from you.

entries.section: (5) The parable of the seven unclean spirits

paragraphs.text: Christ gave a new parable to stress the importance of positive action, saying that there is a man who has an unclean spirit, who by the grace of God was able to be rid of it, and this man became sound again, but the unclean spirit kept seeking another wicked man in whom to dwell and found no water, that is, no opportunity for life and dwelling in another person, so he thought to return to his first friend, perhaps he could find in him a readiness for evil and enter him again. This declares the activity of Satan and his constant search for opportunities to fight us, so continual watchfulness is necessary by living with God, so that he does not find a gap through which to enter our lives.

entries.section: (5) The parable of the seven unclean spirits

paragraphs.text: Satan found his first friend, that is, his spirit and body, empty of every good work, and adorned with an inclination to evil lusts.

entries.section: (5) The parable of the seven unclean spirits

paragraphs.text: Satan rejoiced greatly and found it an opportunity to cooperate with a group of devils numbering seven, that is, a great complete number, so he brought them and they dwelt in this man, and so he rushed into many evils, and his end became worse than the beginning of his life.

We ought to seize the spiritual opportunities when God removes the wars of the demons from us, even for a short time, to cling to God and grow in His love, so that if the devil tries to attack us again he finds us in greater strength and is afraid and draws away.
From the greatness of Christ's words and miracles, a woman of the crowd blessed the mother of Christ, because in Jewish society a woman is blessed through her good offspring.

Christ did not reject the blessing of His mother, but directed attention to the more important thing, which is the blessing of whoever hears and does His word, and this is a still greater blessing for the Virgin, for she not only bore Christ, but she is a spiritual person who keeps the word of God at the highest level.
The door is open for you to share with the Virgin and be blessed if you take care to read the Holy Bible and carry it out as a personal message to you every day.

Many of the Jews asked to see signs from Christ although He had done many miracles, but they still asked for other miracles, so Christ declared to them plainly that they needed the sign of Jonah the prophet, that is, his preaching of repentance to the people of Nineveh; for they needed repentance from their doubts and their pride, and seeing any miracles would not profit them without repentance.

As Jonah preached repentance to the people of Nineveh, so Christ preaches repentance to the Jews, because the Kingdom of Heaven has come near to them. And as Jonah came out of the belly of the whale alive after three days, so Christ died three days and then rose. And as Jonah gave life to the people of Nineveh through their obedience to his word, so Christ gives eternal life to those who keep His commandments.

Christ rebukes His hearers for their unbelief, although the queen of the south, that is, of Sheba (Ethiopia or Yemen), a Gentile, believed in the wisdom of Solomon, whereas the Jews have before them the hypostasis of Wisdom Himself, God the Word, and they refuse to believe in Him.

Christ makes clear the judgment awaiting His hearers if they persist in their unbelief, because the Gentile people of Nineveh, by their faith at hearing the word of Jonah, will condemn the Jews who reject the good news of Christ, who is greater than Jonah.
Do not reject the word of God sent to you in various ways, calling you to repentance, so that you may be saved on the Day of Judgment.

A candle is the word of God, which must be made known through our lives, and if we hide it those around us will not benefit from it, so we do not put it under the bushel of worldly preoccupations or human logical measurements. In a secret place: that is, hiding the teachings and not proclaiming them, because this will prevent people from benefiting from them.
A bushel is a vessel whose mouth is narrower than its base, used for measuring the quantities of grain when sold, in place of scales.

The Pharisees were accusing Christ of not declaring His teachings, and demanding signs from Him, although He was declaring His teachings and working miracles, but the problem was their unreadiness to believe, for they were placing the bushel of doubt over their hearts so that they could not believe.

The light that is in thee be darkness: that is, your eye, which was supposed to be a light to your body, into which good feelings enter that help faith, becomes on the contrary darkened by its evil, seeing only doubt and condemnation, and so keeps the heart away from faith.

Christ moves the talk from the candle to the eye, for the single eye is the light of the body. The meaning of the single eye is the one that sees God and His works in everything around it, and sees the virtues of others and thanks God for everything, and then a person is filled with peace and is lit by the light of God within him. But the evil eye, that is, the one that sees the sins of others, condemns them and murmurs, so its body is filled with disturbance and weariness.
And here Christ makes clear to the Pharisees the reason for their unbelief, which is that their eyes are evil and doubt Him, so their hearts refuse to believe in Him.
You must examine your eyes so that your looks may be single, that is, a source of rest and happiness for you, and keep away from every evil look that darkens your life and corrupts it.
Take care that your look is single, and Christ the true Lamp will shine for you with a brightness that gladdens your life always.
While Christ was teaching the crowds, one of the Pharisees invited Him to eat the midday meal with him, and Christ accepted and went in and sat down at table.
The Pharisees were a proud sect of the Jews, who felt themselves distinguished in spiritual knowledge, and represented the aristocratic class.

And although Christ knew that this Pharisee was not pure in his invitation, but wanted to catch Him in an error, yet He accepted the invitation and seized it as an opportunity to teach him and the Pharisees with him.
Be positive despite the evil of those around you. Do not fear them, and declare the truth to them for the salvation of their souls in the manner that suits them.

It was among the traditions of the Pharisees to wash before the meal, and this points to the importance of purification before any work, and it symbolizes Baptism before partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord. The Pharisees did not want to understand the prophecies about Christ, and were content to hold to the symbols, and Christ intended not to wash before eating, not because He is against external purification, but to teach the Pharisees to care for purity of heart before external purity by washing the hands before eating. And the Pharisee (between himself and his fellow Pharisees) condemned Christ because He had not washed.

It is also mentioned in (Mt 23:25-26). The Pharisees cared for outward spiritual appearances in order to obtain the praise of men, while their hearts were full of evil, so Christ rebuked them, not because washing before food is wrong, but for clinging to the appearance without the substance, and caring for men's praise of them without purifying their inner hearts.

What is meant by the platter is the dish, for it is unreasonable that the inside of the cup or the dish should be full of filth and a person eat and drink from them, content with their outward cleanness.

For God is the Creator of the outward body and the inward spirit, and indeed the inner heart is more important than the outward bodily appearance, and God asks for inward purity and then outward purity.

Christ set down a solution to the problem of the Pharisees, which is pride and selfishness, that they should come out of thinking about themselves to feeling for others, and give alms to the needy, so that their hearts are filled with love and cleansed of selfishness.

This makes clear that they need giving and love of others before caring for outward purity, for if they give alms to others their food and possessions become clean because of their love, more than by their purity because of their washing or the cleansing of their vessels on the outside.

It is mentioned in (Mt 23:23), a continuation of the clinging to the appearances of worship without its substance: the Pharisees were careful in their teaching of the people to give tithes of everything, even the plants of mint and rue, which is a medicinal plant, and likewise the plants of pulse, and they neglected the declaration of truth and the love of God, so Christ called them to care for the substance and then to care for the outward appearances of worship.

It is mentioned in (Mt 23:6). Christ also rebuked their love and pursuit of the praise of men, and their care to be glorified by them in places of worship such as the synagogues or public places such as the markets, and by this their inner pride increases.

It is mentioned in (Mt 23:27). Christ likened the hypocrisy of the Pharisees, who clung to outward worship while their hearts were full of pride and evil, to graves hidden under the ground whose surface looks like beautiful ground but inside are the bones of the dead; their outside appears alive with God, and their inside is death because of their distance from Him, and people glorify them and do not know the evil of their hearts. It is good that you have a sound appearance, but the more important thing is that your heart be pure in repentance and rejection of evil thoughts, so that the purity of your heart appears in your readiness for love, giving and serving those around you.
One of the lawyers present in the Pharisee's house objected to Christ's rebuke, because it was directed also to the lawyers, for they share with the Pharisees in the preceding sins.
The lawyers are those who hold to the Law and teach the statutes to the people, and most of them were Pharisees.

It is also mentioned in (Mt 23:4). Christ was not disturbed by the lawyers' objection, but seized it as an opportunity to rebuke them that they might repent, and said to them that they demand of people heavy and hard teachings and do not apply the least of them in their own personal lives. I wish you would try to carry out in your life first all that you teach others, so that your words may be strong, tried and effective in others, and your words and teachings may be for your own spiritual growth and benefit before those who hear you.

It is also mentioned in (Mt 23:29). Christ also rebuked the lawyers' care in building the tombs of the prophets and adorning them, while they did not repent of the sins of their fathers who killed the prophets and did not submit to their teachings which speak of Christ who stands among them now. By this they bear witness against themselves that they are the sons of the killers of the prophets, and were not cleansed of this trait because they did not repent and did not obey the teachings of Christ.

It is mentioned in (Mt 23:34-36). The wisdom of God, that is, Christ, said that He would send many prophets and apostles to call them to repentance, and if they did not repent, the blood of these prophets would bear witness to their wickedness, and all the wicked would be punished in eternal torment for the shedding of the blood of the martyrs, from the blood of Abel, the first martyr of the world, to the blood of Zacharias, who is said to be Zacharias the father of John the Baptist, whom the soldiers killed after he had placed the child John on the altar and the angel snatched him away to take him to the wilderness, so the soldiers charged with killing the children of Bethlehem under two years old were enraged and killed Zacharias.

It is mentioned in (Mt 23:3). When the lawyer reached the age of thirty they gave him a key, a sign of his authority to teach others the knowledge of God, and the aim of the Law is the knowledge of the awaited Messiah, but they did not believe in Him, and by their teachings they also prevented others from believing, that is, they used their authority wrongly, so their punishment is severe.
They urge vehemently: they become enraged and bear malice against Him, and intend to wrong Him.
Provoke him to speak: they question Him and dispute with Him, hoping to make Him fall into some error.
To catch him: that is, to seize upon any word that condemns Him.
To accuse him before the rulers of the Jews that He is a blasphemer, or before the Romans that He is a agitator of the people.

The scribes, Pharisees and lawyers were enraged because Christ exposed their errors, and instead of repenting they tried to resist His words and to catch some fault in Him so as to try Him and prevent His teachings, which show their sins. Receive the voice of God on the lips of others if it shows your faults so that you may repent, and do not be vexed with them but thank them.
Hypocrisy, fear and concern for material things. Hypocrisy (vv. 1-3):

1- In the mean time, when there were gathered together an innumerable multitude of people, insomuch that they trode one upon another, he began to say unto his disciples "first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy. 2- For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known. 3- Therefore whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light; and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets shall be proclaimed upon the housetops."

It is mentioned in (Mt 16:6-12) that Christ directed His previous words to the scribes and Pharisees; now He turns to His disciples. This warning that follows is for them especially and for believers in general, and it is to guard against the sin of hypocrisy. Its clear example is the Pharisees, who represent the religious leadership of the Jews. They cared about the appearance of holiness, but inside they were full of evil, as is proved by their refusal to believe in Christ and even their attempt to catch Him in some error, because their pride refused to let the crowds leave them and follow Christ. He likened hypocrisy to leaven, because leaven gives a small piece of dough a large size, but the inside is only air bubbles. Leaven also works inside, away from the eyes, just as evil spreads inside the heart while the person shows an outward appearance of great holiness that is completely different from what is within him.

It is also mentioned in (Mt 10:26) that everything a person does of evil in this life will be made known on the day of judgment, in addition to the exposure of many of his sins as time passes during his life. Therefore there is no need for hypocrisy, which will be exposed and will reveal the shame of its owner.

It is mentioned in (Mt 10:27) that what the Pharisees do in secret will be exposed before the light of Christ, who knows what is in their hearts, and by the Gospel, which reveals the ugliness of the sin of hypocrisy.
"The housetops" means the loftiness of the proclamation of the Holy Spirit on the lips of the Apostles and preachers, who will expose sins, including hypocrisy.

It also means that the teachings of the disciples, which are spoken in secret to small numbers because of persecution, will gradually spread, and the time of peace will come when they will be proclaimed openly in the light and from high places such as the housetops, and many will hear them and believe.

Know that every evil you hide in your heart will be judged, so repent of it quickly, and keep away from the judging of others that you speak in secret. For everything will be exposed, and the one you judge may learn what you said about him in secret, and your relationship with him will worsen. Instead of evil talk, take care to speak about love and goodness, even with one person, and this love will gradually spread and be made known to all, and they will see it in your life and in the lives of those to whom you spoke of it.

entries.section: (2) Not fearing, and witnessing to Christ

paragraphs.text: My beloved, this is the first time that Christ uses this expression toward His followers. He declares that they are His own beloved ones, whom He distinguishes from the rest of the evil world and keeps safe from it.

Christ deals with the problem of fear, despising all the violence and persecution that men inflict on His children, since the limit of their persecution is harm to the body, but they cannot harm the spirit; on the contrary, the spirit clings to God and grows in knowing Him. But the One worthy of being feared is God, who has authority over the spirit and the body. If the soul fears Him, it is saved from eternal torment and no longer fears people, because God keeps it from dangers, and no trial befalls it except by His permission.

entries.section: (2) Not fearing, and witnessing to Christ

paragraphs.text: Two sparrows were sold for a farthing, which was the lowest coin in use, and if a person bought four sparrows for two farthings, a fifth sparrow was given to him as a gift, so that the five sparrows cost two farthings. This sparrow that is without price, that is, the gift, is not forgotten by God; rather, He cares for it and gives it its food.

The five sparrows point to the five senses. They look for their food on the earth and fall into the fowler's net, but when they rise to heaven they eat the fruit of the trees. That is, if the senses descend to earthly things the devil hunts them, and if they ascend to heaven they gain spiritual fruits.

entries.section: (2) Not fearing, and witnessing to Christ

paragraphs.text: Christ confirms His care for us, however weak we may be, or despised and worthless in the eyes of people like this sparrow. He even cares for the finest details of our lives: "the very hairs of your head are all numbered," that is, He knows their number and knows the details of every hair in them. Therefore there is no room for fear or anxiety, as long as our God loves us and cares for us to this degree.

entries.section: (2) Not fearing, and witnessing to Christ

paragraphs.text: Christ shows the importance of declaring faith, and not merely being convinced of it in the heart, and its reward is enjoying eternity, because whoever bears witness to Christ on earth, Christ bears witness to him in heaven and gives him a place in eternity. The opposite is also true: whoever denies Him on earth, Christ also denies him in heaven, that is, rejects him, and he goes to eternal torment.

Confessing Christ is not only by declaring that you are a Christian, but by showing the truth, supporting the oppressed, and Christian conduct in holding fast to God's commandments and enduring suffering for their sake.

entries.section: (2) Not fearing, and witnessing to Christ

paragraphs.text: Blaspheme against the Holy Spirit. If a person denies Christ he can repent and be forgiven; but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit, that is, rejects His work in him, which calls him to repentance, and remains persistent in sin all his life, will not be forgiven. For one who denies Christ may afterward respond to the work of the Holy Spirit in him, repent and regain his faith, but whoever refuses repentance has no salvation. Here appears the importance of the sacrament of repentance and confession, which is the only way to salvation.

entries.section: (2) Not fearing, and witnessing to Christ

paragraphs.text: Christ calls us not to fear the one who persecutes us, however violent he may be or however weak we may be, because the Holy Spirit works in us and teaches us what to say in these confrontations, as happened in the trials of the martyrs, and how they silenced the governors who tried them, however weak their education, intelligence or personalities. Do not be troubled by any confrontation in your life, but take refuge in prayer, confident of the power of God that is in you.

entries.section: (3) The parable of the rich fool

paragraphs.text: Disputes over inheritance often arise between brothers, and it was customary to ask the teachers to settle such cases. It seems that one of them was greedy and wanted to take a greater share of the inheritance than he deserved.

entries.section: (3) The parable of the rich fool

paragraphs.text: Christ refused to be a judge and a divider of the inheritance, because His aim is spiritual, namely the salvation of the soul, and not an earthly kingdom. By this they were also trying to catch Him in an error, namely that He had set Himself up as a civil judge without permission from the civil or religious authority.

entries.section: (3) The parable of the rich fool

paragraphs.text: "His life," that is, his happiness on earth, is a gift from God to His children.

Then Christ confronted the real problem in the strife among people, which is greed for material things, and He declared a clear truth: a happy life is not by money but by being with God. So why the love of money?

entries.section: (3) The parable of the rich fool

paragraphs.text: Christ told them a parable: a rich man had many fields, and in one year the produce of his land was greater than in all the past years, and so his barns could not hold it. He did not think of distributing this good to the needy, but was preoccupied with how to find many barns to hold all this good, to use it for himself alone.

entries.section: (3) The parable of the rich fool

paragraphs.text: "My fruits and my goods": he attributed the good to himself and did not thank God.
"Laid up for many years": this rich man forgot that he does not know when his life will end, and he supposed that he had many years ahead, so he did not prepare for his eternity by doing good.

"Eat, drink, and be merry": he thought that joy is in much eating and drinking and not in God, as if he were an animal concerned only with food, and not a human being with a spirit that is satisfied and rejoices in God.

This rich man thought of solving his problem by pulling down his barns and building greater ones to hold the fruit of his abundant crops. He felt reassured and glad, and told his soul to enjoy itself, since it had security in the abundance stored with him, enough fruit for the many years to come in his life.

entries.section: (3) The parable of the rich fool

paragraphs.text: "Thy soul shall be required of thee": you will die and your spirit will be separated and stand before the just Judge to be held to account for its preoccupation with material things instead of God.

"Whose shall those things be?": you will have no authority over all these goods you have acquired; rather they will be distributed to others, that is, those who inherit from you, and some of them may be people you do not want to give to. You will take nothing of them, and they will be given to others.
"Layeth up treasure for himself": he is selfish, gathering the goods of the earth for himself and not to give in charity to the needy, although he is rich and has much in excess.
"Not rich toward God": he did not care about loving God and worshipping Him, nor did he care about doing good to the needy, so as to lay up a treasure for himself in heaven.
On the day when the rich man thought these thoughts, God spoke to him, warning him that he would die that night and would not benefit from all these material goods.
So everyone who relies on material things without God is a fool and ignorant, who does not know how to live, because life is in God, who remains with him forever.
Ask yourself at the end of every day: how much was I occupied with the love of money, and how much time was I occupied with the love of God?
"Therefore": because of this, which He showed in the parable of the rich fool, the vanity of material things.

Christ confronts the problem of all people, which is attachment and preoccupation with material things, and calls them not to be concerned about food and clothing, directing their gaze to the purpose of all these means, which is the life that we should enjoy with God.

How strange it truly is that a person is occupied with the means rather than the goal, and so loses the goal. At the beginning of every day, remember your goal, which is the love of God, and leave aside the cares of the world and useless arguments.

Christ gives a clear example of not being concerned about food, namely the birds, of which He chose the ravens. Although they are unloved birds, and do not trouble themselves to provide their food, for they do not sow, nor reap, nor gather, nor care about preparing dwellings in which to live, yet God feeds them from the leftovers of the crops scattered in the world. If God cares for the birds, how much more for man, the head of all creation?
"That which is least": an increase in the height of one of you of about 50 cm is a small thing compared with the whole creation of man, which God made.
"The rest": the needs of man for food and clothing.

Then He gives a logical proof that we should not be anxious about food: however much a person is concerned, he cannot add one cubit to his stature (that is, about half a meter). If he cannot increase his height, he likewise cannot preserve his body; rather it is God who preserves it for him and provides for his material needs.
So man is unable to do the least thing, and therefore he must depend on God who created him and provides all his needs.
"They toil not, they spin not": she takes care to make her appearance and her clothing.

"O ye of little faith": a call to us to believe in God's fatherhood and in His provision for our lives, so that we are not anxious and occupied with our material needs. Christ gives us an example of not being concerned about clothing, namely the flowers with their beautiful colors and forms, which man tries to imitate, making his clothes like their colors and forms; but the original, the natural flowers, are better in appearance, for Solomon the king in all his glory, with his splendid clothing, did not reach the beauty of these flowers, that is, the lilies. These lilies are grasses, that is, plants that grow in the field for a few months, then dry up and are cast into the oven (the furnace). If God cares for them and gives them this beautiful form, will He not care about our clothing and our appearance if we believe in Him and rely on Him?
"Your Father": He declares God as a Father who cares for His children and knows all their needs.
"Shall be added": because God gives us life with Him, which is the most important, and then adds to it the needs of the body.

Here He gives the conclusion, which is not to be anxious about food and clothing, for the whole world runs after them; but we, the children of God, trust in our God who provides our needs, so that we seek what is more important, namely the reign of God over our hearts, and all material needs are a small thing that He calls the rest, and it is guaranteed from the hand of God who cares for us. Remember God's care for you and for all the creation around you, so that you do not worry about anything.

Christ calls His children who believe in Him the little flock, because the believers who walk according to His commandments are a minority, not only at the time of His presence on earth but even until now, since man is easily drawn to evil. But He reassures them that He is their Father and that they are distinguished from the whole world, because God has prepared the Kingdom for them and is glad to make them dwell in it.

Contemplate God's fatherhood: He is glad to give you the Kingdom, so that your heart may be at peace amid the afflictions of life, and this urges you to hold to His commandments in continual striving, so that you enjoy all that He has prepared for you.
"Sell": free yourselves from attachment to material things .... that is, sell them from your hearts.
"That ye have": all the material things you possess.
"Bags which wax not old": He likens the heavenly treasure to a bag that never perishes, in which are placed not silver and gold but works of mercy.
"A treasure in the heavens that faileth not": the nature of the world's wealth is that it is subject to decrease and ending, but the heavenly treasure remains forever.

Christ directs the attention of His children to how to prepare for the Kingdom, namely by giving alms to everyone in need, so that a person gives up all he has of money, health and various abilities and gives them in love to others. In this he transforms his material treasures, which are subject to theft and to corruption by time or insects, and sends these treasures to heaven by the work of mercy.
And by the work of mercy the treasure becomes one in heaven, so the heart is more attached to heaven, and increases in prayers and in doing good.

Christ also calls us to "let your loins be girded." The girdle is a leather belt tied around a person's waist so that he is ready for work. This belt is made from the skins of dead animals, so it signifies the death of the body to material attachments through fasting, detachment and the control of desires.
The preparation is completed by "lights burning." The lamp is the light that is in man, that is, the soul when it is enlightened by the love of God, spiritual worship and the acquiring of virtues.
"He shall gird himself": the master is Christ, who put on our body and girded Himself with it in order to bear in it all our sins and toils and to redeem us on the cross.

"Make them to sit down to meat": Christ gave rest to His children in His preaching on earth by healing the sick, casting out demons and feeding the crowds. All this is a symbol of the rest He gives them in the Kingdom, and of the great honor of their sitting in heavenly glory, and Christ serves them with His redeeming blood.
"Will come forth and serve them": when He was lifted up on the cross and shed His blood as a ransom for humanity. And He continues to serve them in the Kingdom with His blessings that never end.

Christ calls us to a fourth matter in preparing for the Kingdom, which is spiritual watchfulness, through the parable of a group of servants waiting for their master to return from the wedding, and He pronounces them blessed if they are watching.

These servants signify man's abilities and gifts, which await Christ who comes at His second coming from heaven, where His wedding with His angels is in joy and perpetual rejoicing. If the servants are always watching, they hasten to meet their master as soon as he knocks at the door, that is, calls them to end their life on earth and be with Him in heaven. Spiritual watchfulness is a person's attachment to spiritual worship and repentance and keeping away from the sources of sin, that is, constant concern for the salvation of the soul.

The master shows a love beyond the grasp of the mind, for he girds himself with a belt and comes forth and serves his servants himself. This signifies the love of Christ the Redeemer, who honors His believing children in the Kingdom and makes them glad by the merits of His blood shed on the cross, which He gave for their sake, and He glorifies them with Him forever.

Christ explains the importance of watchfulness in the previous parable: if the master comes in the second watch or the third watch of the night, that is, the second or third quarter of it, and finds them watching, he pronounces them blessed.

The first watch signifies childhood, the second manhood, and the third old age. So at whatever time God requires a person's soul, He finds him ready. He did not mention the first watch, because the child is lacking in understanding and in bearing responsibility for sin, so only the man or the old man is held to account. Also, it was not customary for anyone to return from a wedding in the first watch, which is from the beginning of the night at six in the evening until nine at night.

The second watch is from nine at night to twelve, that is, midnight, and the third watch from twelve to three in the morning. In ancient times it was also not customary to return in the fourth watch, which reaches six in the morning, that is, dawn.

This parable is mentioned in (Mt 24:42-44). "Broken through" means to dig and break into the walls of the house so that the thief enters through this breach and steals what he wants. He confirms the importance of watchfulness by another parable, which is guarding the house against thieves: since the master of the house does not know in what hour the thief will come, he must always watch so that his house is not broken into.

From all that has gone before, we must keep spiritual watchfulness, lest God require our lives at any time, or come at His second coming. Spiritual alertness means continual repentance, keeping away from the sources of sin, and attention to good works and service.
After Peter heard Christ's words about preparing for the Kingdom, he asked what was meant by the servants: were they Christ's disciples or all the crowds?

This parable is mentioned in (Mt 24:45-51). Christ answered Peter's question with another question, which He Himself will answer, namely who is the faithful and wise steward whom his lord sets over his servants.

The servants or attendants are the senses and abilities of man, and he is a steward over them to care for them and use them well. The servants also signify children, and parents are stewards from God to care for them and attend to their needs. Likewise the servants of the Church are responsible for caring for those they serve, whether children or adults.

So Christ's answer to Peter's question is that preparation for the Kingdom is directed to all the people and not only the Apostles; every person has responsibilities, is a steward over them, and must render an account of his stewardship to God.

Christ pronounces the faithful steward blessed, because he understood that his authority is taken from God and that he is only a steward, and so he was faithful in the details of his life. The reward of this steward is that the master sets him over all his goods, that is, gives him the eternal kingdom.
"My lord delayeth his coming": he neglects preparing for the Kingdom, forgetting that God may require him at any moment and end his life.
"To beat the menservants and maidens": he is harsh toward those he serves, so he has no sympathy for the needy or for sinners, and by his harshness he drives them away from the Kingdom.
"To eat and drink, and to be drunken": not only eating and drinking what his body needs, but being absorbed in drinking until drunkenness, that is, being immersed in material concerns.
"In a day when he looketh not for him, and at an hour when he is not aware": death comes suddenly to a person, at a time that the one who is not prepared for the Kingdom does not expect.
"Will cut him in sunder": will end his life.
"His portion": the reward of his life.

"The unbelievers": every unfaithful steward is unfaithful to his lord, and by them He means the wicked whom He casts into eternal torment, and by the unfaithful He also means the demons who disobeyed God.

But if the steward is unfaithful in caring for those he is responsible for, whether his senses or his children or those he serves in the Church, because of his absorption in his desires, this servant can expect nothing but his master's sudden coming to him to end his life and cast him with the wicked unfaithful into eternal torment.
It is understood from the above how important spiritual watchfulness is, by faithfulness in all the abilities that God has given us.

Christ makes clear that there are degrees in punishment and eternal torment. Whoever enjoyed the grace of the New Covenant and knew the love of Christ the Redeemer, and then violated His commandments, will be punished in eternity more than the one who committed the same errors but did not know Christ.

Whoever knows more about God and persists in sin, his punishment is severe; but whoever knows little about God or does not know God's commandments, his conscience is God's voice to him, and he is punished, but less than the former. If you have come to know the way of Christ and the Church, enjoy it, lest, if you neglect it, your punishment be fearful.

"Fire": the flame of the knowledge of the Holy Spirit in His children, which at the same time reveals the evil of the wicked, so they rise up against His children and persecute them; fire also signifies persecutions.

"Kindled": ignited, and this means the increase of the work of the Holy Spirit, who draws the hearts of many who sacrifice everything for His sake, since He was the first to bear these fires in His body by His death on the cross for the redemption of His children, so that they may learn from Him and take up their cross behind Him.

"Baptism" is the baptism of suffering that Christ accepted from His incarnation until the cross, so that all His believing children may walk the same way, enduring suffering for the sake of keeping His commandments and seeking all with love, bearing many toils like their Redeemer, until their love for Him is perfected and they depart to the paradise of bliss. "How am I straitened" means, I cannot but accomplish the redemption.
"Accomplished": the completion of the redemption.
These words are also mentioned in (Mt 10:34-36).

At the level of the family, when some of its members believe, the other members rise against him, and the believer endures because his love for God is greater than his love for people however close they are to him. So a division occurs within the family between believers and unbelievers, caused by the evil of the unbelievers, and there is no peace in the relationships within the family, but the believers keep their inner peace in Christ Jesus.

The two are the Jews and the Gentiles, against three, that is, the Christians who believe in the Holy Trinity. The father signifies Satan, who sets himself up as father of the world against his pagan son who became a Christian. The mother is the synagogue of the Jews against her daughter, that is, the Church made up of Jews who became Christians. The mother-in-law also signifies the synagogue of the Jews, against her daughter-in-law, that is, the Gentiles who became Christians. Christ gives the example of a family made up of five persons, so that it divides two against three, and in detail the father rises against his son, the mother against her daughter, and the mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law (the wife of her son), and the reverse is also true. Do you hold to God's commandments even if the members of your household oppose you? And do you endure suffering with joy for the sake of Christ?

The world depended on agriculture as its basic craft, and the farmer was accustomed to discerning the natural phenomena that affect his farming, such as the mist that rains upon the plants so that they grow, and the south winds that carry warmth that helps growth.

Spiritually, the rains signify heavenly graces, and the hot south wind signifies the work of the Holy Spirit. This is what was accomplished by the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption, as He poured out salvation upon humanity and gave them the Holy Spirit who renews their nature.

If man understands how to discern the condition of the weather and what it foretells, why did the Jews not understand the prophecies of the prophets about Christ, whom they saw before them? Of course there are reasons, namely man's pride and his immersion in material things, which makes him lose the spirit of discernment and wisdom.

As an extension of the lack of discernment, a person does not call himself to account for his sins so as to repent and return to God, that is, he refuses to submit to the divine truth and goes further into sin, justifying himself.

It also appeared in the Sermon on the Mount (Mt 5:25). He gives a practical example, namely a dispute with an adversary: if you do not reconcile with him, you will stand before the judge who will pass judgment on your fault and deliver you to the officer, who will cast you into prison, and you will not come out of it until justice has received its full due. If you had seized something, you will serve days in prison for it, down to the last farthing (the smallest coin).

Besides calling us to settle disputes with others and to keep away from the courts with all our strength, it signifies spiritually the dispute with God. The adversary is the commandment, or the conscience, or the Holy Spirit; the judge is God the Judge on the last day; and the officer, as the Gospel of Matthew puts it, is the angels who cast the soul into prison, that is, eternal torment. Since our sins are unlimited, because they are directed against the unlimited God, we will not be able to pay the last farthing, but will remain in torment forever.

Submit to God's commandments, to the voice of your conscience and to the work of the Holy Spirit; obey your father of confession and the teachings of the Church, and hold fast to a life of repentance, and you will be saved on the last day and enjoy the heavenly Kingdom.
A call to repentance and spiritual striving. A call to repentance (vv. 1-5):

1- There were present at that season some that told him of the Galilaeans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices. 2- And Jesus answering said unto them, "Suppose ye that these Galilaeans were sinners above all the Galilaeans, because they suffered such things? 3- I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

4- Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem? 5- I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish."

After Christ's talk mentioned in the previous chapter, some asked Him about Pilate, the governor of Judea, that is, the southern part of Palestine, and how he killed the Galilaeans, the inhabitants of its northern part, who were known for causing many disturbances. They had risen in a revolt calling for not submitting to Caesar, and it seems they were followers of Judas of Galilee (Acts 5:37). Pilate sent his soldiers to them while they were in the temple offering their sacrifices, and he killed them and mingled their blood with their sacrifices.

It seems there was a disagreement between the Pharisees, who did not incline to using violence against the authorities, and the sect of the Zealots, who did incline to it, and they differed in their judgment of this incident. The Pharisees considered them wicked men who deserved punishment, while the Zealots rose up against Pilate's unjust violence. Some thought that these Galilaeans were more wicked than the rest of the people, because God allowed them to be killed while they were offering their sacrifices in the temple, that is, He did not accept them. In addition, there was a common thought at that time that whoever is struck by a calamity suffers it because of his wickedness, and whoever is not struck is righteous. This is of course a mistaken thought, because God allows afflictions for His children in order to develop them spiritually, and He may give blessings to sinners in order to save them so that they repent.

Christ denied that the killing was a result of their sins being greater than those of others; truly they were sinners like others, but Christ called everyone to repentance, using this incident as a warning.

Not every sin has an earthly punishment, nor does a more severe earthly punishment mean the gravity of the sin. But may it be that when we hear of an affliction or meet one, it leads us to repentance, so that we are saved, not from temporal afflictions but rather from eternal torment.
Christ mentioned an incident that seems to have been recent and to have happened in Jerusalem, namely the fall of a tower upon a group of people who were in it, and eighteen of them died.
This was an affliction not caused by man, and He asked: were these Jews, do you suppose, more wicked than the rest of the Jews?
Christ answered His question in the negative, declaring that all are sinners, and that these incidents should call them to repentance and to preparing for eternity.
May we always prepare by repentance when we hear of any afflictions that befall others or of some falling into sins, and may we not judge them.

entries.section: (2) The parable of the barren fig tree

paragraphs.text: "A certain man": He is God, the owner of the vineyard.
The vineyard is life.
The fig tree represents the life of man.
The fruit is worship and good works.

Fruit trees are planted for the sake of their fruit, and if they bring no fruit they are of no use; likewise God created man to do good works, and if he has no such fruit there is no benefit in his existence in life.

entries.section: (2) The parable of the barren fig tree

paragraphs.text: "Seeking fruit": this means God's repeated asking of fruit from us. He always waits for it and comes to us through His warnings in the Holy Bible, through spiritual sermons, and through the virtues of those around us, which should move us to imitate them.
God was patient with the tree for three years, a long period, and it gave no fruit, so it deserved to be cut down, lest it draw nourishment and occupy a place to no purpose.
The first year signifies the life of humanity after the Fall, the second year is the age of the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and the third year is the age of the Law and the prophets.
In all this humanity was not saved from sin, and did not give the response of love that is required toward God.
Do not make light of God's longsuffering toward you, but seize the opportunity for repentance and good works, lest you destroy your life.

entries.section: (2) The parable of the barren fig tree

paragraphs.text: The vinedresser is Christ, who intercedes for humanity, and he also signifies the priest and the servant who care for souls, call them to repentance and help them with the means of grace.

"Let it alone this year also": signifies the era of grace, in which the soul believes and is saved, and it also signifies the rest of the life that it lives, for this is its opportunity for repentance.

"Dig about it": that is, dig around the tree to pull out the weeds and get rid of harmful insects. This signifies repentance and humility with all their striving, because the digging goes deep downward like humility, and examining the soil and cutting the weeds is the review of the soul through repentance and confession.
"Dung": this is the fertilizer given to the tree, which signifies spiritual food by being nourished through Holy Communion, reading the Holy Bible and prayers.

entries.section: (2) The parable of the barren fig tree

paragraphs.text: Christ's hope in you is that you bear fruit, like the vinedresser's hope in the fig tree. If you disappoint His hope, nothing awaits you but being cut down, that is, death, and then what is more than this, that is, going to eternal torment. Remember, as long as you are alive, that God loves you and expects fruit from you and helps you if you obey His commandments.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the bent woman

paragraphs.text: The temple was in Jerusalem, but the synagogues were spread throughout the land, where the Holy Scriptures were read and interpreted. Christ entered one of these synagogues on the Sabbath day, and it seems that the people expected Him to come to it, so some sick people came for Him to heal them and to hear His teachings, because He used to teach in these synagogues, since He came to fulfill the Law and the prophets.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the bent woman

paragraphs.text: A woman came to the synagogue who was afflicted with an illness that had bent her back for eighteen years, and this was from an unclean spirit (a spirit of infirmity), that is, the work of Satan, which made her look at the ground like animals, and not stand upright looking to heaven like other people.

The number ten signifies the commandments and the Law, and the number eight points to the Resurrection, which took place on the eighth day. So when the Law was completed with the Resurrection, that is, when eighteen years had passed, Christ healed her; that is, it is by Christ that the healing of humanity and its freedom from the authority of the devil is accomplished.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the bent woman

paragraphs.text: Christ commanded her by His word, that is, with the authority of His divinity, and she was loosed from her infirmity and her bending, and was freed from the authority of Satan, after He touched her with His hand, so she was healed immediately and praised God and glorified Him.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the bent woman

paragraphs.text: The ruler of the Jewish synagogue was indignant because he envied Christ, since hearts were attached to Him after this miracle, and he hid his envy under the cover of his adherence to the law of not working on the Sabbath, considering healing to be the work of a physician. And fearing to speak to Christ, he rebuked the people and told them to come to be healed on a day other than the Sabbath, although the woman had not asked Christ to heal her; rather it was He, in His love, who called her.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the bent woman

paragraphs.text: Christ rebuked the ruler of the synagogue for his hypocrisy, for he was not concerned about the Sabbath but envied Christ because of the people's love for Him; and healing is a miracle and not a work that violates the law.

And Christ gave a proof of this by which He put to shame the ruler of the synagogue and those with him of the Pharisees: that the law allows necessary works on the Sabbath day, such as loosing animals and taking them to water them.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the bent woman

paragraphs.text: All the more this Jewish woman, over whom Satan had held sway for eighteen years with the illness of bending, ought to be loosed on the Sabbath day, because this is a necessary need, and she is of course better than the animals. If an animal is tied up for the night only and we pity it for thirst and give it water, how much more does this woman, a daughter of Abraham, that is, a Jewess of the people of God, deserve mercy after Satan had bound her for 18 years and wearied her greatly.

entries.section: (3) The healing of the bent woman

paragraphs.text: The obstinate ones who were with the ruler of the synagogue were ashamed, and the crowds rejoiced at the miracles of Christ in healing them.
Do not be biased in your speech with people, but rejoice in the doing of good by any person and in every place.

entries.section: (4) The parables of the mustard seed and the leaven

paragraphs.text: He likens the Kingdom of God to a grain of mustard seed, which is a very small seed that, when cast into the ground and buried, comes up as a great tree. So the Church began small in Judea and then spread throughout the whole world. A person must be buried like a mustard seed, to rise with Christ as a great tree in which the birds of the air lodge, that is, all the spiritual people who praise God attach themselves to the believer.

entries.section: (4) The parables of the mustard seed and the leaven

paragraphs.text: After Christ gave a parable close to the minds of farmers, He gave another parable that women who make bread understand easily, namely putting leaven into flour, so that it ferments as the leaven spreads through all the dough, and it becomes fit to be made into bread.

So the word of God works within the soul, and "three" points to the body, soul and spirit. The leaven is the proclamation that has spread throughout the whole world, because the world came out of three, the sons of Noah, and the leaven is the proclamation of the Holy Trinity, which has become spiritual food for all the children of God.

Do not despise your weakness, for God is able to work through you so that you influence many, and your prayer and your reading, however little, will change your life. Persevere in holding fast to God and in serving Him.

Christ headed toward Jerusalem, where He would be crucified by the Jews for the redemption of humanity, and He taught in the cities and villages through which He passed, calling them to repentance and preparing them to bear the cross in readiness for the Kingdom.

One of the crowd asked Him about the number of those who reach the Kingdom, and He did not answer him, because it is a theoretical question that does not benefit the salvation of the soul. Then He directed the hearers' attention to how to be saved and reach the Kingdom, namely by spiritual striving, which He expressed as entering by the narrow door, which means bowing down, humility and detachment from material attachments so that we can pass through it. And He made clear that many will seek to enter by it and will not be able, because of their clinging to material desires and pride and their unreadiness for continual striving in prayers and fasts, bearing with others, and laboring in serving them.

He likens God to the master of the house who shuts this narrow door leading to the Kingdom, and this is what happens at the end of a person's life. After this, people try to enter, and God refuses, declaring that He does not know them, that is, that they are not His children, because they preferred the love of the world to the love of Him, and were careless about holding to His commandments, delaying until their lives ended.

The wicked reply and say that we had a relationship with You in our lives, O God, in our daily living (eating and drinking), and we heard Your teaching (You taught in our streets). These had an outward relationship in spiritual practices but without depth and without true love from the heart.

God affirms that He does not know these wicked ones, and asks them "whence you are," that is, that you are not My children but the children of the devil. He reminds them of their evils and of their wronging of others and of themselves by neglecting their salvation, as they walked in the way of sin, and He rebukes them to depart from Him and go to eternal torment.
He describes eternal torment as having in it severe grief, one of whose manifestations is weeping, and also terror and torment that no one can imagine, which is signified by the gnashing of teeth.

On the other side, in the Kingdom, sit the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and also the prophets whom the Jews know, in joy and rejoicing. The wicked Jews who refused to believe in Christ and to walk spiritually look at them and cannot enter to them, and they see with them many believers of Gentile origin who come from the whole world, that is, from the east and the west, and rejoice with the fathers and the prophets in the Kingdom.

Christ declares to His hearers who refuse to believe in Him that those who thought themselves first to enter the Kingdom, such as the Jews, will be far away in eternal torment because of their unbelief in Christ, and the others, such as the Gentiles or the simple Jews who believed in Christ, will be first to enter the Kingdom and enjoy being with God and the saints.
If you bear toils in striving and fight your desires, holding fast to Christ, God will raise you up and give you a leading place in the Kingdom.

Herod is Herod Antipas, the governor appointed by the Romans over Galilee and also Perea, where Christ was preaching at that time. He is the one who killed John the Baptist, and it was to him that Pilate sent Christ bound to be tried.

The Pharisees envied Christ because of the people's love for Him, and it seems they stirred up Herod against Him and frightened him with Christ's popularity and power, so they got from him a word that Christ should leave Jerusalem, so that Herod could be rid of Him without causing a disturbance and troubles among the people. The Pharisees pretended to love Christ and to want to protect His life from Herod's violence, but they were deceivers who wanted to be rid of Christ.

Christ likened Herod Antipas to a fox, for he is deceitful and hard of heart, and declared that He did not fear him, sending with the Pharisees a strong message to him that He would continue His care for His people by casting out demons and healing the sick until He completed His work of redemption, announcing His resurrection on the third day.

The expression "today and tomorrow, and the third day I shall be perfected" was a well-known expression among the Jews, meant to indicate a short period; that is, the three days point to the nearness of the end of His preaching.
"Today and tomorrow" and what follows do not mean a few days, but the period in which He preaches, which is short because the completion of the redemption has drawn near.

"It cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem", where the Sanhedrin sits, the supreme Jewish council which unjustly judges the prophets and kills them, or judges Christ and crucifies Him?? This saying does not mean all the prophets, but most of them perish in Jerusalem.
Christ confirms His continuing in the care of His people until He dies in Jerusalem, which destroyed many of the prophets sent by Him.
It is also mentioned in (Mt 23:37-39).

Christ reproaches Jerusalem, that is, the Jews who dwell in it, because of their great shedding of the blood of the prophets, and declares His love for it throughout history and until now, and His attempt to gather its children and care for them with His love, as a hen lovingly gathers her chicks under her wings because of their weakness and their need for warmth; but sadly the Jews refused to listen to God's word and to believe in Him.
God's grace is ready to save you from all your troubles and sins, so respond to it and enjoy God's embrace.
"Ye shall not see me": because Christ will die and rise and ascend to heaven, and they will not see Him going about preaching among them after that.

"Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord": a prophecy from Christ that of the Jews who refuse to believe in Him, some will afterward believe and declare their faith that Jesus is the awaited Messiah, blessed by God, who comes from heaven in the name of the Lord for the salvation of the world.
Christ declares the regrettable truth, which is the desolation of Jerusalem because of its pride, its stubbornness and its unbelief, that perhaps the Jews may return and believe.

And another truth: the Jews' unbelief that He is the Christ the Saviour; but a time will come when the rest of the Jews will believe and declare their faith, saying, "Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord."
The healing of the man with dropsy. The last place at the table. Like the supper of the lord, and counting the cost. The healing of the man with dropsy (vv. 1-6):

1- And it came to pass, as he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day, that they watched him. 2- And, behold, there was a certain man before him which had the dropsy. 3- And Jesus answering spake unto the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day? 4- "And they held their peace. And he took him, and healed him, and let him go; 5- And answered them, and said, "Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day? 6- "And they could not answer him again to these things.

One of the rulers of the Pharisees invited Christ to a feast on the Sabbath day, not in order to honor Him but to catch Him in some error so as to cast doubt on Him among the people or stir up the authorities against Him. Christ accepted the invitation because He does not fear their schemes, and to seize the opportunity to do good or to teach them the truth; for He seeks the salvation of all. Do not be disturbed by the plots of those around you, for God protects you from them, and continue doing good and showing love to them for Christ's sake.

Jesus found before Him a man sick with dropsy, which is the retention of quantities of water in the body, so that it swells and does not benefit from drinking water, because the water does not reach its organs but is stored up to no purpose. Perhaps this man had heard of Christ's coming and came to be healed.

"The lawyers" are those concerned with applying the Law, and they were present in the house of the Pharisee ruler. Christ knew what was in the hearts of the Pharisees and the lawyers, their attempt to catch Him in some error, so He asked them whether it is lawful to heal on the Sabbath as a good work or not, to teach them that the Lord's day is a freeing from material works so that we may fill it with worship and doing good.
"He took him": to show His compassion and tenderness toward him.

"Let him go": so that he might return to his house and be kept away from the Pharisees' rebukes of him for being healed on the Sabbath day. The lawyers were unable to prove from the Law their wrong idea of not doing good on the Sabbath, so they were silent. And Christ was not hindered by their thoughts from doing good, so He took the sick man and healed him, then let him go enjoying health and freedom from the illness.

Christ confirmed to them the necessity of doing good on the Sabbath, by the proof that the Law provides that if someone's ox or ass falls into a pit, he will pull it out so that it does not die (Deut 22:4); how much more people, whom we should pity and help on the Sabbath day. And they were also unable to answer Him because of the strength of His argument.

The Pharisees felt that they were better than others, so they were eager to sit at the tables of feasts in the chief places at the head of the table. In order to treat this pride in all people, which He may have noticed at the supper of this Pharisee who hosted Him, He told the following example.

If you are invited to a wedding feast, do not sit in the places of honor, lest the master of the wedding come and ask you to leave this place because a person of better standing has come after you, and you are ashamed and leave the place and go to a less honorable one. For if a person thinks he is better than others, the Lord will bring the humble and put them in heaven in his place, while he goes far away, contrary to what he supposed.

Christ advised His hearers that a person should seek the lowest room in humility, feeling that he is less than others, and because Christ humbled Himself by His incarnation and His death on the cross. If you take the lower place, you find Christ beside you, that is, you feel His presence with you and He fills your heart. But if the master of the wedding calls you to a better place, thank him; there is no objection to taking the better place, and you receive it as a grace from God that you do not deserve. Of course, do not take the last place with the aim that the host will honor you before everyone, so that your humility is seen and you become puffed up with pride in the virtue of humility, for this is hypocrisy and false humility.
And the host's bringing you forward to a better place means that God honors you and glorifies you before all creation on the day of judgment.
Christ declared the truth plainly, that the proud one who exalts himself is brought low by God, but whoever seeks humility, God exalts him and honors him.

Humility and hiddenness in your dealings with others are not a giving up of a better place, but a spiritual wisdom, because, away from the outward greatness before people, you experience Christ and feel His presence with you. By your humility you are the wisest of people, because you are seeking the most important thing, which is the companionship of God, given only to the humble. And do not be distressed if people neglect you and you feel alone and isolated, but seek God and seize this opportunity for more prayers and readings, and God will reveal Himself to you and you will rejoice in Him with a joy that cannot be expressed.

Christ directed His words to those who give feasts, that they should not invite their great friends so as to be repaid with similar feasts in their houses; in this way feasts become a business, for they take in return for what they give, and there is no giving in them to the needy. Nor should feasts be an occasion for boasting of the abundance of food and the arrangements of the feast; whoever does this also receives his reward, which is the praise of people, and he has no reward with God.
But this does not mean that love feasts for relatives and friends are rejected, if their purpose is love and fellowship and the sense of God's presence in their midst.
"The maimed": those whose noses or one of their limbs have been cut off, so they are disfigured and hindered from ordinary work, and therefore poor.
"The resurrection of the just": that is, the last day, when the righteous are rewarded in the Kingdom of Heaven, and the wicked are cast into eternal torment.

Christ advised inviting the poor, whether the weak and disfigured (the maimed) or the lame and the blind, and everyone who appears poor or of lower standing in society, for these are unable to make similar feasts, and in this way your feast is love without return, and God repays you for it with the heavenly reward, that is, He honors you and hosts you in the Kingdom of Heaven.

Be concerned with giving without return, that is, do not hope for repayment from all those around you, for the heavenly reward is better than every earthly return. And serve not only those who are poor materially, but rather the weak and disfigured spiritually by the multitude of sins, the lame who cannot walk in the way of the Kingdom, and the blind who do not see God because of their absorption in the desires of the world.

entries.section: (4) The supper and the invited guests

paragraphs.text: It seems that one of the Pharisees or Jews rejoiced at Christ's words about the heavenly reward for whoever invites the poor, so he praised whoever eats bread in the Kingdom of Heaven, because his idea of heaven was material, as he thought that there is eating and drinking there as in the world.

entries.section: (4) The supper and the invited guests

paragraphs.text: "Bade": accepting the invitation is preparing for life with God, not the life itself, as shown by the fact that many accepted the invitation but at the time of fulfillment refused for many reasons, as happens today, when many declare their faith in theory but at the practical application in worshipping God and loving others they make excuses for different reasons.
On this occasion Christ gave a parable about preparing for the heavenly Kingdom: a certain man made a great supper, and bade many.

This man signifies God, who made a supper by His death on the cross, and the offering of His Body and Blood on the altar every day in the Church, which is the pledge of the spiritual heavenly feast that He gives to His children in heaven. And He bade many, for He died for the redemption of the whole world, for He is the one "who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth" (1 Tim 2:4).

entries.section: (4) The supper and the invited guests

paragraphs.text: "His servant": that is, Christ, who took the form of a servant by His incarnation, and came to call people to the feast of His most holy Body and Blood, which He accomplishes on the cross. The servant also signifies the Apostles, who call people to the Church and to preparing for the Kingdom.
"For all things are now ready": the Church is open and in it are the Body and Blood of the Lord, and it awaits the believers to be united with Him.

entries.section: (4) The supper and the invited guests

paragraphs.text: "All" means most of those invited first, who are the Jews, the people of God.
"With one consent": they agreed to neglect faith in Christ, being occupied with material things and honor.
Five yoke of oxen signify the five senses, that is, the desires of the senses.

When the invited were called they excused themselves from coming; God calls us to repentance many times and we refuse. The excuses were very foolish: the first excused himself because he had bought a piece of ground and wanted to see it, although examining fields is not done at night at suppertime.
And this first one signifies those absorbed in earthly things and the love of possessions.

The second excused himself because he had bought five yoke of oxen and wanted to prove them. This also is not done at suppertime but in the daytime, and he signifies those occupied with bodily desires.
The third excused himself because of his marriage. He signifies those occupied with the world and its ties.
And these three point to those of the Jews who refuse God, because God called them first and they refused, and then He called the Gentiles afterward.
Examine the excuses you tell yourself to justify your keeping away from the Church, prayers and service, lest they be foolish and make you lose the Kingdom.

entries.section: (4) The supper and the invited guests

paragraphs.text: God, the master of the supper, was angry at the refusal of the Pharisees, the priests and the rulers of the Jews to accept His invitation to salvation, and He sent to call the common Jews, the poor and simple, and likewise the Gentiles, to His Kingdom, and gathered them from their lowly places in the streets and lanes to raise them by His love to heaven.

entries.section: (4) The supper and the invited guests

paragraphs.text: The servants, that is, the Apostles, did as God commanded them, and many of the simple Jews and the Gentiles came into the faith, so the Apostles told God all about their service and that there is still room in the Kingdom, that is, the blood of Christ is offered for the salvation of all if they believe.

entries.section: (4) The supper and the invited guests

paragraphs.text: "The highways and hedges" are places outside the cities and signify the distant Gentiles.
"That my house may be filled": because God rejoices to receive all believers in His Kingdom.

"None of those men which were bidden": none of those men invited earlier at the beginning of the parable who refused to come to the supper, that is, life with God on earth; these have no place in the Kingdom of Heaven.

God sent His servants a second time to "compel" the poor who are far from God, that is, to encourage them and support them strongly, since from the extremity of their weakness they have fallen into despair and need support; for He seeks the salvation of all the distant ones who do not know the way to the Kingdom, but as for those who know and refuse, God affirms that He will not bring them into His Kingdom. God has pity on the weak and sinners, seeks them and supports them and urges them on in the way of the Kingdom, but He hates stubbornness, recklessness and making light of sin.

"Great multitudes went with him": Christ was on His way from Galilee to Jerusalem, and the people of the cities and villages came out to Him and followed Him to hear His teachings and to be healed of their diseases.

In order to resist superficiality in the lives of His followers, Christ set conditions for salvation and asked us to examine ourselves by them, for they are the cost of obtaining salvation. Although salvation is free by the blood of Christ, He gives it only to those who strive spiritually. The first condition in spiritual striving is that we love God with all the heart, and love our relatives and dear ones whom God has given us, but if our love for anyone or for ourselves hinders us from God, let us hate it and reject it. So we love people and ourselves through God and for the sake of God who gave them to us.

The second condition in spiritual striving is bearing the cross, that is, enduring suffering for holding fast to the faith, and likewise the striving of spiritual worship and service, and in this we become Christ's disciples.

Christ gave an example of counting the cost: a man who wants to build a tower reckons whether he has the cost of building, lest he lay the foundation and be unable to finish the building, and people mock him because he wasted his money in vain and reached nothing.

The spiritual person who wants to build a tower, that is, a spiritual relationship that ties him to heaven, must lay the foundation, which is faith in Christ, and be ready to strive in prayers and fasts, in holding to the commandments, and in repentance with contrition; then the demons, his enemies, will not mock him.

So whoever wants to follow Christ asks himself whether he is ready not to be occupied with love of himself and attachment to others, and likewise whether he is ready for detachment and for enduring suffering for the sake of the faith!

If so, let him go forward with confidence in the spiritual life; but whoever is moved by Christ's words while his heart is attached to the love of the world and to emotional attachments that distract him from God will not be able to complete his way with God. Christ's call to count the cost is not to frighten His followers with the difficulty of the way, but to urge them to prepare by making Him their only goal and being bound to His love, so that they are assured of reaching the Kingdom and enjoying His ever-joyful companionship.

The other parable on counting the cost is of a king who has an army of ten thousand soldiers and is going to fight another whose force is twenty thousand soldiers; he should first think whether he has the means to win or make peace, so as not to be exposed to defeat and death. The meaning is that this warring king should examine his strength: is he able to face the enemy's army? Likewise whoever wants to walk with God should examine his readiness to leave his attachment to material things and to people for God's sake, so that he succeeds in overcoming all his desires and the adverse circumstances of life, and thus is assured of reaching the Kingdom.

The warring king with ten thousand soldiers signifies the spiritual person; the number ten points to the commandments, and the thousand to heaven. The spiritual person fights with God's commandments and with attachment to eternity, but the enemy, Satan, fights with twenty, a war divided into two parts: the first part, signified by ten, a complete war, consists of the blows on the right, which are exaggeration in worship and good works for the purpose of pride; and the second part, signified by the second ten, also a complete war, consists of the blows on the left, which are all kinds of sins and desires.

If a person feels that he is weak, he must be reconciled with God so that God may be his strength and he may overcome the demons; he sends the intercession of the saints, that is, the embassy, and repents of his sins and so makes peace with God.

It is also possible for the warring king with ten thousand to signify the spirit, and the enemy king who has twenty thousand to signify the body, so the person examines himself: is the spirit strong and able to overcome the body and lead it in the way of the spiritual life?
