paragraphs.text: Zacchaeus rejoiced greatly, and came down and opened his house to receive Christ in it.

entries.section: (6) The healing of the blind man on the way to Jericho

paragraphs.text: Zacchaeus was a symbol of evil in the city, so the crowds were astonished at Christ's entering to him and mingling with him. But Christ was seeking His repentant children, however much bad reputation He bore, in order to save them. This is the feeling of the servant who does not look for people's opinion of him but for God's opinion and the salvation of souls, whatever sufferings and troubles he bears.

entries.section: (6) The healing of the blind man on the way to Jericho

paragraphs.text: The faith of Zacchaeus did not stop at trying to see Christ; rather, when He granted him the grace of entering his house, his feelings were moved to repentance, and he expressed it in practice by rejecting the love of money. He promised to distribute half of his goods to the needy, in addition to his repentance for every wrong he had done to any person, and so he applied the Law by restoring fourfold. Let your repentance be practical, by repairing the effects of your sins and walking in the virtue opposite to the sin into which you fell.

entries.section: (6) The healing of the blind man on the way to Jericho

paragraphs.text: Christ declared His joy at the salvation of Zacchaeus and his household, for he had become a true son of Abraham by his practical faith, after having been a son in name only because he was a Jew. He also declared the purpose of His Incarnation and the purpose of all His servants, which is to seek the sinners who are far off so that they may repent and be saved from eternal torment, because they are all God's children.
As they heard these things: He means His talk concerning Zacchaeus.

Immediately appear: quickly, so that He would set up His kingdom in Jerusalem and defeat the Romans, because they thought that the Messiah was an earthly king. While Christ was heading with His disciples to Jerusalem, they were expecting that He would reign as an earthly king in Jerusalem, so Christ seized this opportunity to speak to them about preparing for the true Kingdom of God in eternity.
A certain nobleman is Christ, because He is the true God who became incarnate for our salvation. A far country, that is, heaven, to receive again His kingdom and glory.
Return: He comes back in His second coming to judge the whole world.
Ten servants represent all God's children who believe in Him in the world, because the number ten is the number of perfection.

Ten pounds: the pound (mina) is a silver coin equal to 100 drachmas. The number 100 signifies great perfection, so the pound signifies the word of God and His great gifts that He has given us. Occupy till I come: until He returns to them in His second coming on the day of judgment and repays each one according to his works.
Occupy: use your abilities that I have given you and strive spiritually to obtain spiritual fruits of worship, virtues and various services.
His citizens signify His human children, created in His image and likeness, who reject Him, and signify more particularly the Jews, from whom He was born and who rejected His message.
A message (ambassadors): that is, the Jews who persecuted the Apostles and everyone who preaches Christ after His ascension.
When he was returned: the second coming of Christ.

Having received the kingdom: after receiving the kingdom after His reign in heaven, that is, His being raised up in the Ascension until His second coming. Commanded to be called unto him: He gathers His children to hold them to account on the day of judgment.

The money: the abilities He gave to each one, or the word of God which moved them to spiritual striving. That he might know: to declare his righteousness and reward him, or his wickedness and repay him.
What he had gained by trading: the extent of his spiritual striving and what he has reached.

After the completion of redemption on the Cross and the binding of the devil, and after the time of this life, the day of judgment comes, on which men are held to account for the extent of their faithfulness in their earthly life.
The first: each one is judged alone and does not depend on his relationships with others, so that divine justice may be fulfilled.

Thy pound: in humility he attributed the pound to God and not to himself, and therefore the spiritual growth he reached is from God, and he did not attribute to himself his labor and spiritual striving.
Ten: the perfection of the gain.

The one who gained ten pounds signifies God's servants who labored much for Him, in whom the word of God worked with power and perfection, or any Christian who lived in righteousness and godliness, whether in the world or in monastic life.

Christ praised the one who gained ten pounds and described him as good and faithful, and rewarded him with authority over ten cities, that is, ten souls, which are the souls he gained by his service, so that they enjoy with him eternal bliss. For the servant has no aim in the possessions of this world; his only aim is the salvation of souls, and so he will be in heaven advanced, like a chief over others and near to God, enjoying His glory; he leads others in praising God and serving Him like the archangels or the rank of the Principalities among the angels.

The one who gained five pounds signifies the godly person who by the word of God sanctified his five senses, so God rewarded him with authority over five cities, that is, all his senses, meaning the enjoyment of eternal bliss, and he will be in heaven advanced and a leader of a group of souls in praising God, but in a lower position than the first, because the first one's striving was greater, so he deserved a better place and enjoyed God more.
It is to be noticed in this parable that all the servants received one pound, and one was distinguished from another by the measure of his faithfulness in investing the word of God and his abilities.

But in the parable of the talents mentioned in (Mt 25:14-30), the abilities from God given to each one differ from the other's, and consequently each one is held to account according to what he received, to teach us to be faithful in what we have received, for we shall be called to account for it, whether much or little. So let us not be proud if we have received much, nor grieve and be small in our own eyes if we have received little, for the lesson lies in faithfulness and not in the abundance or fewness of our abilities.

The one who laid up the pound in a napkin is the wicked person who was immersed in the sins of the world and shut the word of God up and prevented it from working in him. Since he separated himself from the word of God, he lost his spiritual sense because of his sloth in striving, so that he did not repent but condemned God as austere, exploitative and unjust, taking up what He laid not down. It is noticed that He mentioned the accounting of only three of his servants and not the ten, for His purpose is to show the kinds of men and the manner of God's reckoning with them.

God the Judge answered him with severity and justice, "Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee." Since you knew that I was expecting profit and gain from the pound I gave you, why did you not trade with it, by your faithfulness in carrying out the commandments, or service and seeking the souls that are far off, or the least striving in trying to carry out the commandment? For the bankers used to give them money and then recover it with interest (usury), so the least trading is to put the money with the bankers to gain even a little. That is, this man refused any spiritual striving, immersed in his wicked lusts.

Christ commanded that the pound, that is, the word of God, be taken from the wicked servant and given to the one who gained ten pounds, who is the servant who entered the Kingdom with many souls with him, so He gave him in addition glory and extra honor in the Kingdom, which the owner of this pound would have enjoyed.

Christ comments that whoever has love and faithfulness in obeying the commandment is given and increased by God in this life and in the age to come, but whoever has no love and obedience to the commandment, everything God granted him is taken from him and he is cast into eternal torment.

All the people who by their sins refused that Christ should reign over them will be judged before His glory on the day of judgment, and they will be slain, that is, they will die not once but will suffer death and torment forever in the eternal fire. God has given you a trust like the rest of His children, so be faithful in your time, your abilities and your gifts, and learn from those who strive around you, so that you become zealous like them and experience God's fellowship on earth, and then rejoice all the more in heaven.
Christ went on with His disciples, going up to Jerusalem because it is built on a mountain, to accomplish there the salvation of mankind by His death on the Cross.
Bethphage: a town near Jerusalem where the priests lived.
Bethany: a town near Jerusalem which was a dwelling place of the people. For Christ came for the salvation of all, and everyone shares in your service.

The Mount of Olives is located beside Jerusalem, and it points to the Church in which His believing children are planted, full of peace, because the olive tree signifies peace, and they also give oil, which is the work of the Holy Spirit dwelling in them and overflowing from them. So Christ draws near to the Church in which He proclaims His salvation.

And He sent two of His disciples to share with Him in the work of salvation, even if it was a small work, for God rejoices in it. Two is a number that represents love, since God makes the two one in the sacrament of marriage.
In sum, God rejoices in the love offered by His children.
You ought to rise above earthly things to share with Christ in His sufferings, and so rejoice in His salvation.
The village over against you: it is Bethphage.

A colt tied: on which no one had ever sat, and it signifies mankind far from God, over which God had not reigned but which wandered in its own lusts and did not bear the sufferings of spiritual striving. In the Gospels of Matthew and Mark it is mentioned that it was a colt and an ass, that is, a female donkey, while in the Gospel of Luke the emphasis is on the colt and the mention of the ass that was with it is omitted.
Loose him: He asked His two disciples to loose the colt, meaning to loose it from the bonds of the world so that Christ may reign over it.

If any man ask you why you loose him: the owners of the colt or their neighbors would object to the colt's being loosed, and they signify those who object to the salvation of God's children when they leave their wicked lusts, but Christ's asking for these souls and His support silences them.
The Lord hath need of him: how great is the humility of Christ, who declares His need for the colt; He needs, in His fatherly love, to save mankind.

In obedience and trust in God, the two disciples carried out what Christ commanded them, despite the difficulty of this by human logic, since they would be regarded as thieves in the eyes of the colt's owners; but when they obeyed and said the words of Christ, that the Lord had need of him, the owners let the colt go with them. It appears that God had given a sign to the colt's owners so that they would not object to its being taken, and the sign is the word, "The Lord hath need of him." The owners may have been acquaintances and lovers of Christ.
If only you would obey the commandment however hard it seems, confident of its blessing and of God's help and truthfulness.

When they brought the colt to Jesus, the two disciples took off their garments and put them on it to make it easy for Christ to ride. Taking off garments means submission, for the slave would take off his garment for the one who bought him, declaring his submission to him. Love makes a person give up even his garments, that is, his necessary needs, and he feels that what he gives up is a small offering, and so his whole life is blessed by Christ.

The disciples and the crowds vied with one another in spreading their garments on the road to be trodden by the feet of the colt on which Christ rode. On the one hand, the crowds declare their submission and their need that Christ, the great King, reign over them; and on the other, the feet of the colt (which signifies far-off mankind when Christ reigned over it) became a blessing to all people, as happens with God's holy children who have become a light to the world.
The mighty works which they had seen: the great miracles Christ did throughout His life, especially strong ones such as raising the dead.
The King that cometh in the name of the Lord: the awaited Messiah who comes to reign over the hearts of His children.

When He came to the Mount of Olives, which signifies the Church, the cries of His children burst forth in rejoicing, asking for His salvation and His reign over their hearts, because of their faith in His great miracles and the sharing of heaven and the angels who glorify Him.
The Pharisees were enraged at the Jews' glorifying Christ as a great king and asked Him to silence them, but He replied to them that if they held their peace, the stones would cry out.
The stones cry out: when their eyes were darkened from seeing Him as King over their hearts and they crucified Him, the stones cried out in that the rocks were rent.

The stones also signify the Gentiles who worship stones (idols), whose hearts are like stones, far from God; but if the Jews hold their peace and refuse to believe, the Gentiles will believe and glorify God.
And this is what happened during the preaching of the Apostles such as St. Paul the Apostle.

Christ looked at Jerusalem, and saw by His divine foreknowledge its rebellion against Him and His crucifixion, and the resistance of the priests and Pharisees to the preaching in His name at the hands of the Apostles, and in the end its destruction at the hands of Titus, the Roman commander, in AD 70, and the killing of those in it. He did not want its destruction, and so He grieved over it and expressed His feelings as a man by weeping. This is the second time that Jesus wept: the first was at the tomb of Lazarus, and the third time will come in the garden of Gethsemane, just before His arrest.
If thou hadst known: would that you knew.
The things which belong unto thy peace: that is, faith in Christ, so that you may receive peace.
They are hid from thine eyes: you hid faith from yourself because of your sins.

Christ cried out to Jerusalem in sorrow that it did not know the way to its true peace, for it had sought it in pride and material lusts which hid the truth from it, which is that peace is in faith in Christ and submission to Him so that it might receive its salvation.
A trench: barriers and walls placed around Jerusalem to obstruct and prevent the Jews' escape from it during the siege.

Christ describes what would happen at the destruction of Jerusalem at the hands of the Romans, who would besiege it until it fell into their hands, and would storm it and kill the Jews in it and tear down the temple and all its buildings, because it did not seize the opportunities of repentance that God sent to it, until He finally visited it with His only Son, but it rose up against Him and crucified Him. If only you would not waste the opportunities of God's visiting you with repentance, so that you escape all evils and keep your peace and inward joy.

entries.section: (5) The cleansing of the temple and Christ's teaching in it

paragraphs.text: Although Christ saw all the stubbornness of the Jews and what they would do to Him in His sufferings and crucifixion, He did not cease positive action. When He entered the temple of Solomon on Monday, that is, the day after His entry into Jerusalem (noting that Luke does not care about the order of events as Mark the Evangelist does), He found the priests and temple servants occupied in its courts with trade and material gain, and consequently the whole people occupied with material things, leaving spiritual worship. So He began to drive all these traders out of the temple courts.

entries.section: (5) The cleansing of the temple and Christ's teaching in it

paragraphs.text: Christ declared to the priests and to all the people that the house of God is set apart for prayer, but their preoccupation and their exploitation of the temple for trade had made it a den of thieves, since they stole hearts from the love and worship of God into immersion in the love of material things.
Beware of using your going to church as an occasion for any other business or human meetings that distract you from the love of God, or you will become a thief in His sight.

entries.section: (5) The cleansing of the temple and Christ's teaching in it

paragraphs.text: Christ was not content with driving the wicked out of the temple, but went on proclaiming His satisfying spiritual teachings in the temple every day, in the hope of rescuing some souls from the coming destruction. But sadly the chief priests, the scribes and the leaders of the people opposed Him instead of helping Him, because they were seeking their positions and their honor, so they did not benefit from His teachings and repent.

entries.section: (5) The cleansing of the temple and Christ's teaching in it

paragraphs.text: They could not find what they might do: they found no reason by which to arrest Him or stop His teachings.
Despite the malice of their hearts and their words of opposition to Christ, the crowds continued to cling to Him and to His life-giving words, and all their opposition failed.
Continue doing good however much the wicked oppose you, for God will support you and give you favor in the eyes of people. Mutual questions: the authority by which Christ works (vv. 1-8):
This discourse is also found in (Mt 21:23-27; Mk 11:27-33).

1- And it came to pass, that on one of those days, as he taught the people in the temple, and preached the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came upon him with the elders, 2- and spake unto him, saying, "Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?" 3- And he answered and said unto them, "I will also ask you one thing; and answer me: 4- The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?" 5- And they reasoned with themselves, saying, "If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not? 6- But and if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us: for they be persuaded that John was a prophet."
7- And they answered, that they could not tell whence it was. 8- And Jesus said unto them, "Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things."

entries.section: (5) The cleansing of the temple and Christ's teaching in it

paragraphs.text: Christ continued His positive work of preaching and teaching in the temple, and the opposition of the Jewish leaders to Him did not cease, so the chief priests and elders gathered around Him and asked Him by what authority He worked miracles and taught, and who gave Him this authority.

Their question was not for inquiry but to expose His error, for their hearts were filled with envy and malice. They meant that He was not of the tribe of Levi or the descendants of Aaron, who were responsible for the service in the temple, but of the tribe of Judah, so how could He perform this service without having taken permission from the high priest or the civil authority.

entries.section: (5) The cleansing of the temple and Christ's teaching in it

paragraphs.text: Christ did not convince them of His divine authority and did not answer them, because their question was an attack to catch Him in an error and not for sound understanding.

Therefore Christ replied to them with another question: if they answered Him, He would answer their question. This question was whether the baptism of John was sent from heaven or was a worthless human invention. His question was not an evasion of answering theirs, because if they answered His question by acknowledging John's message and baptism, they would thereby declare their faith in all that John said about Him, namely that He has complete divine authority and is the Judge of the whole world.
Keep away from foolish discussions, that is, unprofitable ones, when you are sure of the bad intention of the one who asks or argues, so that you keep your peace.

entries.section: (5) The cleansing of the temple and Christ's teaching in it

paragraphs.text: They reasoned with themselves: they stepped aside and consulted how to answer Him, because His question embarrassed them and exposed their error.

The leaders felt embarrassed, because if they agreed that it was from heaven, their envy and pride would be exposed, which had kept them from declaring their faith in John's baptism and submitting to him; and on the other hand, if they said it was of men, that is, that John was merely an ordinary man and not sent by God, the Jews would rise against them, because John was in everyone's eyes a great prophet.

entries.section: (5) The cleansing of the temple and Christ's teaching in it

paragraphs.text: In their bewilderment and embarrassment, they were forced in shame to declare their ignorance, so they said that they did not know. This meant their weakness and their inability to judge by what authority Christ teaches, because the power of His teaching and His many miracles confirm His divinity, but because of their wickedness they oppose Him. Then Christ said to them, "Neither tell I you," the source of my power. Thus He exposed their weakness and got free of the unprofitable dispute.
A certain man: is God.
The vineyard: is mankind and the world which He created.
The husbandmen: are the shepherds in the Old Testament, that is, the priests and the leaders of the people, the scribes, Pharisees and lawyers, to whom God entrusted the care of His people.

Went into a far country for a long time: that is, He gave them complete freedom throughout their lives; for He is present in every place and time, but He left them to do as they wished as though He were far from them.

At the season: it is the time of harvest and gathering the fruits, and it means that after He had given the Jewish priests sufficient opportunity to care for the people and teach them, He sent to ask for the souls who believe in Him and live with Him, that is, He asks for worship, godliness and conduct befitting His children.
A servant: conscience, or some of the prophets.

Beat him, and sent him away empty: they silenced people's consciences and distorted them and did not respond to God; or they opposed the prophets and wearied them and did not respond to their teachings.
After He had left them for a sufficient time, He sent to ask for the virtues, the righteousness and the life of His children, and He sent His servants to demand these fruits.

The first servant: is conscience, that is, the voice of God within us calling us to righteousness, but the wicked rejected it and tormented it and did not give it what it called for, like Cain, who rejected the voice of his conscience to love his brother and went on hating him until he killed him. And so it was with all the wicked in the days of Noah and those dwelling in Sodom and Gomorrah.
Another servant: is the Law of Moses or another group of prophets.

The Jewish priests rejected the Law of Moses by distorting its meanings for their own purposes, and dishonored it by their evil deeds, and did not give it the virtues it asked for, that is, they sent it away empty; or they persisted in rejecting the words of the prophets and dishonoring them.
A third: the prophets in general, or the last group of the prophets.

The priests persecuted the prophets, tormented them and cast them out by rejecting their words and throwing them into prisons. In sum, mankind rejected the voice of God which He sent in many forms so that they might repent and return to Him.
There was nothing left for God but to give them all His love, by sending His only Son Jesus Christ, that perhaps they would respect Him and fear Him because of the power of His words and miracles.

Strangely, the Jewish priests and their leaders felt the power of Christ and His authority and the people's following Him, so they feared for their positions and their earthly power, and did not think of the salvation of their people nor of their own souls, and they conspired to be rid of Him and kill Him. Had they not known the power of Christ, they would have had an excuse, but they knew and rejected out of their pride and their desire for authority and positions.
And so they crucified Christ outside Jerusalem. And Christ asks the hearers what their judgment is on these wicked husbandmen.
It appears from the parable that Christ knew what they would do to Him a few days later, namely His crucifixion outside Jerusalem, yet in His love He accepts the sufferings for our salvation.

The hearers declared their distress at these husbandmen, saying, "God forbid" at what they had done. And Christ declares His judgment, that He comes in the New Testament and dwells by His Holy Spirit on His disciples, and takes the care of His people from the Jewish priests and gives it to His disciples and Apostles in the Church. And nothing awaits these husbandmen but destruction and eternal torment.

Any sin is forgiven, however grave, except hardness of heart and refusing to obey the Church, that is, refusing God's commandments through self-justification and pride. So take care to repent every day and before your father of confession, and you will mend your faults however grave they are and receive forgiveness and strength for life with God.

He reminded them of what is written in the Psalm (Ps 118:22) about Christ who humbled Himself by His Incarnation, likening Him to the stone which the builders rejected, who are the shepherds of the Jewish people, but it became the head of the corner, on which the two walls meeting at one corner depend. The meaning of this is that Christ, whom the Jewish priests rejected, became the salvation of the Jews and the Gentiles and the foundation of the Church.

Whoever opposes the incarnate Christ, this stone, is wearied, loses his peace and torments himself; but the more serious thing is that if this stone falls on anyone, at the appearing of Christ in His second coming to judge the world, it will grind to powder all who died refusing to believe in Him.
The priests understood that they were the wicked husbandmen, so they tried to arrest Christ, but they feared because of the people's love for Him.
Do not become angry with the one who exposes your faults and try to wrong him; he is the voice of God to rescue you from your sins.

The priests were unable to arrest Christ, and they tried to catch Him in an error from His own mouth so as to bring Him to trial before the governor, so they sent to Him some Jews who pretended to be righteous and godly.
Neither acceptest thou the person of any: you do not favor the persons of the great and change the truth to please them.

They approached Him in the spirit of discipleship and praised Him as a teacher of spiritual things who favors no one, in order to deceive Him and make Him fall into an error, and they asked Him whether tribute should be given to Caesar or not. If He agreed, He would be considered a traitor by the Jews, who consider that God is their King and that it is not lawful to give tribute to the Romans; and if He refused to give tribute, He would be considered a stirrer of sedition among the people and would be brought to trial.

God, who knows what is in hearts, knew their craftiness and deceit, so He asked for a penny, and asked whose image and inscription was stamped on it on the penny. They said, "Caesar's," and He answered, "Render therefore unto Caesar the things which be Caesar's, and unto God the things which be God's," that is, give money to the world and its authority, but the heart give to God. By this He made clear a Christian principle, which is submission to the authorities and civil laws so that we may be good citizens submissive to the state, yet distinguished by consecrating the heart to God and carrying out His commandments.
Would that the image in you were God's, so that you become like Him, and not the world's, so that you please it with sins and lusts.

These deceivers felt their helplessness before the wisdom of Christ, so they were silent and marveled at the loftiness of His wisdom and His unexpected answer, which was nevertheless right and profound, because it calls them to the spiritual life and to keep away from foolish discussions or attempts to trap Him in a wrong word.

entries.section: (4) The question about marriage and the resurrection

paragraphs.text: The Sadducees were an aristocratic sect among the Jewish leaders, who believed that when a person dies, his spirit dies as well as his body, that is, they did not believe in the life to come.

entries.section: (4) The question about marriage and the resurrection

paragraphs.text: The Law of Moses required that if someone had no children in his marriage and died, his brother must marry his wife to raise up offspring so that the land of inheritance in Canaan would not be lost, and because all were waiting for the Messiah to come from their descendants.

But the Sadducees did not understand and believe in the life to come, and they exploited this law and composed a story, hoping to embarrass Christ with it and convince Him of their opinion, which is that there is no life after death.

entries.section: (4) The question about marriage and the resurrection

paragraphs.text: The story is that a man married a woman and had no children and died, so his brother married her and had no children and died, and so with the rest of the brothers, who were seven, and then the woman died. The Sadducees' question was whose wife the woman would be in the eternal life, if there is life after death, since the woman had married the seven brothers. They thought that if there is life after death, it would be like earth, each husband living with his wife and children.

entries.section: (4) The question about marriage and the resurrection

paragraphs.text: The children of this world: who live on the earth.
That world: the heavenly life.
The resurrection from the dead: those who live in the Kingdom after the last resurrection and the day of judgment. Neither can they die any more: they have no bodies to die, but are spirits.
Equal unto the angels: spirits like the angels.
The children of God: they are established in their sonship to God, not exposed to falling into sin.

The children of the resurrection: those who rose in the last resurrection after the day of judgment and who are immortal in eternity. Christ answered that marriage exists on earth for begetting offspring and preserving the human race, so that it does not become extinct through death, but in heaven they do not die and therefore do not need marriage, but live as spirits like the angels.

entries.section: (4) The question about marriage and the resurrection

paragraphs.text: Then He gave a proof of the existence of life after death, that God, when He spoke to Moses from the bush, called Himself the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (Ex 3:6), and of course these are alive as spirits after death, because God is too great to call Himself by the names of men who died and were buried and no longer have any worth.

entries.section: (4) The question about marriage and the resurrection

paragraphs.text: The scribes, who believe in the life to come, were pleased on hearing Christ's reply, and the Sadducees were unable before Christ's argument and persuasiveness to question Him or oppose Him.
Do not oppose the opinions of others and justify your own thinking, but listen and appreciate all opinions, for you may find some benefit in them, or they may be more correct than your own opinion.

While Christ was teaching the crowds and sometimes addressing the scribes, Pharisees and Sadducees, He directed His discourse toward His disciples, and it was mostly in the hearing of the scribes and Pharisees. It appears from this discourse, part of which Luke mentions, that Christ was bold and not afraid of the scribes and Pharisees in warning His disciples of their errors, and at the same time, when the scribes and Pharisees heard these words, it was a call for their repentance.
Christ warned them against imitating the scribes in the love of greatness and fame, which they pursue out of their pride and for acquiring money, for they were lovers of gathering money.

The scribes used to wear long robes (tallit), which are garments reaching to the feet that kings and great men wear, and they rejoiced in people's honoring them in every public gathering such as the marketplaces; and when they entered the synagogues or feasts, they asked to be in the foremost places so that people would glorify them.

More than this, in their hypocrisy they meant to prolong their prayers although their hearts were wicked, and they wronged the widows, for Jewish society considered them jurists and trustees whose counsel was sought, and they wrote down people's wills for them before their death, so they exploited this to take their money, especially the money of widows.
Because of this hypocrisy, that is, pretending to holiness despite inner wickedness, they receive greater damnation than an ordinary person if he sins, because he may have sinned out of ignorance.
In proportion to how much you have known Christ and learned in the Church, be exact in your life and hasten to repentance and confession if you sin.
Chapter twenty-one: the signs of the end and watchfulness; the widow's two mites (vv. 1-4):
This incident is mentioned in (Mk 12:41-44).

1- And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury. 2- And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites. 3- And he said, "Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all: 4- for all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had."

Christ stood with His disciples near one of the large chests placed in the temple in a special room for offering gifts, and He saw the rich of the Jews casting their gifts into the chest, making a loud ringing because they were metal and in large quantity.

Then a poor woman, a widow, came in and cast two mites into the chest quietly, so they made no sound. The mite is the smallest Jewish coin, and the two mites equal one-tenth of a denarius, which is equivalent today to about five Egyptian piasters.

Christ praised the woman's gift and even esteemed it above the other gifts, although it was the smallest thing offered in its material value; but in relation to what she had, she gave everything, while the rich, despite the great value they gave, gave a small part of what was left over beyond their needs. For God looks at the measure of love in the heart. The cup of cold water you offer may be greater than great services offered by others, if it is all the effort you have. Therefore do not despise what you can offer to God of prayers, fasts, worship and service, however small, but take care to offer everything you have with love and joy, for it is very precious in His sight. The destruction of the temple (vv. 5-7):
This discourse is mentioned in (Mt 24; Mk 13).

5- And as some spake of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said, 6- "As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down." 7- And they asked him, saying, "Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass?"
Some: the disciples, as the Gospels of Matthew and Mark relate.

The temple of Solomon was adorned with stones and gifts, and they used to renovate its buildings and expected that the Messiah would come and make it His dwelling place, so the disciples stood with Christ praising this great spiritual building, and Christ foretold to them that this building would be torn down and utterly destroyed.

The disciples thought, like the rest of the Jews, that this temple would continue until the day of judgment, so they asked Christ about the signs of the end when the temple would be destroyed, and they did not know that it would be destroyed in AD 70 at the hands of the Romans.
Do not be dazzled by the delights of the world or let your heart cling to them, for they pass away, but take care to prepare your heart as a temple for God by many prayers, readings and meditations.

Christ warned against being attached to the time of His coming, because many will appear in the world to deceive people that He has come in the second coming, whether by declaring themselves to be christs, or founders of schools of thought, or by miracles, like Simon the Magician in the days of the Apostles, or the many heresies that appear to this day, and some of them fix the date of the end of days. Sadly all this is said in the name of Christ, although it has no relation to Him, as He declares in this verse.

Among the signs of the approach of the end of the world is the rise of wars between nations and disturbances and revolutions within them... All this declares the instability of the material world, to lift our eyes toward eternity. These wars will recur, but the end is not yet, for there are still many other signs that we shall speak of.

Nature will declare its instability in the form of earthquakes in the earth, and troubles in agriculture so that the earth does not give its yield, and famines occur, and diseases spread as pestilences that kill many; and there will even appear upheavals in the sky such as thunder, lightning and storms, declaring the instability of the material heaven, so that we await a new earth and a new heaven in eternity.

If a person departs from God, he is shaken as by an earthquake, and hungers for lack of the word of God and of partaking of the sacraments, and bad thoughts spread within him like a plague, and inner conflicts arise between spirit and body, and even his spirit, that is, his heaven, is troubled by many thoughts. Therefore the only solution is to return to God by repentance and to cling to Him.
But before all these: before Christ's second coming.
They shall lay their hands on you: the arrest of the believers, their trial, imprisonment and torture.
They shall persecute you: this means kinds of persecutions and deprivation of rights and various insults.
For my name's sake: for the sake of faith in Christ and not for personal faults.

When Satan feels the nearness of the Lord's coming, he persecutes the believers, trying to draw them away from the faith, using in this the Jewish synagogues spread through all the lands and the Roman authorities, and he still uses various groups and bodies to persecute the truth in God's children; but their holding fast to their faith bears witness to the truth of what they believed, and declares the loftiness and power of Christianity.
Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before: do not worry about what you will answer to the persecutions and troubles the wicked cause you.

A mouth and wisdom: the word of God on the tongue of the Christians before the persecutors, which silences them and shows their wickedness. Christ reassures us that He will work in us when the wicked persecute us, and give us wisdom and power that show their weakness, because it is His divine power which cannot be overcome, as happened on the lips of the martyrs, who showed the helplessness of those who persecuted them, and many non-Christians believed because of that and were even martyred for Christ's sake, and sometimes the governors themselves and the persecutors believed and were martyred.
Trust in the power of God within you when you face a difficult situation or pressures from the world. Only pray and hold fast to God, and He will defend you.

Christ warns us that persecution comes not only from strangers or enemies but also from the nearest of the near, such as family members, relatives and friends. When a member of the family believes in Christ, the others persecute him, or when a person holds fast to the Church, those around him oppose him because they do not value the spiritual life, until a person sometimes feels that everyone hates him, so that the devil makes him doubt the possibility of succeeding in his life in the midst of the world.

On the other hand, Christ declares that all these persecutions cannot harm us except by His permission, according to our endurance, so that they cannot hurt even one hair of our heads. He asks only that we hold fast to the faith and be patient in these afflictions, and so we win for ourselves eternal salvation. Do not be troubled if everyone around you opposes you. Be humble, bear with them and treat them with love, and return to the Church and your father of confession to be sure of what you hold, and trust that God supports you.

entries.section: (5) The siege and destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Christ prophesied the destruction of Jerusalem, which was accomplished in AD 70 at the hands of Titus the Roman, and its siege two years before, and this is a declaration that its destruction had drawn near.

entries.section: (5) The siege and destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The Jews crucified Christ and refused to believe in Him, and He gave them an opportunity afterward of about 40 years, but they did not repent and believe, so the Lord was angry and destroyed Jerusalem, as is written by the prophets such as Daniel and Zechariah (Dan 9:26-27) (Zech 11; 14:1-2), that perhaps they would understand and repent afterward. And He advises His believing children dwelling in Jerusalem to flee from it, and those in the land of Judea around Jerusalem to flee to the mountains so that the Romans do not kill them.
The Christians obeyed Christ's warning, and history records that none of them was killed in the destruction of Jerusalem, because they fled quickly before the siege was completed.

entries.section: (5) The siege and destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: During the flight from Jerusalem the weak stumble, such as pregnant women and nursing mothers carrying their infants. They signify the spiritually weak, because they stumble when they flee from evil, so they fall into lusts and perish.

And the Gentile Romans will trample Jerusalem and kill those in it, and take them captive and carry them away to their lands. And Jerusalem will remain in turmoil and weariness until the Gentiles believe in Christ, and in the end Israel will believe, as St. Paul the Apostle explained (Rom 11:25-26).

If only you would grow strong spiritually in times of rest and be bound to the Church, so that when affliction befalls you, you are not troubled but flee to God and call upon Him for help, and so pass through in peace and do not fall into sin.

Before Christ's coming, signs appear in the sun, moon and stars, that is, there will be disturbing natural phenomena evident to all mankind, and they appear also on land and sea and cause general distress to all people, so that when everything around them shakes, they repent and prepare for eternity. When the nations are perplexed by these phenomena and grow weary of the distress and anguish surrounding them, they return to God... and great fear covers people because of the disasters that have occurred and what could occur even more than this in the heavenly bodies.
When you see or hear of changes in nature, know that you are nearing the end, so repent and prepare.
When all the preceding signs are completed, Christ comes from heaven in splendor and majesty with His Cross on the clouds, in intense brightness, appearing to the whole world.
Look up, and lift up your heads: be filled with hope, vigor and earnest striving.

He charges His believing children, when they see these signs and the appearing of Christ, to be strengthened in spiritual striving, because their redemption from the body has drawn nigh, as Christ takes them to His heavenly Kingdom.

Be persevering in your striving all day long to the last moment of your life, because the devil does not rest in his warfare until you are established in your victories and receive eternal glory, and do not be alarmed at your falls, but rise quickly, confident of God's power which supports you, until He takes you to the Kingdom He has prepared for you.

Just as we know from the appearance of fruit on the fig tree that summer has come, so also we know the seasons of the year from the fruits of the trees; so when the preceding signs occur, we know that the coming of the Lord is near.
Christ also prophesies that the destruction of Jerusalem will take place in this generation. And indeed some of the hearers lived until they saw the destruction of Jerusalem.

And Christ affirms that every word He said will be fulfilled, for heaven and earth shall pass away, but the word of God which He has declared to us shall not pass away forever, but we continue to live by it in the heavenly Kingdom.
If God's word is sure, then take care to read the Holy Bible and to keep the commandment in your heart and apply it in your life, and you will live forever.

After Christ's discourse about the destruction of Jerusalem and the signs of the end of days, affirming that we should not be preoccupied with calculating the time of His coming, He declared the summary of His discourse, which is to beware of being preoccupied with the delights and cares of the world, so that we lose our reason and our purpose and are like those drunk with wine, and do not prepare for the day of judgment, which comes upon us unawares when we are unprepared.

Christ declares that the day of judgment will come suddenly like the snare of the hunter into which the prey falls without feeling it. And all mankind will be subject to it, and therefore all must prepare by spiritual alertness.
Pray always: prayers and spiritual striving.

All these things that shall come to pass: the signs mentioned before, which befall mankind before the day of judgment, and they do not affect God's children or disturb them if they hold fast to Him and are prepared at all times.
To stand before the Son of man: the last judgment.

Christ offers the only solution for escaping the day of judgment, which is spiritual watchfulness, that is, guarding against the sources of sin and rising from it by repentance if we fall into it, with our hearts occupied with prayers and the relationship with God, so that we grow accustomed to being with Him and do not fear facing Him on the day of judgment, but rejoice because He delivers us from the toils of the world and lifts us to the Kingdom.

Put before your eyes at the beginning of each day that you will die and face God, and so be careful in all your actions, words and thoughts, and live with Him and enjoy His fellowship, and thus be prepared at all times, and no longer fear death or the last judgment.
Satan entered: through the lust of the love of money.
Of the number of the twelve: that is, one of those nearest to Christ, and this shows the heinousness of his sin.
The chief priests: the heads of the twenty-four divisions of the priests, in addition to the high priest and the former chief priests.
Captains: the commanders of the guard under the chief priests.

Judas Iscariot fell into the love of money. Although he was one of Christ's disciples, since he had the bag he used to steal from it, and then the love of money grew in his heart, so he wanted to sell Christ his Teacher and deliver Him to the Jews; so he went to the chief priests and agreed with them to betray Christ to them.

The chief priests rejoiced at his betrayal and promised to give him its price, thirty pieces of silver, which is the price of the compensation paid at the death of a slave if an ox gores him, for example (Ex 21:32). Thus Christ was sold at the price of a slave, the lowest of prices, and Judas accepted this agreement and began to look for an opportunity to find Christ away from the crowds in order to arrest Him.
The bitterness of betrayal is hard, so do not seek your own advantage before others', and what you would not want to happen to you, do not do to another.

Then came: drew near, since the next day, Friday, was the time of the Passover feast, so Christ did this on Thursday, a day before its time, so that He Himself would be our Passover when He was crucified on Friday at the time of the Passover feast. The Passover feast drew near, that is, the feast of Unleavened Bread, and so that He might fulfill all righteousness for us, He sent Peter and John to prepare the Passover for Him and His disciples according to the law of Moses.
The city: Jerusalem.
The house: the house of St. Mark, where He ate the Passover and instituted the Lord's Supper after it.

The two disciples asked Christ about the place He chose to eat the Passover in, and He said to them that when they entered the city they would find a man carrying a pitcher of water, and to follow him until he entered a house, and to prepare the Passover there. This man was Mark the Apostle, according to the tradition of the Church.
The pitcher of water signifies Baptism, which a person must receive first and then enjoy the Body and Blood of the Lord (the Lord's Supper).

When you have entered the house, ask its owner, who is Mark the Apostle, where Christ and His disciples will eat the Passover, and he will guide you to an upper room in his house, furnished and prepared for this; there make ready the Passover. In faith they obeyed, and found it as He had told them, and prepared the Passover.

He did not mention that it was Mark so that Judas Iscariot would not know and tell the chief priests, because He wanted to complete the Passover and to institute the sacrament of Holy Communion before He was arrested.
Obedience makes it easy for a person to order all his life, so obey God's commandments and you will find rest.

entries.section: (4) The Passover and the Lord's Supper

paragraphs.text: When the hour came to eat the Passover, which according to the Law is between the two evenings, that is, between the third and fifth hours in the afternoon, Christ reclined with His disciples to eat the Passover, and this was contrary to the custom of the Jews, who ate it standing. The Lord had commanded this so that they would remember their bondage in the land of Egypt, but now that Christ had come to free them by His death for them, He seated them around Him as sons and not as slaves.

entries.section: (4) The Passover and the Lord's Supper

paragraphs.text: Christ desired to eat this Passover with His disciples, because it was the last time He would eat a meal with them on earth, as a religious love feast with its spiritual symbols, which are fulfilled in His life-giving Cross, and from which is founded the sacrament of His most holy Body and Blood, which He declares and gives to His children on the same day after eating this Passover.

entries.section: (4) The Passover and the Lord's Supper

paragraphs.text: I will not drink of the fruit of the vine: I will not drink wine with you on earth a second time, for this is the last Passover He keeps with them.

Until the kingdom of God shall come: the heavenly Kingdom, where we are satisfied spiritually with Christ in heaven. Christ declares that He will not eat of this Passover again on earth, and that He will eat it with His disciples and all who believe in Him when their salvation is completed on the Cross, and He will satisfy them forever in His Kingdom. For Christ is our Passover and our spiritual food, not only by His Body and Blood in the Church, but in eternity He is the satisfaction of all His children... this is the fulfillment of the Passover in heaven.

This cup is one of the cups of wine that they drink with the Passover, and it is implicitly understood that He tasted it and then gave it to His disciples after giving thanks, according to the custom of the Jews. And He repeats that this is the last time He keeps the Passover and drinks of its wine until He drinks it spiritually in the eternal Kingdom. For wine signifies joy, and His joy is completed by the salvation of all His children and their entering the Kingdom, and that after the day of the last resurrection.

entries.section: (4) The Passover and the Lord's Supper

paragraphs.text: Here Christ institutes the sacrament of the Eucharist, that is, thanksgiving. He took bread other than the food of the Passover, and gave thanks, and broke it, and gave it to the disciples to eat, declaring that this is His true Body which He gives on the Cross, and He requires His Apostles and all His Church to do this sacrament always, to remember His love and the giving of His life on the Cross. The remembrance is not of a story that happened long ago, but is concrete, that is, a true Body and true Blood, as He made clear in (Jn 6:53-56).

And after giving them His Body to eat, He took a new cup other than the cups of the Passover and gave it to them to drink, declaring that the wine in it had been changed into His Blood, which He sheds on the Cross for the salvation of the world. Christ made the Lord's Supper, that is, instituted the sacrament of Holy Communion, immediately after the Passover, to declare that the Passover is a type of partaking of His Body and Blood.

entries.section: (4) The Passover and the Lord's Supper

paragraphs.text: Christ declared a bitter truth, which is that one of His disciples would betray Him and deliver Him to the Jews, for He said, "the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table," that is, one of the disciples at the table of the Passover. St. Luke does not care about chronological order, for Christ said these words after the Passover and before the institution of the sacrament of the Eucharist, as the other Gospels relate.

And Christ shows the heinousness of this man's sin (Judas Iscariot): Christ is not troubled by His sufferings and crucifixion, for they are necessary in His plan and must be accomplished, but this does not cancel the hideousness of Judas's betrayal and the punishment awaiting him in eternity. These words stirred grief and perplexity in the disciples' hearts, and they asked who this betraying disciple was.

As it was determined: Christ decided to die for the redemption of mankind, so He will surely die, but woe to the betrayer who sells his Master, for Christ's bearing of sufferings does not cancel the wickedness of Judas.
God warns us of our sins so that we do not fall into them, so would that we heed His warnings and repent quickly.

Christ was preparing for His sufferings to redeem mankind whom He loves, while the chief priests were consulting with envy and malice how to arrest Him and kill Him; and His closest ones, the disciples, were preoccupied, instead of sharing His sufferings, with seeking who among them was the greatest, who would take a greater place in the earthly kingdom that they thought Christ would set up. Opinions differed and a dispute arose among the disciples, each of them seeking how to be greater and more important than the others.

Christ understood what had passed among His disciples and reproved them for their love of preeminence, since this vice is one of the traits of the Gentiles far from God, who seek greatness and give gifts in order that people may call them benefactors and generous, and by this they lord it over one another.

But among those who believe in Christ, whoever is greater in age or position or knowledge, and so on, should make himself smaller and less than the rest, and whoever has the ability to lead and to go ahead should deal as a servant to all. Therefore in the Church of the New Testament, whoever teaches another and leads him in the way of the spiritual life is called a servant, to remember always to put himself lower than all.

Christ presented Himself as an example of humility, for He, the Teacher, who ought to sit while His disciples serve Him, was concerned to serve them, even to wash their feet. He washed His disciples' feet after the Passover and before the institution of the sacrament of Holy Communion. This quarrel either happened after the washing of the feet or happened before entering Jerusalem, but Luke mentioned it later because he does not care about the chronological order of events. To them.

Continued with me in my temptations: they left their families, and bore the insults and enmity of the scribes and Pharisees. I appoint unto you a kingdom: I give you the heavenly Kingdom as a reward for what you have endured.

As my Father hath appointed unto me: that is, Christ has His kingdom from eternity, which He has in the Father, and He emptied Himself by the Incarnation and took the form of an ordinary man, and then returns to His glory after His resurrection and ascension.

That ye may eat and drink... in my kingdom: spiritual satisfaction with Christ in the Kingdom of Heaven. It also means God's reign over the hearts of the disciples by faith in the Church, so that they partake of His Body and Blood all their lives on earth.
On thrones: this shows the greatness of the disciples' standing in the Kingdom of Heaven.

Christ praises His disciples because they bore with Him the sufferings of service, leaving their families and homes, and He promises them the eternal Kingdom with Him, and that they will eat at the spiritual table in heaven and enjoy His fellowship forever. And in this place of theirs they will judge all the Jews who did not believe in Him, for the Jews will look at His disciples in the glory they obtained because of their faith, and will regret it in eternal torment because they were with them in the same circumstances and did not believe. Put others before yourself in honor, and if you take a leading position, praise and lift up those with you, seeking in your heart what is more important, which is fellowship with God, and you will receive happiness on earth and joy in heaven.

Here Christ calls Simon by his old name, which means the weak, and not Peter, the strong rock, the name Christ gave him, because Satan seized the opportunity of Christ's entering into His sufferings and aimed his arrows at the disciples to show their weakness, and even to sift them as wheat. This was by God's permission, so that when their personal weakness appeared they would be humbled, and He would support them by His Holy Spirit, and their faith and their clinging to Him would increase.
That thy faith fail not: even if you fall through the weakness of your faith, your faith will not vanish, but you will rise, repent and return to God.
Strengthen thy brethren: this shows the weakness of the disciples and the exposure of all of them to doubting and denial like Peter, and their need to have their faith strengthened.

Christ comes forward in humility to pray for us, showing His love and fatherhood. And He speaks here as a man although He is God who is able to do all things, to teach us humility, love and prayer for others.

Then an important spiritual meaning appears, which is that the penitent, once he has turned from his sins, ought to do a positive work: he calls souls to Christ and strengthens them in the faith, as Christ asked Peter, when he repented, to strengthen his brethren. For the penitent feels for sinners like himself, and so he is tender toward them and encourages them.
Take care to live the life of repentance, so that you are a true servant who gathers souls to Christ and not merely a teacher of lifeless teachings.

This discourse is mentioned in (Mt 26:33-35). Here the impetuosity of Simon Peter appears, which came from love but without prudence, for he promised not to leave Christ even to prison and death, forgetting his weakness and his need of God's support. For this reason Christ directed the discourse to him before the rest of the disciples, to teach him and them humility, repentance and reliance on God's help.

Christ called Simon by this name although He had named him a rock, that is, Peter, but he would weaken and deny Him three times, and He gave him a sign, which is the crowing of the cock after this denial. The cock confesses the name of God by its familiar voice, but Peter the man denies Christ and says, "I know him not." Christ also warned Peter against denying, saying in effect, you know Me, so beware of saying that you do not know Me, and despite this warning Peter denied Him. Beware of denying Christ by your sins which cause others to stumble, so that you become a curse upon His holy name.

Christ alerted His disciples to the principle of not depending on material things when going out to serve, which they applied when they served in Judea; but now, as they prepare to preach in the whole world Christ crucified and risen from the dead, they need spiritual striving with all their energies, which He indicated by the purse and the scrip, that is, all their resources. What is meant is not reliance on money and stored food for going out to serve, but spiritual striving of prayers, fasts and prostrations, perseverance in teaching and persuading others, and all the gifts that God gives to servants.

Then He says that whoever has no abilities and gifts and feels weakness, let him sell his garment, meaning let him live in detachment and asceticism even from necessities, and in prayers and fasts, and leave the comfort of the body and buy the sword of the Spirit... that is, hold fast to the word of God.
That which is written (Isa 53:12): "He was numbered with the transgressors": His crucifixion between two thieves.
Have an end: I shall accomplish the redemption and rise from the dead.

Here Christ affirms the necessity of His bearing the sufferings, the crucifixion and death, for this is necessary for the redemption of mankind and will end at the appointed time, that is, the time of the Cross; and then He rises from the dead and gives the Holy Spirit to His children, so that they preach Him in the whole world.

The disciples did not understand Christ's spiritual meaning, which is striving with the sword of the Spirit, and they thought He was speaking of a material battle in which they would gather money and swords for war, as appears from the literal meaning of the words, so they answered Him that they had two swords. And of course these were a group of fishermen who had not been trained in the use of swords, and it is said that they were not two swords but two large knives which they had used in eating the Passover.

And Christ replied to them that it was enough, that is, enough talk on this subject, because they did not understand His meaning, and He does not mean that two swords are enough for a material battle, as shown by His rebuke of Peter when he tried to use his sword to cut off the ear of the high priest's servant at the arrest of Christ). Mt 26:52) If you are fighting a repeated or increasing sin, you need to use all your spiritual weapons, and because of your striving God has compassion on you and lifts these wars from you.
Went out: from the city of Jerusalem.
The Mount of Olives: at its foot is the garden of Gethsemane, which He entered.
Christ was accustomed to go to a garden on the Mount of Olives with His disciples. Some say that it belonged to Mark the Apostle, and He went to it after eating the Passover and the Lord's Supper.

When they arrived at the garden on the mountain, He called His disciples to pray, since they were about to face hard events, which were seeing their Teacher arrested and then crucified, and their exposure to fear and doubt and all the wars the devil had prepared for them; for prayer protects them from falling into temptation and turning away from God. However hard your circumstances, trust that your prayers and your clinging to God will carry you through the affliction in peace without falling into sin.
A stone's cast: about 20 meters, a near distance that allowed the three disciples to see Him and hear Him.

Christ left eight of His disciples at the entrance of the garden, and moved away from them with the remaining three, and then went into the depth of the garden a distance of about 20 meters, to be alone in prayer, and each group praying together.

Christ knelt down as a man, declaring the weight of the coming sufferings, not only the bodily sufferings on the Cross but also the psychological ones, by the denial and withdrawal of the disciples from Him and the standing of the crowds He had served demanding His crucifixion, and also the spiritual sufferings in bearing all the sins of men while He is the Righteous One. Therefore He asked in prayer, as a man, that the cup of suffering pass from Him, for it was very heavy, but at the same time He carries out the highest training in Christianity, which is surrendering the will to God, so He says, "not my will, but thine, be done." And though He is perfect God and knows that He will complete the bearing of the Cross, He showed that He has a perfect humanity that suffers pain. And He prayed this prayer three times, for He would return to His three disciples and find them asleep and wake them to pray and go back and pray alone, as the Gospel of Matthew relates.
Ask God's help and the lifting of the affliction from you, but in the end accept His will, for it is your good even if you do not see that at present, but believe in His good ordering of your life.
Heaven responded to Christ who suffered for us, but mankind was preparing death for Him, and even those nearest to Him, His disciples, did not stand with Him but were overcome by sleep.
And here the love of the angels for men appears, for an angel came to strengthen Christ as a man, to show their readiness to help men in all their afflictions.
Christ continued in fervent prayer, feeling all the sufferings coming upon Him, and His sweat was as it were great drops of blood, that is, pressed out by sorrow (the word Gethsemane means a press).
Persevere in your prayers however hard the affliction or however delayed the answer, for God cares greatly about every word and tear and drop of sweat in your prayer.

After His prayer Christ went back to look at His disciples and found them heavy with sleep, for they were sorrowful at what they had heard from Him about the sufferings coming upon Him, so Christ roused them to wake and continue in prayer so that temptation would not overcome them.

After Christ's prayers in the garden of Gethsemane and His discourse with His disciples about the importance of prayer as protection from falling into temptations, Judas Iscariot, a disciple of Christ, came, and with him a crowd of chief priests, captains of the temple guard and some soldiers with torches, swords and staves to arrest Christ, and the agreed sign was that whomever Judas kissed they would seize.

The betrayal of Christ by Judas was utterly heinous, because without cause the disciple who clung to his Teacher betrays Him and sells Him to His enemies at the lowest of prices, the price of a slave, thirty pieces of silver. Despite Judas's wickedness, Christ still loved him, so He rebukes him in case he seizes the last chance and repents, saying to him how he uses the means of expressing love, the kiss, for betrayal and evil and the killing of others, indeed the killing of his Master and Teacher, the one who had done everything for him and who came for his salvation and the salvation of all mankind.
And on the other hand, how can he deliver to death Christ, the Son of man, the Righteous One who never sinned.
Peter, and with him the rest of the disciples, asked Christ, "Shall we smite with the sword?", that is, shall they use their swords to defend Him?

For they had understood His earlier words about buying swords to mean a material battle in which they would defend Christ with these swords. And Peter rushed in, without waiting for Christ's answer, and cut off the right ear of the high priest's servant, because he was a fisherman and did not know how to use swords, or even knives. The Evangelists did not mention the names of the striker and the struck except John alone, because he wrote his Gospel at the end of the first century after the martyrdom of Peter the Apostle, since there was no longer any fear of the Roman authority rebuking him for trying to kill the high priest's servant (Jn 18:10).

Here the divinity of Christ and His wonderful love for His enemies appear, for He touched the severed ear and it was healed at once, declaring that His battle is with the spiritual hosts of evil and not with men, and He defeats them by His death on the Cross and binds Satan.

And His healing of the high priest's servant was to stop the soldiers from arresting or harming His disciples, especially Peter, who cut off the servant's ear. Sadly those who came to arrest Him were not affected by this miracle, and continued in the hardness of their hearts and arrested Him to kill Him.
Offer your love to all, even to your enemies, and declare the truth and rebuke them if they listen to you, that perhaps they will repent and return to God.
Captains of the temple: the Levites responsible for guarding the temple, who were under the chief priests.
The elders: the elders of the Jews who were esteemed among the people.
Your hour: the time that God permitted for Him to offer Himself to die for the world.
The power of darkness: the power of evil which the devil moves to harm everyone who does good.

Christ showed His love for the crowd that came to arrest Him by alerting them to the evil they were doing... It is astonishing that they came as a large group armed with swords and staves to arrest Him as though He were a dangerous criminal fleeing from justice, though He is the good Teacher who preached every day in the temple to save all. But He declares God's permission that the devil should have power and stir up their malice to arrest Him and kill Him.
Take heed lest you rush into wronging another although he is innocent.
When they had arrested Christ, they led Him to be tried at the house of Caiaphas the high priest, after they had first tried Him at the house of Annas, the father-in-law of Caiaphas.

While Christ was being tried inside the house of Caiaphas the high priest, Peter sat in the midst of the hall, that is, a little way from the place of Christ's trial, and around Peter was a group of maidservants and servants who had kindled a fire because the weather was cold at night.

As Peter was sitting, one of the maidservants noticed that he had been one of those close to Christ during His teachings and miracles among the crowds, and she declared this to all around, but Peter denied, pretending that he did not know Christ Jesus.
After a short while one of those in the hall noticed Peter, and said to all that this man was one of the followers of Christ, and Peter denied a second time.

The trial continued, and after about an hour a third person noticed Peter and his speech with the accent of the Galileans, and declared this before all, but Peter denied for the third time that he knew Christ, and immediately after that the cock crew, and this was the sign Christ had mentioned to Peter when He warned him that he would deny Him.

The trials did not distract Jesus from the salvation of Peter's soul, for when the cock crew Christ left everyone and looked at Peter who was sitting outside. He looked with the rebuke of love to alert him to the sin into which he had fallen so that he would repent, and Peter could not bear the love of Christ shining upon him from His eyes, so he went outside the house and wept bitterly, feeling his weakness and ingratitude in denying the loving Christ who had cared for him for more than three years. Despite the heinousness of Peter's sin, the tears of his repentance and deep remorse were his way back to God. Repentance is the shortest road to the heart of God, the tender and forgiving, however great your sins.

After Christ's second trial, they scourged Him with 39 stripes according to the Roman law, and they were not content with harming Him bodily but also psychologically, by mocking Him and jeering at Him.
Among the ways of mocking Him, they covered His face and began to strike Him, then lifted the covering and asked Him to prophesy who had struck Him, if He knew the hidden things as they say of Him.
They continued mocking Him as a sinner and criminal, though He is the Righteous and Holy One who bore in silence all their reproaches.
It is hard to bear insults without sinning, especially from those younger than you or lower in position, but remember what the King of kings and Lord of lords bore.

As soon as it was day: the Law provides that no one be sentenced to death except in the daytime, so they were not content with the night trials, and the supreme council of the Jews, the Sanhedrin, that is, the seventy elders, assembled in the daytime to try Christ for the third time.

They brought Christ to the third trial in their council, where the chief priests and the scribes, who are the elders esteemed among the Jews, were gathered, and they asked Him whether He was the Christ, and He answered them that they were unwilling to believe His words, for they had seen His miracles and heard His teachings before and rejected them out of their envy and wickedness, and that whatever He said to them they would not release Him, because they were insistent on killing Him and were looking only for evidence and a reason to complete their crime.

When Christ felt their inability to find a charge against Him, He gave them a ground on which to rely in killing Him, for He told them that the hour had drawn near for the Son of man to sit on the right hand of the power of God, that is, to regain His divine glory in heaven. He here repeats what He declared in His trial before Caiaphas, which took place at night (Mt 26:64).

So they asked Him to be certain of the meaning of His words whether He meant that He was the Son of God, and Christ affirmed this to them as they spoke and said. And so Christ declared His divinity plainly so that whoever wishes may believe in Him, and these words of His would be a judgment on whoever does not believe and on whoever dares to crucify Him and kill Him.
Christ reveals Himself to you however deep you are sunk in sin, that perhaps you will take heed and repent.

The ignorant Jews thought they had found tangible evidence to condemn Him and crucify Him, and did not understand that the wise Christ, whom they had not been able to catch with a single word throughout all their former plots, is the one who declared His divinity, bearing their malice and their use of these words of His to kill Him.
The three official trials, the crucifixion and death: the events in this chapter are mentioned in (Mt 27; Mk 15; Jn 18:28 to the end of ch. 19). His trial before Pilate (vv. 1-7):

1- And the whole multitude of them arose, and led him unto Pilate. 2- And they began to accuse him, saying, "We found this fellow perverting the nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, saying that he himself is Christ a King." 3- And Pilate asked him, saying, "Art thou the King of the Jews?" And he answered him and said, "Thou sayest it." 4- Then said Pilate to the chief priests and to the people, "I find no fault in this man." 5- And they were the more fierce, saying, "He stirreth up the people, teaching throughout all Jewry, beginning from Galilee to this place." 6- When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man were a Galilaean.
7- And as soon as he knew that he belonged unto Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who himself also was at Jerusalem at that time.
The whole multitude of them: the chief priests, the scribes and the elders of the Jews, members of the Sanhedrin, and all their followers.

In the third trial before the council, the Jews charged Christ with claiming divinity, and sentenced Him to death according to the Jewish Law, forgetting all the prophecies that bear witness to Him. But now they brought Him to Pilate to be tried the fourth trial, and they accused Him with a charge suited to the civil authority, namely stirring up sedition, and also forbidding the payment of tribute, and then claiming that He was a king.

And of course all these were false charges, because He taught the people love and peace, and when they asked Him about the tribute He declared plainly, "Render unto Caesar the things which be Caesar's"; and as for the third charge, that He is a king, He is a spiritual king over people's hearts and never asked to be an earthly king; on the contrary, when they tried to seize Him and make Him a king, He left them and hid from their eyes, fleeing from earthly kingship (Jn 6:15). And this is the first official trial before the civil authority.

Pilate questioned Christ, as was the custom of the Romans in trying the accused, and since he noticed the simplicity of His clothing and appearance, which was not fitting for an earthly king or even merely a rich man of material standing, he asked Him, "Art thou the King of the Jews?" Christ answered, "Thou sayest it," that is, your words are true, so He confirmed his words. Pilate continued to question Christ, as St. John relates in detail in his Gospel (Jn 18:33-38), and he found no ground or charge that would warrant arresting Him, so in the end he went out to the crowds of the Jews led by the priests and scribes and declared His innocence to them.

Herod: is Herod Antipas who killed John the Baptist (Mt 14:1). When the Jews' accusations against Christ failed and His innocence appeared before the Roman authority, they stirred up the people and began to cry out, declaring that Christ was a troublemaker, in order to make Pilate doubt his judgment. And to show the gravity of the charges brought against Christ, they declared that He was a stirrer-up of the people, not only in the region of Judea, which Pilate governs, but also in Galilee, which is under the authority of another governor named Herod. Thus they put Pilate in an embarrassing position, since if he declared His innocence they would bring a charge against Christ before another governor, Herod. And in that case Pilate would be shown to be lenient toward the accused before Caesar in Rome.

So when Pilate made sure that Christ was from Galilee, and Herod, the governor of Galilee, was visiting Jerusalem, he sent Him to him to try Him so as not to exceed the authority of the governor to whom He belonged according to Roman law, and so that he could rely legally on Herod's opinion, whether for acquittal or for condemnation, in judging Christ. From this the weakness of Pilate's character appears before the pressures of the wicked Jewish leadership.
Be strong in declaring the truth however much others oppose you for their own purposes; seek God's help and His pleasure before you are swept along with those around you.

Herod had heard of Christ, His teachings and His miracles, so he longed to see Him in order to enjoy seeing His signs, and not to believe in Him or to repent of his sins; so he was glad at Pilate's sending Christ to him, and began to try Him in the fifth trial, not to know the truth but to see a miracle from Him. Christ did not answer him a word, for He knew the hardness of his heart: he had not benefited at all from the teachings of John the Baptist but killed him, and now he does not want to believe but to enjoy seeing miracles to satisfy his curiosity.
